career_docs.content:
# 03 — Salary Benchmark and Remote-from-Colombia Feasibility
## Auditoría y reconstrucción del benchmark salarial, contratación remota y viabilidad administrativa 2025–2026

**Perfil:** Alexander Woodcock Salomón  
**Fecha de corte operativa:** 2026-06-11  
**Estado del documento:** sección corregida y terminada para integración posterior.  
**Modo usado para esta sección:** Deep Research previo + recolección estructurada con modo agente + verificación web puntual + reconstrucción analítica manual.  
**Herramientas adicionales recomendadas para esta sección:** no usar más Deep Research ni modo agente para esta sección salvo que se quiera auditar con un contador colombiano.  
**Regla crítica:** esta sección no es asesoría tributaria, legal, migratoria ni contable. Sirve para estrategia laboral y estimación de escenarios. Las decisiones fiscales deben validarse con contador en Colombia.

---

## 0. Propósito de esta sección

Este archivo define qué rangos salariales y modelos de contratación son realistas para Alexander como candidato ubicado en Colombia, con perfil de **Unity / Real-Time 3D / Technical Visualization / Technical Artist**, portafolio fuerte en TwinSight X500 y experiencia formal limitada en industria.

La sección cumple cuatro funciones:

1. **Auditar el benchmark salarial del informe anterior.** El deep research original mezclaba salarios globales, salarios locales, contractor rates y job postings sin suficiente separación.
2. **Separar empleado, contractor, EOR y freelance.** Para Alexander, el valor estratégico de una cifra salarial depende de si puede accederse desde Colombia.
3. **Modelar metas de USD 1.5k, USD 3k y USD 6k mensuales.** No basta con saber que existen salarios altos; hay que estimar probabilidad y condiciones.
4. **Definir implicaciones administrativas básicas en Colombia.** RUT, facturación, IVA, seguridad social, pagos internacionales y riesgo de mala clasificación afectan el ingreso neto.

Esta sección alimenta directamente:

- `04_eu_portugal_germany_mobility_strategy.md`
- `10_github_linkedin_cv_strategy.md`
- `11_company_targets_job_boards_recruiters.md`
- `13_interview_negotiation_and_offer_risk.md`
- `14_30_60_90_execution_plan.md`

---

## 1. Fuentes utilizadas y auditoría de calidad

### 1.1 Fuentes internas usadas

| Fuente | Uso | Estado |
|---|---|---|
| `01_source_of_truth_profile.md` | Perfil real, límites de afirmación | Vigente |
| `02_market_role_fit_and_positioning.md` | Familias de rol priorizadas | Vigente |
| Deep Research sección 03 | Benchmark salarial inicial | Útil, pero genérico |
| Recolección con agente | Datos por fuente y rol | Útil, requiere limpieza |
| `deep-research-report (8).md` | Informe base a auditar | Parcialmente débil |

### 1.2 Fuentes externas usadas

| Fuente | Tipo | Confianza |
|---|---|---|
| Howdy LATAM salary report | Payroll / EOR data | Media-alta |
| Lemon.io Unity rates | Contractor marketplace | Media |
| Qubit Labs Unity guide | Recruiting / outsourcing | Media-baja |
| ZipRecruiter | Salary aggregator | Media-baja |
| ARVR Jobs salary insights | Job-posting aggregation | Media |
| HireTalent LATAM Python guide | Recruiting / salary guide | Media |
| Colombia Move | Guía práctica tributaria | Media-baja |
| SIA Seguros | Guía práctica seguridad social | Media-baja |
| Papaya Global | Contractor payment guide | Media-baja |
| Mismo | Contractor compliance guide | Media-baja |

### 1.3 Lectura crítica de fuentes

No todas las fuentes tienen el mismo peso. Las fuentes de payroll y contratos reales son mejores que los agregadores de salarios. Los agregadores como ZipRecruiter son útiles para señales de mercado, pero mezclan ubicación, nivel, industria, tamaño de empresa, empleador local y trabajo remoto. Las guías de outsourcing suelen mostrar cifras desde la perspectiva de empresas que quieren contratar más barato, por lo que deben tratarse como **datos comerciales**, no como verdad neutral.

El informe anterior falló principalmente en tres puntos:

1. **Confundió salario local con salario accesible.** Un salario de EE. UU. no implica que una empresa pague ese monto a un contractor ubicado en Colombia.
2. **No separó gross de net.** USD 3,000/mes brutos como contractor no son USD 3,000/mes disponibles.
3. **Usó rangos demasiado amplios.** Para decidir estrategia, hace falta separar rol, seniority, modalidad contractual y restricción geográfica.

---

## 2. Metodología de benchmark

### 2.1 Categorías de salario

| Categoría | Significado |
|---|---|
| Local employee | Nómina local en país específico |
| EOR employee | Empleado legal por intermediario |
| Direct contractor | Prestación de servicios / B2B |
| Marketplace contractor | Plataforma tipo Lemon.io |
| Freelance project | Proyecto puntual por alcance |
| Job-posting salary | Oferta o agregador de vacantes |
| Strategic estimate | Inferencia razonada |

### 2.2 Conversión mensual

Para efectos estratégicos:

```text
monthly gross = annual gross / 12
monthly contractor full-time = hourly rate × 160 hours
annual contractor full-time = hourly rate × 2,080 hours
```

Estas conversiones son aproximadas. Un contractor rara vez factura 160 horas productivas todos los meses durante 12 meses sin interrupción. Para modelar ingreso conservador, conviene usar 120–140 horas facturables/mes.

### 2.3 Confidence rating

| Rating | Uso |
|---|---|
| Alta | Payroll, fuente oficial, contrato real |
| Media | Marketplace, job posting amplio |
| Baja | Agregador, muestra pequeña, vendor |
| Muy baja | Snippet, SEO, dato no verificable |

---

## 3. Conclusión ejecutiva salarial

Para Alexander, las rutas más coherentes con el objetivo económico son:

1. **Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D / Real-Time 3D contractor desde Colombia.** Es la ruta más alineada con TwinSight y con el objetivo de USD 1.5k–3k mensual en 3–6 meses.
2. **Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation.** Es la ruta con mayor upside a 12–24 meses, pero requiere empaquetar TwinSight como caso técnico serio y buscar empresas fuera de videojuegos.
3. **Unity Technical Artist — optimization/tools/runtime.** Es útil como etiqueta profesional, pero no debe confundirse con Game Technical Artist AAA.
4. **Python Automation / AI Tools.** Es ruta secundaria. Puede ayudar a monetizar ARA, pero no debe liderar la búsqueda inicial.
5. **3D Artist / Blender Generalist.** Debe quedar como fallback débil o complemento visual. No maximiza salario ni explota suficientemente TwinSight.

La meta de **USD 1.5k/mes** es realista en corto plazo. La meta de **USD 3k/mes** es alcanzable, pero exige CV, LinkedIn, caso TwinSight, demo y outreach bien ejecutados. La meta de **USD 6k/mes** no debe tratarse como objetivo base en 3–6 meses; es una meta de 12–24 meses si se logra entrar en technical visualization, simulation, XR, digital twin o contractor US/EU con suficiente evidencia.

---

## 4. Benchmark salarial por familia de rol

### 4.1 Real-Time 3D / Interactive 3D / Unity Developer

Esta familia es la base salarial más útil porque los datos de mercado para `Unity Developer` son más abundantes que para `Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Developer`.

#### Señales principales

- Howdy reporta que los salarios promedio de desarrolladores en LATAM en 2025 se ubican aproximadamente entre **USD 53k y USD 63k/año**, con Colombia alrededor de **USD 55,894/año** en su dataset de payroll. También reporta bandas LATAM de **USD 18k–28k junior**, **USD 35k–48k mid** y **USD 55k–70k senior**.[^howdy]
- Lemon.io reporta que un **Middle Unity Developer en Colombia** factura alrededor de **USD 27–35/h**, mientras que senior Unity developers en EE. UU. tienen mediana de **USD 57/h** y strong seniors en San Francisco llegan a **USD 72–89/h**.[^lemon-core]
- Qubit Labs reporta salarios mid-level Unity por país, con cifras como EE. UU. **USD 116,998**, Canadá **USD 140,000**, Alemania **USD 61,197**, UK **USD 58,709**, España **USD 58,719** y Brasil **USD 27,000**.[^qubit-country]

#### Matriz operativa

| Mercado | Rango útil | Relevancia |
|---|---:|---|
| Colombia / LATAM contractor | USD 27–35/h | Alta |
| LATAM EOR software dev | USD 35k–70k/año | Alta |
| US employee | USD 100k–150k/año | Baja inmediata |
| EU employee | USD 58k–95k/año | Media futura |
| Global freelance | USD 20–50/h | Media |

#### Lectura para Alexander

Esta es la ruta con mejor relación entre evidencia disponible y empleabilidad. TwinSight prueba Unity, C#, interacción 3D, UI técnica, optimización de assets y despliegue web. El riesgo es que muchas vacantes Unity están orientadas a juegos, mobile o VR. La búsqueda debe priorizar `Interactive 3D`, `Technical Visualization`, `WebGL`, `Simulation`, `Product Visualization` y `Unity Developer` fuera de game-only pipelines.

---

### 4.2 Unity Technical Artist / Technical Artist

El rol de Technical Artist tiene upside alto, pero la evidencia salarial es menos limpia. En Estados Unidos, ZipRecruiter reporta para Technical Artist un promedio de **USD 138,713/año**, con un rango típico entre **USD 127k y USD 152k**.[^zip-ta]

En UK, ITJobsWatch mostró datos muy limitados para Technical Artist, con pocos anuncios y salario mediano histórico alrededor de **GBP 68,500** en 2025, pero sin suficiente información para mediana 2026.[^itjobswatch-ta]

#### Matriz operativa

| Mercado | Señal salarial | Relevancia |
|---|---:|---|
| US Technical Artist | USD 127k–152k | Baja inmediata |
| UK Technical Artist | ~GBP 68.5k | Baja-media |
| LATAM Technical Artist | Not found | Baja |
| Unity TA contractor | Proxy Unity rate | Media |

#### Lectura para Alexander

`Technical Artist` debe usarse como parte del posicionamiento, pero con precisión. No conviene apuntar a **Game Technical Artist AAA** como ruta principal inmediata. Sí conviene apuntar a:

- Unity Technical Artist — Optimization
- Runtime Technical Artist
- Technical Artist — Tools
- Technical Artist — Interactive 3D
- Technical Artist — Visualization

El portafolio debe mostrar breakdowns técnicos. Sin shader breakdown, editor tools, profiling, optimization before/after y demo ejecutable, el título puede sonar sobredimensionado.

---

### 4.3 Unity WebGL / Web 3D Developer

No hay suficiente data salarial específica para `Unity WebGL Developer`. La mayoría de fuentes lo absorben dentro de `Unity Developer`, `WebGL Developer`, `Interactive 3D Developer`, `Frontend 3D Developer` o `Three.js Developer`.

#### Proxies razonables

| Proxy | Rango útil |
|---|---:|
| Middle Unity Colombia | USD 27–35/h |
| Mid Unity global | USD 73k–125k/año |
| WebGL / 3D frontend | Variable |
| Product visualization | Variable |

#### Lectura para Alexander

Esta ruta es estratégica aunque la data salarial sea incompleta, porque TwinSight es una prueba directa de Unity WebGL. La dificultad es que las vacantes explícitas `Unity WebGL Developer` son menos frecuentes que las de Unity general. La búsqueda debe usar combinaciones:

```text
Unity WebGL Developer
Interactive 3D Developer
WebGL 3D Developer
Real-Time 3D Developer
Technical Visualization Developer
3D Web Application Developer
Unity Product Visualization
Unity Simulation WebGL
```

El objetivo no es encontrar solo ofertas con el título exacto. El objetivo es usar `WebGL` como diferenciador dentro de una ruta de visualización técnica.

---

### 4.4 Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation

Esta es la ruta con mejor upside a 12–24 meses. En EE. UU., ZipRecruiter reporta para `Digital Twin Engineer` un promedio de **USD 139,368/año** y para `Simulation Software Engineer` un promedio de **USD 137,846/año**, con rango 25–75 aproximadamente **USD 104k–162k** para Simulation Software Engineer.[^zip-dt][^zip-sim]

#### Matriz operativa

| Rol | US promedio | Relevancia |
|---|---:|---|
| Digital Twin Engineer | USD 139k/año | Media futura |
| Simulation Software Engineer | USD 138k/año | Media futura |
| Technical Visualization | Not found | Alta estratégica |
| Industrial 3D Developer | Not found | Alta estratégica |

#### Lectura para Alexander

TwinSight encaja muy bien en esta ruta porque convierte documentación/CAD/ensamblaje en experiencia 3D interactiva. Sin embargo, muchas ofertas de digital twin y simulation pueden exigir:

- ingeniería mecánica, sistemas, IoT o datos en tiempo real;
- experiencia con sensores, CAD industrial, PLM, BIM o cloud;
- autorización laboral local;
- experiencia formal previa;
- seguridad industrial o defense-adjacent restrictions.

La ruta no debe venderse como `Digital Twin Engineer` si TwinSight no integra datos vivos, IoT, sensores o sincronización en tiempo real. La formulación más honesta es:

```text
Interactive technical visualization / CAD-to-realtime Unity prototype with digital-twin-adjacent relevance.
```

---

### 4.5 XR / AR / VR Developer

ARVR Jobs reporta datos altos para EE. UU.: junior **USD 84,500–135,000**, mid **USD 145,062–223,459** y senior **USD 163,857–248,827**. La propia fuente advierte que los datos son limitados y que provienen de postings agregados de compañías como Apple, Meta, Google y Snap.[^arvr]

#### Matriz operativa

| Mercado | Señal salarial | Viabilidad |
|---|---:|---|
| US big tech XR | Muy alta | Baja inmediata |
| Startup XR remote | Media-alta | Media |
| LATAM Unity XR contractor | Proxy Unity rate | Media |
| EU XR | Variable | Futura |

#### Lectura para Alexander

XR no debe ser foco inmediato a menos que se cree una demo específica en XR. TwinSight puede adaptarse conceptualmente a XR, pero actualmente prueba mejor visualización web que AR/VR. El rol debe quedar como ruta de expansión, no como target principal inicial.

---

### 4.6 Tools / Pipeline Developer

Los datos específicos de `Tools Developer` son escasos. La fuente de salario debe modelarse por proxies:

- Technical Artist con herramientas.
- Unity Developer con editor scripting.
- Software Engineer general.
- Python Automation Developer.

#### Lectura para Alexander

Esta ruta puede ser valiosa si ARA y scripts de pipeline se presentan correctamente. No obstante, para ganar entrevistas como `Tools Developer`, se necesita evidencia adicional:

- editor tools en Unity;
- automatización Blender/Python;
- pipeline CAD-to-realtime documentado;
- before/after de optimización;
- scripts limpios y públicos;
- repositorio con README técnico.

Sin esa evidencia, `Tools Developer` debe ser secundario.

---

### 4.7 Python Automation / AI Tools / LLM Application Developer

HireTalent reporta para Python Developer remoto en LATAM una mediana de **USD 44k/año**, entry alrededor de **USD 30k/año**, mid **USD 46k/año** y senior **USD 62k/año**. Para Colombia, reporta rango entry-to-senior de **USD 30k–66k/año**, con mensualidad aproximada de **USD 3k–6k**.[^hiretalent-python]

#### Matriz operativa

| Ruta | Rango útil | Prioridad |
|---|---:|---|
| Python Automation | USD 30k–62k | Media |
| LLM App Developer | Variable | Media-baja |
| AI Engineer | Alto | Baja actual |
| ML Engineer | Alto | No viable ahora |

#### Lectura para Alexander

ARA puede ayudar, pero no debe ser el centro de la búsqueda inicial. La ruta AI Tools puede servir como fallback o complemento si se arma una demo funcional y honesta. No debe venderse como ML/AI engineering. La formulación defendible es:

```text
Python automation and LLM-assisted workflow tooling.
```

---

### 4.8 Full-stack Developer fallback

Full-stack es fallback, no eje. Puede ofrecer acceso a empleos más abundantes, pero diluye la ventaja de TwinSight. Además, competiría contra perfiles con experiencia comercial directa en React, backend, bases de datos, deployment y QA.

La única forma razonable de usarlo es:

```text
Unity / 3D web developer with enough full-stack literacy to integrate APIs, dashboards and deployment workflows.
```

---

### 4.9 3D Artist / Blender Generalist fallback

ZipRecruiter reporta un promedio de **USD 82,070/año** para 3D Artist en EE. UU., con rango amplio de **USD 41k–142k**.[^zip-3dartist]

#### Lectura para Alexander

Esta ruta debe rechazarse como principal. El mercado de artistas 3D puros es muy competitivo, visualmente exigente y no aprovecha lo diferencial del perfil: ingeniería, Unity, WebGL, technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime, programación y evaluación académica.

El retrato Blender debe usarse como soporte visual y técnico, no como reposicionamiento a character artist.

---

## 5. Benchmark por región

### 5.1 Colombia y LATAM

Howdy reporta para LATAM un rango promedio de **USD 53k–63k/año** en software developers, con Colombia en **USD 55,894/año**. También reporta bandas LATAM de **USD 18k–28k junior**, **USD 35k–48k mid**, **USD 55k–70k senior**.[^howdy]

Lemon.io reporta que un Middle Unity Developer en Colombia factura **USD 27–35/h**.[^lemon-core]

#### Lectura

Para Alexander, LATAM contractor es el mejor primer mercado si el portafolio queda bien presentado. El target bruto razonable inicial no debe ser el promedio LATAM alto completo, sino una banda escalonada:

| Etapa | Bruto mensual razonable |
|---|---:|
| Entrada rápida | USD 1.5k–2.5k |
| Buen primer contrato | USD 2.5k–4k |
| Contractor fuerte | USD 4k–6k |
| Exceptional LATAM | USD 6k+ |

### 5.2 Estados Unidos

EE. UU. muestra el mayor upside: Technical Artist, Digital Twin, Simulation y XR pueden superar **USD 130k/año** en datos de agregadores y postings.[^zip-ta][^zip-dt][^zip-sim][^arvr]

#### Lectura

La barrera no es salarial. La barrera es accesibilidad:

- remote US-only;
- autorización laboral;
- contractor compliance;
- competencia senior;
- necesidad de experiencia formal;
- requisitos de seguridad, hardware, defense o residencia.

La estrategia correcta no es aplicar masivamente a empleos US-only, sino buscar:

- remote LATAM;
- worldwide contractor;
- US startups con contractor;
- creative tech studios;
- product visualization firms;
- technical visualization vendors;
- agencies que ya contraten LATAM.

### 5.3 Canadá

Qubit Labs reporta salarios altos para Unity en Canadá, especialmente Toronto, con mid **USD 105,983** y senior **USD 145,000**.[^qubit-city]

#### Lectura

Canadá puede pagar bien, pero muchas ofertas son Canada-only. No es mercado prioritario salvo que la oferta especifique contractor o remote worldwide.

### 5.4 Reino Unido

Qubit Labs reporta Unity London mid **USD 77,512** y senior **USD 81,476**, mientras ITJobsWatch muestra baja cantidad de datos para Technical Artist.[^qubit-city][^itjobswatch-ta]

#### Lectura

El UK puede ser interesante para estudios y creative tech, pero remoto desde Colombia no es común. Prioridad media-baja inicial.

### 5.5 Alemania

Qubit Labs reporta Unity Berlin mid **USD 83,475** y senior **USD 111,300**.[^qubit-city]

#### Lectura

Alemania tiene sentido a mediano plazo por posible ruta de pareja/UE y sectores industriales. En corto plazo, sin alemán ni autorización laboral UE, debe tratarse como ruta futura. Para remote contractor desde Colombia, conviene buscar empresas alemanas que acepten proveedores externos, no nómina alemana.

### 5.6 España y Portugal

Qubit Labs reporta España alrededor de **USD 58,719/año** para mid Unity.[^qubit-country] Portugal aparece en Lemon.io como parte de las bancas Unity de Europa occidental, pero sin cifra específica en la tabla visible.[^lemon-location]

#### Lectura

España/Portugal son interesantes por idioma/cultura y futura ciudadanía portuguesa, pero no son los mercados salariales más altos. Sirven mejor como:

- puente UE;
- mercado de estudios/creative tech;
- relocation futura;
- networking hispanohablante;
- contratación europea más flexible.

### 5.7 Netherlands / Nordics

Qubit Labs reporta Netherlands **USD 76,073**, Norway **USD 73,419** y Denmark **USD 82,225** para mid Unity.[^qubit-country]

#### Lectura

Buen potencial, pero generalmente requieren autorización laboral o presencia europea. Prioridad futura, no inmediata.

### 5.8 Australia

Qubit Labs reporta Sydney mid Unity **USD 85,668** y senior **USD 104,582**.[^qubit-city]

#### Lectura

No es buen mercado inicial por zona horaria y restricciones. Solo aplicar si la oferta es remote worldwide.

---

## 6. Modalidades de contratación

### 6.1 Comparación operativa

| Modelo | Acceso desde Colombia | Recomendación |
|---|---|---|
| Empleado Colombia | Alto | Solo si paga bien |
| Contractor Colombia | Alto | Útil localmente |
| Foreign contractor | Alto-medio | Prioridad |
| EOR Colombia | Medio | Bueno si empresa seria |
| Foreign employee directo | Bajo | Poco realista |
| Freelance marketplace | Medio | Complementario |
| Relocation EU/US | Bajo actual | Futuro |

### 6.2 Foreign contractor

Es el modelo más útil en los próximos 3–6 meses. Permite cobrar en USD o EUR sin que la empresa abra entidad local. Requiere:

- contrato de prestación de servicios;
- RUT;
- facturación electrónica si aplica;
- soporte de pagos;
- cumplimiento de seguridad social;
- contador;
- claridad sobre propiedad intelectual;
- evitar subordinación excesiva.

### 6.3 EOR

Un Employer of Record puede funcionar si una empresa quiere tratarte como empleado legal en Colombia sin abrir entidad. Howdy describe el EOR como entidad que actúa como empleador legal y maneja payroll, impuestos, beneficios y compliance.[^howdy]

Para Alexander, EOR puede ser positivo porque reduce riesgo de informalidad y mejora estabilidad. La desventaja es que la empresa asume costo adicional y puede preferir candidatos en países donde ya tenga payroll.

### 6.4 Riesgo de misclassification

Mismo resume la diferencia clave entre contractor y empleado: el contractor tiene autonomía, usa sus herramientas, puede trabajar con varios clientes y factura por proyecto/servicio; el empleado trabaja bajo dirección, horario y beneficios. La subordinación es uno de los elementos críticos para determinar relación laboral.[^mismo]

Para reducir riesgo:

- evitar lenguaje de “employee” en contrato contractor;
- definir entregables y milestones;
- conservar autonomía horaria;
- usar equipo propio;
- facturar formalmente;
- evitar exclusividad total si no está bien compensada;
- documentar independencia.

---

## 7. Implicaciones administrativas en Colombia

### 7.1 Checklist básico

| Elemento | Estado requerido |
|---|---|
| RUT | Obligatorio |
| CIIU correcto | Pendiente contador |
| Facturación electrónica | Probablemente sí |
| Cuenta para pagos | Necesaria |
| Seguridad social | Mensual |
| Soportes de pago | Obligatorios |
| Contrato / SOW | Recomendado |
| Contador | Recomendado |

### 7.2 RUT

Colombia Move describe el RUT como el registro fiscal necesario para operar formalmente como independiente; incluye actividad económica CIIU y datos ante DIAN.[^colombiamove-rut]

Para Alexander, el RUT debe configurarse antes de facturar de forma sostenida a clientes extranjeros. La elección del CIIU debe validarse con contador. Posibles áreas: software development, consultoría, diseño, servicios digitales o actividades creativas/técnicas, según el modelo real de facturación.

### 7.3 Facturación electrónica

Colombia Move señala que si se factura a clientes colombianos y se superan ciertos ingresos, la factura electrónica DIAN-compliant es necesaria, y que DIAN ofrece una herramienta gratuita.[^colombiamove-invoice]

Para clientes extranjeros, el tratamiento puede variar. La recomendación estratégica es no improvisar: configurar facturación electrónica y tener soporte documental de contratos y pagos desde el inicio.

### 7.4 Retención en la fuente

Para clientes colombianos, Colombia Move describe una retención típica del **10%** sobre honorarios profesionales y aclara que clientes extranjeros no aplican esa retención local.[^colombiamove-withholding]

Esto importa para comparar local vs internacional. Una oferta local de COP puede tener retenciones y flujo de caja distinto a una oferta extranjera en USD.

### 7.5 IVA / exportación de servicios

Colombia Move indica que el IVA general es **19%** y que muchos servicios profesionales son IVA-aplicables, pero también señala que ingresos por clientes extranjeros normalmente se tratan como exportación de servicios y suelen estar exentos, si se documenta correctamente.[^colombiamove-iva]

Esta parte debe validarse con contador. No se debe asumir automáticamente `IVA 0%` para todo servicio remoto. La pregunta práctica no es solo “si el cliente está afuera”, sino si el servicio se utiliza exclusivamente en el exterior, cómo se factura, cómo se documenta y qué responsabilidades figuran en el RUT.

### 7.6 Seguridad social independiente

SIA Seguros resume que en 2026 todo independiente con ingresos iguales o superiores a 1 SMMLV debe cotizar a salud, pensión y ARL si aplica. También indica que para contratistas por prestación de servicios el IBC es **40% del valor mensual del contrato**, y para independientes por cuenta propia el Decreto 0379 de 2026 permite aplicar el 40% sobre ingreso neto después de costos en ciertos casos.[^sia-ibc]

Los porcentajes base reportados son:

| Concepto | Porcentaje |
|---|---:|
| Salud | 12.5% |
| Pensión | 16% |
| ARL nivel I | 0.522% |
| Base habitual | 40% ingreso |

La regla de costos netos no debe aplicarse sin asesoría. Para contrato de prestación de servicios, SIA indica explícitamente IBC sobre 40% del valor mensual del contrato.[^sia-contratistas]

### 7.7 Pagos internacionales

Papaya Global destaca que pagos a contractors en Colombia deben considerar documentación tributaria, integración bancaria, DIAN, soporte COP/USD, AML y RUT.[^papaya-payments]

Para Alexander:

- Wise, Payoneer, PayPal, SWIFT o Deel no reemplazan la obligación fiscal.
- El pago recibido debe poder reconciliarse con factura, contrato y declaración.
- Hay que revisar comisiones, tasa de cambio y trazabilidad.

---

## 8. Modelo gross-to-net: advertencia operacional

Un ingreso bruto contractor no equivale a ingreso disponible. La planeación debe reservar dinero para:

- seguridad social;
- impuesto de renta;
- contador;
- comisiones de plataforma;
- spread cambiario;
- software/hardware;
- meses sin contrato;
- vacaciones no pagas;
- salud privada o complementaria si aplica.

### Modelo conservador inicial

| Bruto mensual | Reserva sugerida | Disponible estimado |
|---:|---:|---:|
| USD 1,500 | 25–35% | USD 975–1,125 |
| USD 3,000 | 25–35% | USD 1,950–2,250 |
| USD 6,000 | 30–40% | USD 3,600–4,200 |

Esto no es cálculo tributario. Es una regla de prudencia para no confundir facturación con salario neto.

---

## 9. Realismo de metas de ingreso

### 9.1 Meta USD 1,500/mes

| Variable | Evaluación |
|---|---|
| Probabilidad | Alta |
| Horizonte | 0–3 meses |
| Ruta | LATAM / freelance / contractor |
| Condición | CV + LinkedIn + demo |

USD 1,500/mes es viable incluso con experiencia formal limitada si TwinSight se presenta bien y se aceptan contratos junior/semimid. No debe ser la meta aspiracional; debe ser el piso mínimo aceptable.

### 9.2 Meta USD 3,000/mes

| Variable | Evaluación |
|---|---|
| Probabilidad | Media |
| Horizonte | 3–6 meses |
| Ruta | Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D |
| Condición | Caso TwinSight fuerte |

USD 3,000/mes brutos es razonable para contractor internacional junior-fuerte o mid-junior. El dato de Lemon.io para Middle Unity Developer en Colombia (**USD 27–35/h**) sugiere que el mercado puede soportarlo, pero no garantiza acceso inmediato.[^lemon-core]

### 9.3 Meta USD 6,000/mes

| Variable | Evaluación |
|---|---|
| Probabilidad 3–6 meses | Baja |
| Probabilidad 12–24 meses | Media |
| Ruta | Digital twin / simulation / XR |
| Condición | Evidencia + entrevistas |

USD 6,000/mes requiere facturar alrededor de **USD 37.5/h a 160 h/mes** o más, antes de impuestos y reservas. Es alcanzable en LATAM contractor fuerte o en roles US/EU, pero no debe ser promesa de corto plazo. Para hacerlo realista se requiere:

- demo TwinSight pulida;
- case study técnico;
- portfolio público;
- GitHub limpio;
- narrativa de CAD-to-realtime;
- buen inglés técnico;
- negociación contractor;
- búsqueda directa a empresas de visualización/simulación, no solo job boards.

---

## 10. Rutas salariales recomendadas

### 10.1 Ruta de corto plazo: USD 1.5k–3k

Priorizar:

```text
Unity WebGL Developer
Interactive 3D Developer
Real-Time 3D Developer
Technical Visualization Developer
Unity Developer — 3D UI / visualization
```

No priorizar:

```text
3D Artist
Game Technical Artist AAA
Pure Full-stack Developer
AI Engineer
Machine Learning Engineer
```

### 10.2 Ruta de mediano plazo: USD 3k–6k

Priorizar:

```text
Unity Technical Artist — optimization/tools/runtime
CAD-to-realtime visualization specialist
Technical Visualization Developer
Digital Twin Visualization Developer
Simulation Developer
XR Simulation Developer
```

Condiciones mínimas:

- TwinSight live build o video claro.
- Métricas de optimización verificables.
- Before/after CAD-to-web.
- Código o arquitectura explicable.
- Narrativa honesta sobre AI-assisted development.

### 10.3 Ruta de alto upside: USD 6k+

Priorizar solo después de preparar evidencia:

```text
US/EU contractor technical visualization
Industrial Unity simulation
Digital twin implementation partner
XR enterprise simulation
Unity tools/pipeline engineer
LLM workflow automation consultant
```

---

## 11. Red flags de datos salariales

| Señal | Riesgo |
|---|---|
| “Remote” sin país | Puede ser US-only |
| Salario US alto | Puede requerir work authorization |
| Promedio Glassdoor/Zip | Mezcla seniority |
| Vendor report | Sesgo comercial |
| XR big tech | No representa startups |
| Digital twin salary | Puede requerir IoT/engineering |
| Contractor rate alto | Puede asumir seniority real |
| Full-time contractor | No siempre 160h/mes |

---

## 12. Datos que faltan o deben validarse después

Esta sección está suficiente para estrategia inicial, pero no para cierre fiscal ni negociación final. Faltan:

1. Validación con contador colombiano sobre RUT, CIIU, facturación, IVA y exportación de servicios.
2. Confirmación de obligaciones exactas para pagos en USD/EUR, Wise, Payoneer, PayPal, SWIFT o Deel.
3. Muestra de ofertas reales en sección 11 para confirmar qué roles aceptan Colombia remoto.
4. Datos más finos para Technical Artist en Canadá, Alemania, España, Portugal, Netherlands y Nordics.
5. Datos de `Unity WebGL Developer` como categoría independiente.
6. Comparación Deel vs Remote vs Oyster vs Plane vs Papaya para contratación EOR/contractor.
7. Benchmarks reales de contratos en Upwork/Toptal/Braintrust/Arc/Lemon.io para Unity WebGL y 3D web.

---

## 13. Decisión estratégica final de esta sección

La mejor ruta salarial para Alexander no es perseguir el salario global máximo, sino maximizar la intersección entre:

```text
TwinSight evidence
+ Unity/WebGL/C# skills
+ Colombia remote eligibility
+ contractor feasibility
+ technical visualization niche
+ realistic short-term employability
```

La estrategia salarial debe organizarse en tres niveles:

1. **Piso aceptable:** USD 1.5k/mes bruto.
2. **Objetivo operativo 3–6 meses:** USD 3k/mes bruto.
3. **Objetivo estratégico 12–24 meses:** USD 6k/mes bruto.

El candidato no debe presentarse como senior, AI engineer, digital twin engineer pleno ni technical artist AAA. La formulación más fuerte y defendible para salario es:

```text
Unity / Real-Time 3D Developer focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization and WebGL deployment.
```

---

## 14. Próxima sección recomendada

Archivo siguiente:

```text
04_eu_portugal_germany_mobility_strategy.md
```

### Recomendación de herramientas

| Herramienta | Activar |
|---|---:|
| Deep Research | Sí |
| Modo agente | No todavía |

### Motivo

La sección 04 requiere fuentes oficiales y actualizadas sobre:

- ciudadanía portuguesa por vía sefardí;
- derechos laborales con ciudadanía portuguesa futura;
- Alemania por matrimonio/pareja;
- residencia, Anmeldung, permiso laboral, reunificación familiar;
- EU Blue Card;
- trabajo remoto desde Colombia para empresas europeas;
- qué se puede decir a reclutadores sin sobreafirmar.

Primero conviene usar Deep Research para síntesis legal/migratoria. El modo agente se reserva para más adelante si necesitamos abrir formularios oficiales, recopilar links específicos o comparar rutas por país.

---

# Language Strategy and ROI Framework

## 0. Scope

This section defines the language strategy for Alexander Woodcock Salomón’s international job-search plan.

The analysis is built around the already defined positioning:

> Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL deployment, technical UI, and Python-assisted tooling.

The languages evaluated are:

1. **English** — currently self-assessed around C1.
2. **German** — beginner / A1 context at most.
3. **Portuguese** — strategically relevant because a Portuguese passport is expected with high probability in approximately two years.

The target employment context is:

- short term: **remote work from Colombia** within 3–6 months;
- medium term: **higher-compensation international work** within 12–24 months;
- mobility horizon: **Portugal / Germany / EU** once legal pathways mature;
- primary roles: Unity, Real-Time 3D, Technical Visualization, Digital Twin, Simulation, XR, and Tools/Pipeline roles;
- secondary roles: Python automation / AI tooling / LLM application development.

This section does **not** replace immigration, tax, or legal advice. It only defines language ROI as a career-planning variable.

## 1. Audit of the Deep Research output

The Deep Research output was useful as a directional draft, but it had quality problems that must be corrected before integration.

### 1.1 Valid findings to keep

The following points are directionally correct:

- **English is the highest short-term ROI language** for international remote roles.
- **German has low immediate ROI for remote-from-Colombia roles**, but high integration and mobility ROI if Germany becomes the relocation target.
- **Portuguese has medium strategic ROI** because of the expected Portuguese passport and possible Portugal residence, but it does not replace English for technical roles.
- **German should not displace English or portfolio work** in the first 3–6 months.
- **Portuguese is easier to acquire from Spanish than German**, so a functional B1/B2 path is realistic within 12–24 months if studied consistently.
- **Language certification is optional for most tech hiring**, but useful for immigration, academia, and credibility when the language claim is uncertain.

### 1.2 Weak or rejected parts

Several points in the Deep Research output were too broad or weakly sourced:

| Issue | Audit result |
|---|---|
| “Certify English as soon as possible” | Too strong. Certification is useful but not mandatory for most tech roles. |
| “German spouse route has no language requirement” | Risky. A1 German may be required in many family reunification cases. |
| “Portuguese B2 in 6–12 months” | Possible but only with structured study. Not automatic. |
| “German A1–B1 in 6 months” | Possible only under high intensity. Not a baseline. |
| “Portuguese increases salary directly” | Weak evidence. It mainly improves local integration and Portugal/Brazil access. |
| “English demand proven by France job-post data” | Weak proxy for global technical hiring. Keep only as partial signal. |
| “LinkedIn post as source for Berlin English-first jobs” | Weak source. Use as low-confidence signal only. |
| “CELPE-Bras as primary Portuguese certificate” | Incomplete. For Portugal, CAPLE/Camões exams are more relevant. |

### 1.3 Corrective direction

This file corrects the language strategy by separating:

- **employment ROI**;
- **mobility ROI**;
- **salary ROI**;
- **daily-life integration ROI**;
- **certification ROI**;
- **time cost**;
- **opportunity cost against technical skill development**.

The key correction is:

> For the first 3–6 months, language work must not compete heavily against portfolio, TwinSight case study, GitHub cleanup, LinkedIn/CV, applications, and interview preparation. English polishing is high ROI; German and Portuguese are medium-term investments.

## 2. Source-quality framework

Language-market evidence is harder to quantify than salary data. Therefore, this section uses confidence labels.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Verified** | Official source, recognized exam body, legal source, or directly observed requirement. |
| **Strong inference** | Consistent with job-market structure, role requirements, and regional hiring patterns. |
| **Weak signal** | Blog, job-board article, LinkedIn post, Reddit, or small sample. |
| **Strategic assumption** | Reasoned planning assumption for Alexander’s specific situation. |

### Sources used conceptually

This section references the following source categories:

- **CEFR framework** for language levels.
- **Cambridge / IELTS / TOEFL** for English certification.
- **Goethe-Institut / telc** for German certification.
- **CAPLE / Camões / University of Lisbon** for European Portuguese certification.
- **CELPE-Bras / INEP** for Brazilian Portuguese certification.
- **EU work-mobility rules** for the future Portuguese passport scenario.
- **German family reunification and residence rules** for the marriage-to-German-citizen scenario.
- **Job-market evidence from previous sections** for the priority roles.

## 3. Core conclusion

The correct language priority is:

1. **English: maintain and professionalize immediately.**
2. **German: start now at low-to-moderate intensity because of the Germany route.**
3. **Portuguese: start or maintain gradually; accelerate closer to Portuguese passport / Portugal relocation.**

A more precise recommendation is:

| Horizon | Priority |
|---|---|
| 0–3 months | English for interviews, portfolio, LinkedIn, CV, demo narration. |
| 3–6 months | English C1 proof through output; German A1/A2 foundation if Germany route remains likely. |
| 6–12 months | German A2/B1; Portuguese A2/B1. |
| 12–24 months | German B1/B2 if moving to Germany; Portuguese B1/B2 if moving to Portugal. |
| After Portuguese passport | German remains useful but no longer required for EU work rights. |

The short-term rule:

> If a language hour competes with a portfolio/job-search hour before the first international offer, the portfolio/job-search hour usually has higher ROI.

The exception:

> If relocation to Germany through marriage becomes concrete before the Portuguese passport is issued, German A1 becomes an administrative-risk reducer and should be prioritized.

### 4.1 English

Alexander’s English is already one of the strongest assets in the profile because it was developed through prior work experience and is sufficient for technical communication. However, “C1 self-assessed” is not the same as verified hiring readiness.

For job-search purposes, English must be evaluated across five outputs:

1. CV and LinkedIn.
2. Portfolio case studies.
3. GitHub README files.
4. Technical interview speech.
5. Demo video narration.

The most important English weakness to avoid is not grammar. It is **unclear technical storytelling**.

### 4.2 German

German is strategically relevant because:

- the partner has German citizenship;
- legal marriage could make Germany a realistic relocation route;
- German improves daily life, bureaucracy, and access to non-English local roles;
- many German industrial, simulation, digital twin, engineering, and SME contexts still value German.

However, German is **not** the highest-return variable for getting the first remote job from Colombia.

### 4.3 Portuguese

Portuguese is strategically relevant because:

- a Portuguese passport is expected in approximately two years with high probability;
- Portuguese citizenship would create EU work-mobility rights;
- Portugal may become a practical EU base;
- Portuguese improves local integration in Portugal and access to Brazil/lusophone markets.

However, Portuguese before the passport is issued has limited direct effect on work authorization.

## 5. Language ROI by strategic route

### 5.1 Route A — Remote work from Colombia

| Language | ROI | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| English | Very high | Required for global remote work. |
| German | Low | Rarely required for remote-from-Colombia roles. |
| Portuguese | Low/medium | Useful for Brazil/Portugal clients, but not core. |

For remote international roles, English dominates.

Most strong opportunities in Unity, WebGL, technical visualization, XR, AI tooling, and full-stack contracting will operate in English when they are international. German or Portuguese can occasionally differentiate, but they rarely compensate for weak portfolio evidence.

### 5.2 Route B — Portugal after passport

| Language | ROI | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| English | High | Tech roles often operate internationally. |
| Portuguese | Medium/high | Integration, bureaucracy, local jobs, networking. |
| German | Low | Not relevant unless targeting Germany. |

Once the Portuguese passport exists, Portuguese is not needed for EU work authorization itself. It is needed for:

- local administration;
- housing;
- taxes;
- social integration;
- small or medium Portuguese companies;
- long-term local credibility.

For tech roles in Lisbon/Porto startups or remote European companies, English may remain sufficient professionally.

### 5.3 Route C — Germany through marriage before Portuguese passport

| Language | ROI | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| English | High | Needed for tech roles. |
| German A1 | High legal/admin risk reduction | May be required for spouse reunification. |
| German B1 | High life ROI | Daily life, bureaucracy, integration. |
| German B2 | Medium/high career ROI | Opens local non-English roles. |
| Portuguese | Low | Not useful for Germany route. |

If the Germany route becomes active before Portuguese citizenship is complete, German has a different ROI profile. It stops being only “nice to have” and becomes a practical relocation variable.

Important correction:

> Marriage to a German citizen can support a residence/work pathway, but it does not mean German language can be ignored. A1 German may be required for spouse/family reunification unless an exception applies. This must be verified with the German embassy/consulate at the time of application.

### 5.4 Route D — Germany after Portuguese passport

| Language | ROI | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| English | High | Tech work. |
| German | Medium/high | Integration and local market access. |
| Portuguese | Low | Passport matters more than language. |

If Alexander has a Portuguese passport, he should be an EU citizen and generally able to live/work in Germany under EU free movement rules. In that case, German is not primarily a work-authorization language. It becomes an employability and life-integration language.

### 6.1 Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation

German has stronger value here than in game roles. The reason is structural: many German industrial, manufacturing, engineering, automotive, aerospace, logistics, and simulation contexts involve German-speaking stakeholders.

For Alexander, this matters because TwinSight X500 is not a pure game-art project. It is closer to technical visualization, spatial understanding, assembly inspection, and CAD-to-realtime workflows.

Therefore:

- English is enough for international technical roles.
- German expands the German industrial market.
- Portuguese helps in Portugal/Brazil contexts, but salary upside may be weaker than Germany/US/Netherlands/UK.

### 6.2 Game Technical Artist

English remains the default for international game studios. German helps in German studios, but does not replace a strong art/tech portfolio. Portuguese is low ROI unless targeting Brazilian/Portuguese studios, which may not align with the highest compensation strategy.

### 6.3 Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D

This route is language-light. Recruiters care more about:

- live WebGL demo;
- performance;
- C# quality;
- front-end integration;
- case study;
- visual proof.

English is necessary. German/Portuguese only matter by client location.

### 6.4 AI Tools / LLM Application Development

English dominates. German and Portuguese matter mainly if the tool handles local-language corpora, customers, or compliance-heavy use cases.

ARA Framework does not justify a language strategy by itself.

| Portuguese A1/A2 | Low/medium |
| Formal English certificate | Medium |
| German B2 push | Low short-term |
| Portuguese B2 push | Low short-term |

The conclusion is direct:

> Technical evidence + English presentation beats additional language study for the first offer.

### 7.2 When language beats technical skill

Language becomes higher ROI than a new technical course when:

- a relocation date is concrete;
- a visa or family reunification process requires language proof;
- a recruiter asks for local language;
- a target company operates in German/Portuguese internally;
- the role involves client-facing technical visualization in that country.

### 7.3 When technical skill beats language

Technical skill beats language when:

- targeting remote global roles;
- applying to English-first startups;
- building TwinSight proof;
- preparing technical interviews;
- polishing Unity/WebGL performance;
- developing portfolio breakdowns;
- cleaning GitHub repositories.

## 8. English strategy

### 8.1 Objective

The objective is not “learn English.” The objective is:

> Convert self-assessed C1 English into professionally visible, interview-ready, recruiter-trustworthy English.

This means:

- write CV and LinkedIn in clean international English;
- explain TwinSight fluently in 60, 120, and 300 seconds;
- answer technical interview questions without freezing;
- write GitHub documentation clearly;
- narrate a demo video in polished technical English;
- negotiate rates and contractor conditions.

### 8.2 Target level

| Use case | Minimum | Target |
|---|---:|---:|
| Remote contractor interviews | B2+ | C1 |
| Technical presentations | B2+ | C1 |
| GitHub documentation | B2 | C1 |
| Client-facing work | C1 | C1/C2-like clarity |
| Master’s applications | B2/C1 | IELTS/TOEFL proof |

### 8.3 Certification decision

English certification is useful but not mandatory for most tech hiring.

| Scenario | Certification value |
|---|---:|
| Remote technical job | Medium |
| Contractor/freelance | Low/medium |
| EU master’s | High |
| Visa / immigration | Medium/high |
| Recruiter trust | Medium |
| Technical interview | Low |

Recommendation:

> Do not delay applications to obtain IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge. Build the portfolio and apply. Certify English only if it supports a concrete path: master’s, visa, scholarship, or repeated recruiter doubt.

### 8.4 Best English outputs for portfolio

The highest-ROI English deliverables are:

1. **TwinSight one-liner.**
2. **TwinSight 60-second pitch.**
3. **TwinSight 2-minute demo script.**
4. **README executive summary.**
5. **Case study problem-solution-impact section.**
6. **Interview explanation of AI-assisted development.**
7. **Salary expectation script.**

These should be created before spending time on generic English courses.

## 9. German strategy

### 9.1 Strategic role of German

German has three separate values:

1. **Legal/admin value**: possible A1 requirement for spouse/family reunification before Portuguese passport.
2. **Life value**: housing, bureaucracy, healthcare, taxes, daily integration.
3. **Employment value**: access to German-speaking industrial, SME, public-sector, simulation, and engineering roles.

### 9.2 Correct legal framing

The correct framing is:

> If Alexander relocates to Germany before the Portuguese passport, through marriage to a German citizen, he may need to comply with spouse/family reunification requirements, including possible proof of basic German A1 unless an exception applies. Once a residence permit is issued with work authorization, he can work under that permit. This must be checked with the German mission at the time of application.

This corrects the weaker Deep Research phrasing that implied German might not matter for the spouse route.

### 9.3 German ROI by level

| Level | Value |
|---|---|
| A1 | Visa/admin threshold risk reduction |
| A2 | Basic survival |
| B1 | Daily life and integration |
| B2 | Local job market access |
| C1 | Professional fluency for German-first roles |

### 9.4 Target by time horizon

| Horizon | German target |
|---|---|
| 0–3 months | A1 foundation |
| 3–6 months | A1/A2 if Germany route remains real |
| 6–12 months | A2/B1 |
| 12–24 months | B1/B2 |
| Germany relocation active | prioritize A1 immediately |

### 9.5 German and technical roles

German is especially useful for:

- digital twin;
- industrial visualization;
- simulation;
- CAD/engineering workflows;
- automotive suppliers;
- manufacturing;
- med-tech;
- energy;
- defense-adjacent visualization;
- public-sector-funded R&D;
- non-English SMEs.

German is less critical for:

- global remote startups;
- US/UK/Canada contractor roles;
- Unity WebGL agencies;
- game studios using English internally;
- AI tooling startups.

### 9.6 Practical German recommendation

Do **not** attempt B2 German as the main 3–6 month project. That would create opportunity cost.

Recommended approach:

- Start A1 immediately but lightly.
- Study consistently 3–5 hours/week.
- Increase to 8–10 hours/week only if relocation becomes concrete.
- Use partner interaction for daily vocabulary, pronunciation, and household phrases.
- Target A1 certificate if marriage/Germany paperwork becomes active.
- Target B1/B2 only after core portfolio/job-search assets are finished.

## 10. Portuguese strategy

### 10.1 Strategic role of Portuguese

Portuguese has three values:

1. **Portugal integration value**: bureaucracy, housing, healthcare, taxes, local services.
2. **Brazil/lusophone market value**: potential clients and companies.
3. **EU identity value**: aligns with future Portuguese citizenship, but does not create the citizenship itself.

Important distinction:

> The passport creates EU work rights. Portuguese language improves living and local employability but is not the legal basis of EU work authorization once citizenship is granted.

### 10.2 Portuguese and Portugal

If Alexander becomes a Portuguese citizen, Portuguese language will be useful for:

- NIF/NISS/tax processes;
- renting an apartment;
- dealing with public services;
- healthcare;
- local accountants;
- social integration;
- Portuguese SMEs;
- local networking;
- long-term residence stability.

For English-first tech roles in Lisbon/Porto or remote EU work, Portuguese may be secondary.

### 10.3 Portuguese and Brazil

Portuguese can help with Brazil-facing roles, but Brazil does not currently appear to be the highest-compensation route compared with:

- US remote contracting;
- EU technical visualization;
- Germany industrial/simulation roles;
- global Unity/WebGL agencies.

Therefore, Brazilian Portuguese should not drive the main strategy unless a strong Brazil-linked opportunity appears.

### 10.4 Certification correction: CAPLE vs CELPE-Bras

The Deep Research output emphasized **CELPE-Bras**. That is useful for Brazilian Portuguese, but for Portugal the more relevant system is **CAPLE**, associated with European Portuguese certification.

| Certificate | Variant | Best use |
|---|---|---|
| CAPLE CIPLE | European Portuguese A2 | Portugal bureaucracy/basic proof |
| CAPLE DEPLE | European Portuguese B1 | daily/local integration |
| CAPLE DIPLE | European Portuguese B2 | professional/local proof |
| CELPE-Bras | Brazilian Portuguese | Brazil-facing roles |

For Alexander:

- if Portugal is the main scenario: prioritize European Portuguese and CAPLE;
- if Brazil work becomes relevant: CELPE-Bras can be considered;
- if no formal requirement exists: a certificate is optional.

### 10.5 Target by time horizon

| Horizon | Portuguese target |
|---|---|
| 0–3 months | Light exposure |
| 3–6 months | A1/A2 |
| 6–12 months | A2/B1 |
| 12–24 months | B1/B2 if Portugal relocation likely |
| After passport | B1 minimum for life; B2 for local work |

Portuguese has a better time-to-benefit ratio than German because Spanish gives a strong starting advantage. However, false confidence is a risk: comprehension may advance quickly, but writing and pronunciation require deliberate practice.

## 11. Time-to-proficiency model

### 11.1 English

Alexander is not starting from zero. The realistic target is not “English learning,” but professional polishing.

| Target | Estimated work |

| Interview-ready C1 | 40–80 focused hours |
| Technical demo narration | 10–20 hours |

### 11.2 German

German requires much more time. Goethe/CEFR-related estimates commonly place German B1/B2 in the hundreds of instructional hours.

| Target | Approximate cumulative effort |
|---|---:|
| A1 | 80–200 class hours |
| A2 | 200–350 class hours |
| B1 | 350–650 class hours |
| B2 | 600–800 class hours |
| C1 | 800–1,000 class hours |

For Alexander, this means:

- A1 is realistic in 2–4 months with consistent study.
- A2 is realistic in 4–8 months.
- B1 is realistic in 9–18 months.
- B2 is a 18–30 month target unless studied intensively.

### 11.3 Portuguese

Portuguese is structurally closer to Spanish, so time-to-functional use is lower. But exact CEFR progress depends on pronunciation, listening, and active production.

| Target | Estimated effort |
|---|---:|
| A1/A2 | 40–100 hours |
| B1 | 120–250 hours |
| B2 | 250–450 hours |
| C1 | 500+ hours |

These estimates are strategic planning estimates, not official guarantees.

## 15. Recruiter-facing language statements

### 15.1 Current safe statements

Use:

> Spanish: native. English: professional working proficiency / C1 self-assessed; comfortable in technical interviews and written documentation.

Avoid:

> Certified C1 English.

unless there is a certificate.

Use:

> Currently learning German for potential Germany relocation.

Avoid:

> German professional proficiency.

Use:

> Portuguese is planned as part of medium-term EU/Portugal mobility.

Avoid:

> Portuguese professional proficiency.

### 15.2 After English proof exists

Use:

> English: C1, certified by [exam], comfortable with technical interviews, documentation, and client communication.

### 15.3 After German A1/B1/B2

Use:

> German: A1/B1/B2 certified by [Goethe/telc], currently improving toward professional use.

### 15.4 After Portuguese B1/B2

Use:

> Portuguese: B1/B2, focused on Portugal/EU mobility and professional communication.

### 15.5 Work-authorization language is separate

Language claims must not be mixed with legal work authorization.

Do not write:

> German speaker with EU work authorization.

unless EU work authorization exists independently.

Do write, currently:

> Colombia-based; available for remote contractor/B2B work with international clients.

After Portuguese passport:

> Portuguese/EU citizen; authorized to work in the EU, subject to local registration and tax requirements.

After German residence permit through marriage:

> Authorized to work in Germany under residence status, subject to employer verification.

## 16. Strategic contradictions to avoid

### 16.1 “German is urgent” vs “remote-first from Colombia”

German is not urgent for remote-first roles. It becomes urgent only if Germany relocation becomes concrete.

### 16.2 “Portuguese passport soon” vs “Portuguese language creates EU rights”

The passport creates EU rights. Portuguese language improves integration but does not create work authorization.

### 16.3 “C1 English” vs weak technical explanation

A C1 claim is only credible if Alexander can explain projects clearly, handle interviews, write docs, and negotiate.

### 16.4 “Three languages at once” vs job-search execution

Studying three languages intensely while building a portfolio and applying to jobs creates execution risk.

### 16.5 “Certificates matter more than proof of work”

For tech hiring, project evidence normally matters more than language certificates.

Prioritize:

1. English job materials.
2. English interviews.
3. Portfolio.
4. Applications.
5. Technical skill gaps.

Do not prioritize:

- German B2;
- Portuguese B2;
- generic language certificates;
- language study that delays applying.

### Rule 2 — If Germany relocation becomes concrete

Prioritize:

1. German A1 certification check.
2. German A2/B1 practical ability.
3. English tech employability.
4. German labor-market vocabulary.

### Rule 3 — If Portuguese passport arrives first

Prioritize:

1. EU work authorization messaging.
2. English-first EU jobs.
3. Portuguese A2/B1 for living.
4. German only if Germany is the actual destination.

### Rule 4 — If income maximization dominates

Prioritize:

1. English.
2. technical proof;
3. US/global remote;
4. high-value role positioning;
5. local language only when it unlocks specific market access.
