career_docs.content:
# 15_final_integrated_strategy

## Purpose

This is the integrated strategy document that connects the previous sections into one coherent operating model.

It does not replace the detailed files. It functions as the final synthesis layer:

- what the profile is;
- which roles to target;
- how to position the portfolio;
- how to apply;
- how to negotiate;
- how to avoid strategic dilution;
- what to do in the next 90 days;
- what to build over 12–24 months.

This document assumes the thesis is complete and pending defense.

---

# 1. Strategic diagnosis

## Current position

Alexander Woodcock Salomón is best positioned as a **Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL deployment, and Python-assisted tooling**.

The strongest evidence is not formal industry experience. The strongest evidence is the **TwinSight X500** thesis project, supported by secondary technical projects such as ARA Framework, Blender portrait work, and selected software/tooling experiments.

## Core asymmetry

The profile has a strong project but limited formal industry history.

That creates a specific strategy:

```text
Do not compete as a generic junior developer.
Do not compete as a pure 3D artist.
Do not compete as a generic full-stack developer.
Compete as a niche candidate with unusually relevant proof in Unity WebGL, technical visualization and CAD-to-realtime.
```

## Main market advantage

TwinSight creates a defensible bridge between:

- Unity;
- WebGL;
- interactive 3D;
- CAD-to-realtime asset optimization;
- technical UI;
- inspection/assembly visualization;
- usability validation;
- technical documentation.

This combination is more aligned with **technical visualization, simulation, digital twins, XR, product visualization and industrial 3D** than with pure game art.

## Main weakness

The main weakness is not lack of potential. It is **lack of packaged proof**.

The profile must be converted into recruiter-readable evidence:

- case study;
- demo video;
- GitHub README;
- portfolio;
- screenshots;
- CV bullets;
- LinkedIn project entry;
- interview explanation.

Until that exists, the job search will underperform.

---

# 2. Source-of-truth profile

## Current factual profile

| Area | Correct statement |
|---|---|
| Location | Colombia |
| Main language | Spanish |
| English | C1 self-assessed |
| German | Beginner / none |
| Portuguese | Relevant for future EU/Portugal route |
| Degree | Ingeniería Multimedia, UNAD |
| Thesis | Complete, pending defense |
| Prior studies | Advanced coursework in Electronic Engineering, UNAL |
| Immediate work authorization | Colombia-based contractor / employment depending on structure |
| EU work authorization now | No |
| Future EU route | Portuguese passport expected in ~2 years |
| Germany route | Possible through marriage/residence with German partner |
| Current main proof | TwinSight X500 |
| Primary career identity | Real-Time 3D / Unity Technical Visualization |

## Claims that should be avoided

Do not claim:

- current EU work authorization;
- German residence;
- Portuguese passport already issued;
- senior industry experience;
- formal Unity certification unless obtained;
- formal Rebelway/CG Cookie certification unless issued;
- production AI engineering seniority;
- that ARA is the thesis if TwinSight is the thesis;
- that AI wrote the project without your technical ownership;
- that all projects are production-ready.

## Claims that are safe if phrased accurately

Safe claims:

- thesis project completed, pending defense;
- Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype;
- CAD-to-realtime optimization;
- C# runtime systems;
- interactive 3D UI;
- component selection, exploded view, clipping/cross-section;
- Blender optimization and asset preparation;
- academic validation using SUS / NASA-TLX / Think-Aloud if supported by final thesis data;
- AI-assisted implementation with human technical judgment, debugging and ownership;
- Python automation and LLM orchestration prototype through ARA if shown as prototype.

---

# 3. Recommended positioning

## Primary positioning statement

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

## Expanded version

```text
I build interactive real-time 3D systems for technical visualization using Unity, C#, WebGL and Blender. My work focuses on converting complex CAD or technical assets into optimized, browser-accessible 3D experiences with inspection tools, technical UI, visual modes, and performance-conscious deployment.
```

## Spanish version

```text
Desarrollador 3D en tiempo real / Technical Artist Unity enfocado en visualización técnica interactiva, optimización CAD-to-realtime y despliegue WebGL.
```

## Do not position primarily as

| Positioning | Reason |
|---|---|
| Full-stack developer | Dilutes strongest proof |
| 3D artist generalist | Lowers compensation and weakens technical angle |
| AI engineer | ARA is not enough proof for ML/AI engineering |
| Game artist | TwinSight is stronger for technical/industrial visualization |
| Pure XR developer | XR is adjacent, not current strongest proof |
| Senior technical artist | Formal industry evidence is insufficient |

---

# 4. Role targeting model

## Primary role families

| Priority | Role family | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real-Time 3D / Interactive 3D Developer | Strongest fit with TwinSight |
| 2 | Unity WebGL / Web 3D Developer | Direct fit with deployment medium |
| 3 | Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation Developer | Best strategic niche |
| 4 | Unity Technical Artist | Viable if framed around optimization/tools/runtime |
| 5 | Tools / Pipeline / Python Automation Developer | Secondary route supported by ARA |

## Secondary role families

| Role | Use |
|---|---|
| XR / AR / VR Developer | Apply when Unity + technical visualization overlap |
| Product Visualization Developer | Good fit if WebGL/configurator oriented |
| Creative Technology Developer | Good if interactive 3D/WebGL strong |
| Technical 3D Generalist | Use only if technical systems are emphasized |

## Fallback role families

| Role | Condition |
|---|---|
| Full-stack developer | Only under cashflow pressure |
| Python automation developer | Use when ARA is polished |
| 3D artist / Blender generalist | Only if tied to technical art |
| Local web freelance | Cashflow only, not core strategy |

---

# 5. Salary and work-model synthesis

## Practical salary targets

| Target | Timeframe | Realism | Best path |
|---|---:|---|---|
| USD 1.5k/month | 0–3 months | High | LATAM contractor, local remote, small Unity/WebGL contract |
| USD 3k/month | 3–6 months | Medium | International contractor, LATAM nearshore, Unity/WebGL project |
| USD 6k/month | 12–24 months | Low short-term / medium long-term | US/EU contractor, digital twin, simulation, XR, seniorizing path |

## Correct interpretation

USD 3k/month is not unrealistic. It requires:

- working portfolio;
- strong case study;
- consistent applications;
- contractor readiness;
- ability to interview in English;
- avoiding low-value local roles.

USD 6k/month is not impossible, but it should not be treated as the immediate baseline. It requires one or more of:

- better portfolio maturity;
- stronger interview performance;
- international contract access;
- niche technical visualization positioning;
- EU work authorization;
- stronger professional network;
- proven work history.

## Preferred work model now

| Model | Current usefulness |
|---|---|
| Foreign contractor / B2B | Highest short-term ROI |
| LATAM nearshore contractor | Realistic |
| Colombian employee | Stability, lower ceiling |
| EOR employee | Good if company supports it |
| Direct foreign employee | Usually difficult |
| Freelance marketplace | Useful for cashflow, noisy |
| EU employee | Future, after passport/residence |

## Gross-to-net warning

All compensation targets must be evaluated as gross and net.

Contractor income must account for:

- taxes;
- social security;
- payment platform fees;
- currency conversion;
- unpaid vacation;
- sick days;
- equipment/software;
- accountant/legal support.

A USD 3k/month contractor agreement is not the same as USD 3k/month net.

---

# 6. Colombia remote-readiness checklist

Before taking international contractor work, prepare:

| Item | Status needed |
|---|---|
| RUT | Required |
| Electronic invoicing | Verify with accountant |
| CIIU activity | Choose correctly |
| Export-service treatment | Verify case-by-case |
| VAT/IVA responsibility | Verify |
| Social security | EPS, pension, ARL |
| Payment method | Wise/Payoneer/SWIFT/etc. |
| Contract template | Reviewable |
| Tax reserve | Monthly |
| Accountant | Strongly recommended |

Do not treat payment platforms as tax compliance. They only move money.

---

# 7. EU / Portugal / Germany mobility synthesis

## Current legal position

At present, the candidate should say:

```text
I am based in Colombia and available for remote contractor/B2B work. I do not currently hold EU work authorization.
```

## Portuguese passport route

The Portuguese passport expected in ~2 years is strategically important, but it is not current authorization.

Once issued, it may unlock:

- right to live and work in Portugal;
- right to work across EU/EEA subject to local registration rules;
- easier EU applications;
- stronger recruiter response for EU roles;
- relocation without employer-sponsored visa in many cases.

Until issued, it should be described carefully:

```text
I expect to obtain Portuguese citizenship/passport in approximately two years, but I am currently Colombia-based and available as a contractor.
```

## Germany route through marriage/residence

Marriage to a German citizen can be a real route if relocation happens legally and the corresponding residence title is granted.

It can potentially unlock:

- residence in Germany;
- work authorization;
- local employment applications;
- access to German/EU employer market;
- more relevance for German language.

It should not be presented as current work authorization.

## Blue Card

The EU Blue Card is an alternative route, but not the primary plan.

It is more relevant if:

- a German/EU employer offers a qualifying salary;
- the degree/qualification is accepted;
- the role fits shortage or skilled-worker requirements;
- relocation is planned.

## Recruiter-facing work authorization statements

| Scenario | Statement |
|---|---|
| Now | Colombia-based, available for remote contractor work |
| Applying to US remote | Available as independent contractor from Colombia |
| Applying to EU now | No current EU work authorization; remote contractor possible |
| After Portuguese passport | EU citizen, authorized to work in EU/EEA |
| After German residence | Authorized to work in Germany, if residence title grants work rights |
| German marriage not completed | Do not claim German work authorization |

---

# 8. Language strategy synthesis

## Priority order

| Language | Priority | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| English | Immediate | Main language for remote roles |
| German | Conditional strategic | Useful if Germany route activates |
| Portuguese | Medium-term | Useful for Portugal/Brazil/integration, not main job lever |
| Spanish | Native advantage | LATAM, Spain, client communication |

## English

English should remain the highest immediate language priority.

Short-term focus:

- interview fluency;
- technical explanations;
- salary negotiation;
- written CV/LinkedIn/portfolio;
- demo narration;
- recruiter calls.

A formal English certificate is not urgent unless a visa, university or employer explicitly requests it.

## German

German is not the highest ROI for the next 3–6 months if the goal is remote income from Colombia.

German becomes high ROI if:

- relocation to Germany becomes concrete;
- marriage/residence route is activated;
- local German employers become targets;
- integration and bureaucracy become immediate.

Recommended path:

```text
0–6 months: A1 survival if feasible
6–12 months: A2/B1 if Germany route remains likely
12–24 months: B1/B2 if relocating
```

## Portuguese

Portuguese helps with:

- Portugal integration;
- Brazil market;
- bureaucracy;
- social life;
- future EU base.

It does not by itself create EU work authorization before the passport exists.

For Portugal, prioritize European Portuguese if relocation to Portugal is likely.

---

# 9. Education and course strategy synthesis

## Main principle

Courses without certificates are still useful if they generate public evidence.

They are weak as credentials but useful as skill acquisition.

## Correct rule

```text
Course value = output artifact, not course completion.
```

## Short-term course policy

During the first 90 days, courses must not displace:

- TwinSight case study;
- portfolio MVP;
- CV/LinkedIn/GitHub cleanup;
- applications;
- interviews.

## Rebelway

Rebelway is valuable if used for:

- technical art specialization;
- Houdini/procedural thinking;
- VFX reel fragments;
- real-time FX;
- future technical artist differentiation.

It should not become the main short-term path unless the target shifts toward VFX/FX technical art.

## Certifications

| Certification | Usefulness |
|---|---|
| Unity certification | Moderate if affordable and fast |
| English certificate | Only if needed |
| Blender certificate | Low compared to portfolio |
| Rebelway non-certified | Useful via artifacts |
| Google/Data certs | Low unless pivoting |
| Master’s | Medium/long-term, not immediate |
| PhD | Not recommended now |

## Master’s

A master’s can be useful if it supports:

- EU relocation;
- computer graphics;
- simulation;
- XR;
- digital twins;
- research/industry hybrid;
- structured immigration.

It is not the fastest path to income.

## PhD

A PhD should be avoided for now unless the target becomes research, academia, or advanced simulation/graphics R&D.

For the current goal, it delays income and creates opportunity cost.

---

# 10. Portfolio architecture synthesis

## Portfolio hierarchy

| Level | Project |
|---|---|
| Flagship | TwinSight X500 |
| Secondary technical | ARA Framework |
| Supporting art/TA | Blender portrait |
| Optional | ai-news-aggregator |
| Defer | FitApp-Free |
| Hide/archive | Weak old repos |

## Portfolio MVP structure

```text
Home
Work
  TwinSight X500
  ARA Framework
  Blender portrait
About
Contact
```

## Home-page message

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
Interactive technical visualization
CAD-to-realtime optimization
Unity WebGL / C# / Blender / Python tooling
Available for remote contract work from Colombia
```

## TwinSight must be visible first

TwinSight should have:

- hero image or video;
- short problem statement;
- technical role;
- pipeline;
- feature list;
- metrics;
- screenshots;
- demo video;
- code/architecture overview;
- limitations;
- AI disclosure.

## ARA must not compete with TwinSight

ARA should be positioned as:

```text
AI-assisted research automation prototype / Python tooling project
```

Not as:

```text
main thesis
production AI platform
ML engineering proof
enterprise AI system
```

---

# 11. TwinSight case study synthesis

## Public positioning

```text
TwinSight X500 is a Unity WebGL interactive 3D technical visualization prototype for inspecting and understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone. It converts complex technical documentation and CAD-derived assets into an optimized real-time 3D experience with component inspection, exploded view, cross-section tools, visual modes and academic usability evaluation.
```

## Core case study narrative

```text
Seeing parts is not enough. Users need to understand spatial relationships.
```

## Must-show evidence

| Evidence | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Triangle reduction | Optimization proof |
| WebGL build | Deployment proof |
| Selection system | Interaction proof |
| Exploded view | Spatial reasoning proof |
| Cross-section | Technical visualization proof |
| Visual modes | Rendering/UI proof |
| SUS/NASA-TLX | Evaluation proof |
| Screenshots | Recruiter proof |
| Demo video | Fast communication |
| GitHub README | Technical proof |

## Interview explanation

The strongest answer structure:

```text
1. Problem
2. Constraint
3. Pipeline
4. Interaction systems
5. Optimization
6. Evaluation
7. Tradeoffs
8. What I would improve
```

## AI disclosure

The correct stance:

```text
I used AI as an implementation assistant and debugging accelerator, but I was responsible for architecture decisions, integration, testing, technical judgment, validation and final ownership.
```

Avoid:

```text
AI built everything.
```

Also avoid:

```text
I wrote every line manually.
```

---

# 12. GitHub / LinkedIn / CV synthesis

## GitHub

GitHub should communicate:

- technical seriousness;
- project clarity;
- readable READMEs;
- relevant pins;
- no clutter;
- no weak tutorial repos on the front page.

Pinned repos should prioritize:

1. TwinSight X500.
2. ARA Framework.
3. Portfolio site.
4. Blender technical breakdown.
5. ai-news-aggregator only if functional.
6. Optional tools/scripts repo.

## LinkedIn headline

Recommended:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist | Unity WebGL, C#, CAD-to-Realtime Optimization, Technical Visualization
```

## LinkedIn About structure

1. What you build.
2. Flagship project.
3. Technical stack.
4. What roles you target.
5. Availability.

## CV structure

One-page base CV:

```text
Header
Professional Summary
Technical Skills
Selected Projects
Experience
Education
Courses / Training
Languages
Availability
```

## CV variants

Create these first:

| CV variant | Use |
|---|---|
| Real-Time 3D / Unity | Main |
| Technical Visualization / Digital Twin | Main |
| Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D | Main |
| Tools / Python Automation | Secondary |

Do not create the full-stack fallback CV first.

---

# 13. Company targeting synthesis

## Target categories

Use the section 11 target ecosystem as source.

Highest-priority categories:

1. Unity / real-time 3D studios.
2. Technical visualization / digital twin / simulation companies.
3. XR / AR / VR companies.
4. WebGL / Web 3D creative technology companies.
5. Product visualization / configurator companies.
6. LATAM nearshore companies.
7. Remote-first technical agencies.
8. Tools / Python automation companies as secondary.

## Priority logic

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| A | Strong fit, role plausible, portfolio relevant |
| B | Good fit, requires adaptation |
| C | Lower fit or weaker compensation |
| Watchlist | Future, EU, senior, or low probability |

## Application logic

A-priority applications require:

- tailored CV;
- tailored message;
- correct project link;
- company-specific reason;
- follow-up.

B-priority applications require:

- role-specific CV;
- short custom opener;
- portfolio link.

C-priority applications should not consume deep customization time.

---

# 14. Application system synthesis

## Weekly target

| Action | Weekly target |
|---|---:|
| A-priority applications | 5–10 |
| B-priority applications | 10–20 |
| Recruiter outreach | 10–20 |
| Speculative outreach | 5–10 |
| Follow-ups | 10–20 |
| Portfolio improvement blocks | 2–4 |

## Tracker must include

- company;
- role;
- priority;
- location;
- remote scope;
- contractor option;
- salary range;
- work authorization notes;
- CV variant used;
- portfolio link used;
- application date;
- follow-up dates;
- response;
- interview stage;
- offer score;
- rejection reason.

## Feedback loop

| Signal | Meaning |
|---|---|
| No replies | Positioning or target problem |
| Replies but no interviews | Portfolio/CV weak |
| Interviews but rejection | Technical prep gap |
| Low salary offers | Wrong market |
| EU-only blockers | Authorization issue |
| Full-stack replies only | Profile diluted |

---

# 15. Interview and negotiation synthesis

## Preparation priorities

Prepare hardest for:

1. explaining TwinSight;
2. Unity optimization;
3. WebGL constraints;
4. CAD-to-realtime pipeline;
5. C# architecture;
6. technical UI;
7. AI-assisted development disclosure;
8. contractor availability;
9. salary expectations.

## Take-home test policy

Accept only if:

- scope is limited;
- time requirement is reasonable;
- no production work is being extracted;
- ownership/IP terms are clear;
- the company is legitimate;
- the role is high enough priority.

Reject or renegotiate if:

- unpaid test exceeds reasonable scope;
- it resembles client work;
- it requires full feature delivery;
- no feedback is promised;
- company avoids contract clarity.

## Negotiation stance

For contractor work:

```text
My expected range depends on scope, duration, time-zone overlap, and whether the role is contractor or employee. For international contractor work, I usually evaluate monthly retainers or hourly rates based on project complexity and expected availability.
```

Do not reveal minimum too early.

## Offer scorecard

Score offers on:

- gross compensation;
- net compensation;
- role fit;
- portfolio leverage;
- contract safety;
- remote stability;
- learning ROI;
- EU leverage;
- payment reliability;
- IP and exclusivity terms.

---

# 16. 30/60/90 execution synthesis

## Days 1–30

Main objective: **build credible market presence.**

Deliverables:

- TwinSight case study;
- demo video draft;
- GitHub cleanup;
- LinkedIn rewrite;
- base CV;
- two CV variants;
- portfolio MVP;
- tracker;
- first applications.

## Days 31–60

Main objective: **test market response.**

Actions:

- 50–90 total applications;
- 40–80 direct contacts;
- recruiter outreach;
- ARA cleanup decision;
- portfolio iteration;
- interview preparation;
- salary scripts.

## Days 61–90

Main objective: **convert pipeline into interviews/offers.**

Actions:

- double down on role families generating replies;
- remove weak paths;
- prepare technical stories;
- negotiate carefully;
- evaluate offers with scorecard;
- define next 90-day plan.

---

# 17. Strategic risks

## Highest risks

| Risk | Why it matters | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Strategic dispersion | Too many roles/projects | Role lock |
| Course hoarding | Delays portfolio | Artifact rule |
| Portfolio perfectionism | Delays applications | MVP deadline |
| Overclaiming | Interview credibility risk | Claim discipline |
| Underclaiming | Low salary offers | Metrics and proof |
| AI disclosure mishandling | Trust risk | Prepared answer |
| EU misstatement | Legal/recruiter risk | Accurate authorization text |
| Low-quality jobs | Career dilution | Offer scorecard |
| Weak GitHub | Technical credibility | Repo cleanup |
| No follow-up | Lost pipeline | Tracker cadence |

## Primary control mechanism

The tracker is the control system. Decisions must be based on data, not emotion.

---

# 18. What to do next

## Immediate next actions

1. Finish thesis defense preparation.
2. Create TwinSight case study assets.
3. Record 60–120 second demo.
4. Clean GitHub.
5. Publish portfolio MVP.
6. Update LinkedIn.
7. Build base CV and two variants.
8. Start A/B company applications.
9. Track every action.
10. Review after 30 days.

## Do not do next

Do not:

- start a new flagship project;
- overbuild ARA before TwinSight is public;
- spend weeks choosing portfolio tech;
- apply broadly as full-stack;
- start intensive German before job assets exist;
- wait for Portuguese passport before applying;
- make FitApp a portfolio priority;
- publish weak repos;
- accept vague unpaid trials.

---

# 19. Final recommended strategy

## Best path

The best path is a **balanced but focused international contractor strategy**:

```text
Use TwinSight X500 as proof for Unity / Real-Time 3D / Technical Visualization roles.
Prioritize remote work from Colombia now.
Build toward EU employability through future Portuguese passport and possible Germany residence.
Use ARA and Python tooling only as secondary differentiation.
Avoid profile dilution.
```

## Core execution sentence

```text
For the next 90 days, every action must either strengthen TwinSight as proof, improve recruiter-facing credibility, create interview opportunities, or increase contractor readiness.
```

## Final target profile

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist with a focus on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL deployment, and Python-assisted production tooling.
```

## Final role targets

1. Real-Time 3D / Interactive Technical Visualization Developer.
2. Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer.
3. Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation Developer.
4. Unity Technical Artist focused on runtime, optimization and tooling.
5. Tools / Pipeline / Python Automation Developer as secondary path.

## Final rule

The first job does not need to be the final destination.

It must satisfy:

- compensation above the minimum threshold;
- remote feasibility from Colombia;
- defensible contract terms;
- role fit with the real-time 3D direction;
- ability to build toward USD 3k–6k/month;
- no major strategic dilution.

If a role provides money but destroys positioning, treat it as a temporary cashflow decision, not as the main career strategy.

# 16_final_consistency_audit_and_gap_register

## Purpose

This document is the final consistency audit before converting the research system into application materials.

It checks whether the strategy files from `00` to `15` are coherent, actionable, and safe to use publicly. It does not rewrite the CV, LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolio, or outreach messages yet.

The goal is to identify:

- what is already closed;
- what is still uncertain;
- what requires external verification;
- what requires user confirmation;
- what should be produced next;
- what should not be claimed publicly;
- what could create legal, credibility, or execution risk.

---

# 1. Current document system

## Completed strategic files

| File | Status |
|---|---|
| `00_master_audit_blueprint.md` | Complete |
| `01_source_of_truth_profile.md` | Complete |
| `02_market_role_fit_and_positioning.md` | Complete |
| `03_salary_benchmark_and_remote_colombia.md` | Complete, but requires future tax/accounting verification |
| `04_eu_portugal_germany_mobility_strategy.md` | Complete, but legal facts should be rechecked before relocation |
| `05_language_strategy_and_roi.md` | Complete |
| `06_education_courses_rebelway_masters_phd.md` | Complete |
| `07_portfolio_strategy_and_project_architecture.md` | Complete |
| `08_twinsight_x500_case_study.md` | Complete |
| `09_ara_ai_tools_and_secondary_projects.md` | Complete |
| `10_github_linkedin_cv_strategy.md` | Complete |
| `11_company_targets_job_boards_recruiters.md` | Complete as target ecosystem; needs live verification before application |
| `12_application_system_and_tracker.md` | Complete |
| `13_interview_negotiation_and_offer_risk.md` | Complete |
| `14_30_60_90_execution_plan.md` | Complete |
| `15_final_integrated_strategy.md` | Complete |

## Remaining operational files

These still need to be generated:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `17_cv_base_and_role_variants.md` | CV base + role-specific variants |
| `18_linkedin_final_rewrite.md` | LinkedIn profile copy |
| `19_github_readme_templates.md` | GitHub profile + repo README templates |
| `20_portfolio_copy_and_site_structure.md` | Portfolio copy and structure |
| `21_twinsight_demo_video_script_and_shotlist.md` | Demo scripts and shot list |
| `22_outreach_templates_english_spanish.md` | Recruiter and company messages |
| `23_interview_answer_bank.md` | Interview answers and technical stories |
| `24_offer_evaluation_scorecard.md` | Offer scoring and decision system |
| `25_application_tracker_template.xlsx` | Spreadsheet tracker |
| `26_weekly_execution_dashboard.md` | Weekly execution dashboard |

---

# 2. Core strategy consistency check

## Final positioning

Current approved positioning:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

This is consistent across:

- role-market fit;
- portfolio strategy;
- TwinSight case study;
- GitHub/LinkedIn/CV strategy;
- company targeting;
- application plan;
- final integrated strategy.

## Consistency result

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Primary role identity | Consistent |
| Project hierarchy | Consistent |
| Salary targets | Mostly consistent |
| EU mobility | Consistent |
| Language strategy | Consistent |
| Course strategy | Consistent |
| Application system | Consistent |
| Interview/negotiation | Consistent |
| Company targeting | Useful but verification-limited |

## Main strategic thesis

The strategy is coherent if the profile is not diluted.

The strongest path is:

```text
TwinSight X500 → Real-Time 3D / Unity WebGL / Technical Visualization → international contractor or remote role → later EU leverage through Portuguese passport or German residence.
```

This must remain the core execution line.

---

# 3. Contradiction audit

## Resolved contradictions

| Previous contradiction | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Thesis described as in-progress | Corrected: thesis complete, pending defense |
| ARA described as thesis | Corrected: TwinSight is the thesis/flagship |
| EU authorization implied | Corrected: no current EU work authorization |
| German relocation treated as immediate | Corrected: conditional future route |
| Portuguese passport treated as current | Corrected: expected future route |
| Courses treated as credentials | Corrected: skills/portfolio input, not certifications |
| Full-stack route overemphasized | Corrected: fallback only |
| 3D artist route overemphasized | Corrected: supporting signal, not primary |
| AI tooling overclaimed | Corrected: secondary tooling route |
| CAD-to-realtime treated as role title | Corrected: differentiator/keyword, not main title |

## Remaining possible contradictions

| Issue | Risk | Required action |
|---|---|---|
| Exact thesis metrics | Medium | Verify final thesis numbers |
| Public repo state | Medium | Confirm what is actually visible |
| Portfolio MVP availability | High | Build or publish it |
| GitHub cleanup status | High | Execute repo cleanup |
| Company list freshness | Medium | Verify top 30 targets before applying |
| Legal contractor setup | High | Consult accountant |
| EU legal route timing | Medium | Reconfirm before acting |
| Portuguese passport certainty | Medium | Treat as high probability, not current fact |

---

# 4. Claims audit

## Safe public claims

These can be used in CV, LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolio, and interviews if factually true:

- Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype.
- Real-time 3D drone assembly inspection.
- CAD-to-realtime asset optimization.
- C# runtime interaction systems.
- Component selection and technical UI.
- Exploded view and cross-section/clipping.
- Visual modes for inspection.
- Blender-based optimization and asset preparation.
- Thesis completed, pending defense.
- Academic usability evaluation if final data is confirmed.
- AI-assisted implementation under human technical ownership.
- Python automation prototype through ARA.

## Conditional claims

Use only if confirmed:

| Claim | Condition |
|---|---|
| Triangle reduction from 6.5M+ to 95,617 | Verify exact source and final number |
| SUS 91.88 | Verify final report |
| NASA-TLX 8.69 vs 19.89 | Verify final report |
| 96 task-condition records | Verify methodology |
| 12 validation participants | Verify final sample |
| Live WebGL demo | Confirm public URL |
| Public GitHub code | Confirm repo state |
| ARA almost functional | Confirm reproducible run |
| Blender portrait complete | Confirm final renders/breakdown |
| English C1 | Use as self-assessed unless certified |
| Portuguese passport in ~2 years | Phrase as expected, not guaranteed |

## Claims to avoid

Do not claim:

- “Senior Technical Artist.”
- “EU work authorization” before passport/residence exists.
- “German work authorization” before residence title exists.
- “Certified Unity Developer” unless certified.
- “Certified Rebelway / CG Cookie” if no certificate exists.
- “Production AI engineer.”
- “Enterprise-ready AI platform.”
- “Commercially shipped Unity product” unless true.
- “All code written manually” if AI assistance was used.
- “AI built the project” because it undermines technical ownership.
- “Full-stack specialist” as main positioning.

---

# 5. Source reliability audit

## High-confidence internal facts

| Fact | Confidence |
|---|---|
| Thesis status: complete, pending defense | High |
| TwinSight is flagship | High |
| UNAD Multimedia Engineering | High |
| UNAL Electronic Engineering coursework | High |
| Colombia-based remote preference | High |
| English C1 self-assessed | Medium-high |
| Portuguese passport expected | Medium-high |
| German partner route possible | Medium |
| ARA secondary project | High |
| Courses mostly non-certified | High |

## Medium-confidence research facts

| Area | Reason |
|---|---|
| Salary ranges | Market varies by source |
| Contractor rates | Platform/vendor dependent |
| Company targets | Needs live verification |
| Job board quality | Changes over time |
| EU routes | Legal rules change |
| Portugal tax regimes | Changes frequently |
| German Blue Card thresholds | Annual updates |
| Colombian tax/admin rules | Needs accountant |

## Low-confidence or future-verification areas

| Area | Reason |
|---|---|
| Exact remote policy per company | Changes constantly |
| Whether a company accepts Colombia contractors | Must verify per opening |
| Whether a role is worldwide remote | Must verify posting |
| Whether a salary applies to Colombia-based contractor | Usually not direct |
| Whether export-service VAT treatment applies | Case-specific |
| Whether ARA is public-ready | Requires technical audit |
| Whether portfolio is strong enough | Requires external review |

---

# 6. Legal and administrative gap register

## Colombia contractor setup

| Item | Current status | Risk | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| RUT | Unknown | High | Confirm/update |
| CIIU code | Unknown | Medium | Select with accountant |
| Electronic invoicing | Unknown | High | Confirm requirement |
| IVA responsibility | Unknown | High | Verify with accountant |
| Export services treatment | Unknown | High | Verify per contract |
| Social security | Unknown | High | Define monthly process |
| ARL | Unknown | Medium | Verify by contract type |
| Payment method | Unknown | Medium | Choose Wise/Payoneer/SWIFT |
| Tax reserve | Unknown | High | Define percentage |
| Contract review process | Unknown | High | Create checklist |

## Required action

Before accepting international contractor work, consult a Colombian accountant or tax professional.

The strategy can proceed before that, but any signed contract must be checked.

## Germany / Portugal

| Item | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Portuguese passport | Expected future | Track documentation/timeline |
| EU work rights | Not current | Do not claim |
| Germany marriage route | Possible | Verify legal requirements if activated |
| German residence | Not current | Do not claim |
| German tax/health system | Future | Research when relocation is real |
| Portugal tax status | Future | Research when move is planned |

---

# 7. Portfolio readiness gap register

## TwinSight

| Asset | Status | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Case study text | Planned | Needs final public version |
| Demo video | Planned | Needs recording/editing |
| Screenshots | Needed | Must capture final build |
| WebGL demo | Unknown | Public URL needed if available |
| GitHub README | Planned | Needs final version |
| Metrics table | Available in draft | Verify final numbers |
| Contribution statement | Defined | Needs public wording |
| AI disclosure | Defined | Needs placement |
| Asset disclaimer | Needed | Confirm CAD/manufacturer permissions |
| Technical diagrams | Needed | Create pipeline/system diagrams |

## ARA

| Asset | Status | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Public repo | Unknown | Decide public/private |
| README | Needed | Draft controlled README |
| Demo | Unknown | Create screenshots or short run |
| Architecture diagram | Needed | Add if published |
| Claims | Risky | Avoid production/enterprise claims |

## Blender portrait

| Asset | Status | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Final renders | Unknown | Confirm |
| Breakdown | Needed | Topology/materials/grooming |
| ArtStation entry | Needed | Publish only if polished |

## ai-news-aggregator

| Asset | Status | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Functional state | Unknown | Test |
| Public value | Unclear | Only include if demo works |
| Main profile relevance | Low-medium | Do not prioritize |

## FitApp-Free

| Asset | Status | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Functional state | Unknown | Defer |
| Portfolio relevance | Low | Do not prioritize |
| Strategy role | Distraction risk | Keep private for now |

---

# 8. GitHub readiness gap register

## Required GitHub actions

| Action | Priority |
|---|---|
| Pin TwinSight first | Critical |
| Write TwinSight README | Critical |
| Add project images/GIFs | High |
| Hide weak tutorial repos | High |
| Archive old portfolio attempts | High |
| Clean repo descriptions | High |
| Add ARA README if public | Medium |
| Add GitHub profile README | Medium |
| Remove misleading thesis references | Critical |
| Add license/disclaimer where needed | Medium |

## GitHub risk

A weak GitHub front page can reduce credibility faster than having fewer public repos.

Quality beats quantity.

---

# 9. LinkedIn and CV gap register

## LinkedIn gaps

| Section | Required |
|---|---|
| Headline | Replace with final positioning |
| About | Rewrite around TwinSight and target roles |
| Experience | Reframe freelance/self-employed |
| Education | Correct thesis description |
| UNAL | Phrase as advanced coursework |
| Projects | Add TwinSight |
| Featured | Add portfolio/GitHub/demo |
| Skills | Reorder around Unity/C#/WebGL/Blender |
| Languages | English as professional/self-assessed |
| Work authorization | Colombia contractor now, EU future carefully |

## CV gaps

| Asset | Required |
|---|---|
| Base CV | Needed |
| Unity/Real-Time 3D CV | Needed |
| Technical Visualization CV | Needed |
| WebGL/Interactive 3D CV | Needed |
| Tools/Python CV | Later |
| Full-stack fallback CV | Only if needed |
| Bullet bank | Needed |
| One-page format | Required |

---

# 10. Company targeting gap register

## Current status

Section 11 provides a useful target ecosystem but should not be treated as a fully verified live database.

## Main limitations

| Limitation | Risk |
|---|---|
| Careers pages may change | Medium |
| Remote policies may be outdated | High |
| LinkedIn URLs may need verification | Medium |
| Some companies may not hire juniors | High |
| Some roles may require EU/US authorization | High |
| Some companies are too senior/enterprise | Medium |
| Salary tiers are estimates | Medium |

## Future agent task

Use mode agent only for a narrow verification task:

```text
Verify top 30 A-priority companies:
- active roles;
- careers URL;
- remote scope;
- contractor possibility;
- seniority;
- work authorization;
- relevant contact/recruiter if public.
```

Do not ask the agent to rebuild the whole strategy.

---

# 11. Application system readiness

## Ready

The application system is structurally ready.

It includes:

- A/B/C/Watchlist categories;
- tracker fields;
- weekly cadence;
- follow-up rules;
- customization depth;
- metrics;

# 17_cv_base_and_role_variants

## Purpose

This document converts the approved career strategy into CV-ready material.

It includes:

- a base one-page CV structure;
- role-specific CV variants;
- reusable bullet banks;
- project descriptions;
- skills blocks;
- education wording;
- training/course wording;
- language and work-authorization wording;
- claims to avoid;
- editing rules.

This is not the final designed PDF CV. It is the source text for producing one-page ATS-friendly resumes.

---

# 1. CV positioning rules

## Core identity

Use this as the main professional identity:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
```

Expanded version:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

## Primary CV target families

Use separate variants for:

1. Real-Time 3D / Unity Developer.
2. Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation Developer.
3. Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer.
4. Unity Technical Artist.
5. Tools / Python Automation Developer.

## Do not use one generic CV for every job

The base CV should be adapted per role family. The same facts can be reorganized, but the claims must remain consistent.

## Critical claim discipline

Do not claim:

- Senior Technical Artist.
- EU work authorization now.
- German residence now.
- Portuguese passport already issued.
- Unity certification if not obtained.
- Rebelway / CG Cookie / Alive certification if no certificate exists.
- Production AI engineer.
- Enterprise AI platform developer.
- Commercially shipped Unity product unless true.
- Full-stack specialist as primary identity.

---

# 3. Base CV — ATS-friendly one-page version

## Header

```text
Alexander Woodcock Salomón
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
Colombia | Open to remote contractor roles
Email: [email] | Phone: [phone]
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexander-woodcock-0132382a6/
GitHub: https://github.com/delarge95
Portfolio: [portfolio URL]
ArtStation: https://www.artstation.com/alexanderwoodcocksalomon3
```

## Professional summary

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment. Background in Multimedia Engineering with advanced Electronic Engineering coursework, combining Unity, C#, Blender, WebGL, technical UI, asset optimization, and Python-assisted tooling. Built TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting drone assembly through component selection, exploded views, cross-sections, visual modes, and usability evaluation.
```

Alternative shorter version:

```text
Unity-focused Real-Time 3D Developer specializing in interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, WebGL deployment, and technical UI. Built TwinSight X500, a thesis project that converts drone assembly documentation and CAD-derived assets into an optimized interactive 3D inspection experience.
```

## Technical skills

```text
Unity: C#, Unity WebGL, URP, UI Toolkit, Shader Graph, runtime interaction systems, component selection, visual modes, performance-conscious deployment

Real-Time 3D: CAD-to-realtime optimization, high-poly to low-poly workflow, retopology, UVs, baking, mesh optimization, technical visualization, WebGL constraints

3D Tools: Blender, Marmoset Toolbag, RizomUV, CAD-derived asset cleanup, hard-surface modeling, technical asset preparation

Programming & Tooling: C#, Python, Git/GitHub, AI-assisted coding workflows, basic FastAPI, LangGraph prototype experience, web automation concepts

Design & Evaluation: technical documentation, usability evaluation, SUS, NASA-TLX Raw, Think-Aloud, multimedia engineering, visual communication

Foundations: computer graphics, linear algebra, physics, electronics coursework, systems thinking
```

## Selected projects

### TwinSight X500 — Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Prototype

```text
Thesis project | Unity, C#, WebGL, URP, UI Toolkit, Blender
```

Bullets:

```text
- Built an interactive Unity WebGL 3D visualization prototype for inspecting and understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone.
- Developed runtime interaction systems for component selection, exploded view, cross-section/clipping, visual modes, and technical part information panels.
- Implemented a CAD-to-realtime asset workflow using Blender-based cleanup, optimization, retopology, UV preparation, and high-to-low asset processing.
- Optimized CAD-derived geometry from over 6.5M triangles to approximately 95,617 triangles. [verify final number]
- Designed a browser-accessible inspection experience focused on spatial understanding, technical clarity, and mobile/web performance constraints.
- Evaluated the prototype through usability and workload instruments, including SUS, NASA-TLX Raw, and Think-Aloud methodology. [verify final metrics]
- Used AI as an implementation and debugging assistant while retaining responsibility for architecture, integration, validation, technical judgment, and final ownership.
```

Shorter version for one-page CV:

```text
- Built TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection, including component selection, exploded view, cross-section tools, visual modes, and technical UI.
- Created a CAD-to-realtime pipeline using Blender optimization and asset preparation, reducing CAD-derived geometry from over 6.5M triangles to approximately 95,617 triangles. [verify final number]
- Evaluated the prototype using SUS, NASA-TLX Raw, and Think-Aloud methodology, connecting technical implementation with user-centered validation. [verify final metrics]
```

### ARA Framework — AI-Assisted Research Automation Prototype

```text
Prototype | Python, LangGraph, LangChain, Redis, Semantic Scholar API, Playwright/MCP concepts
```

Bullets:

```text
- Developed a Python-based research automation prototype using LangGraph-style agent orchestration for niche analysis, literature research, technical architecture planning, implementation guidance, and report synthesis.
- Designed a multi-agent workflow with checkpointing, budget awareness, external research APIs, PDF/document processing concepts, and structured Markdown report generation.
- Positioned the system as a research-tooling prototype, not as a production AI platform, emphasizing automation architecture, workflow design, and technical documentation.
```

Shorter version:

```text
- Built ARA Framework, a Python/LangGraph research automation prototype for multi-agent literature analysis, technical planning, and structured report generation.
```

### Hyperrealistic Blender Portrait — Technical Art Study

```text
Personal project | Blender, topology, materials, grooming, lighting, rendering
```

```text
- Completed a high-fidelity Blender portrait study focused on topology, material definition, grooming, lighting, and realistic rendering.
- Used the project as technical art evidence for 3D pipeline understanding rather than as a primary character-artist positioning asset.

```text

## Experience

```text

```

```text

- Used AI-assisted development workflows to accelerate implementation, debugging, research, and documentation while maintaining final technical ownership.
- Completed web/freelance projects for small clients, covering implementation, design support, deployment, and client communication. [adjust with actual client details]
```

### Earlier Professional Experience

Use only if space allows.

```text

```

```text

Bullets:

```text

```

### Universidad Nacional de Colombia — UNAL

Recommended wording:

```text

Bullets:

```text

- Academic background supports technical reasoning in real-time systems, optimization, hardware-aware thinking, and technical visualization.
```

Avoid:

```text
Bachelor’s degree in Electronic Engineering

## Courses and training

Use this section only if space allows.

```text
Selected non-certified training:
- CG Cookie HUMAN — High-Fidelity Character Pipeline & Topology
- Alive! — 3D Animation Mechanics & Dynamic Motion
- Rebelway courses — Houdini / real-time FX / procedural workflows [if completed or in progress]

```

## Languages

```

If no certificate exists, avoid:

Use:

```

## Availability and work authorization

Current safe wording:

```text
Available for remote contractor/B2B work from Colombia.
```

Expanded version:

```text
Currently based in Colombia and available for remote contractor/B2B work. Expected future Portuguese citizenship/passport may support EU work authorization in the medium term, but current applications should be treated as Colombia-based remote/contractor availability.
```

# 18_linkedin_final_rewrite

## Purpose

This document converts the approved career strategy and CV positioning into a complete LinkedIn profile rewrite.

It includes:

- final headline recommendation;
- 15 headline alternatives;
- About section;
- Experience rewrite;
- Education rewrite;
- Projects section;
- Featured section order;
- Skills ordering;
- Creator/activity strategy;
- recruiter keyword strategy;
- availability and work-authorization wording;
- future EU/Portugal/Germany wording;
- sections to avoid or downplay.

This document is written in English because the target market is international remote work.

---

# 1. LinkedIn positioning rule

The LinkedIn profile must communicate one coherent identity:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

It must not present separate unrelated identities such as:

```text
Full-stack developer + AI engineer + 3D artist + game developer + researcher + designer
```

Those areas can exist as supporting evidence, but not as equal headline identities.

---

# 2. Final recommended headline

Use this as the primary headline:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist | Unity WebGL, C#, CAD-to-Realtime Optimization, Technical Visualization
```

## Why this headline works

It balances:

- role identity;
- engine/tool keywords;
- technical visualization niche;
- recruiter-search keywords;
- portfolio alignment with TwinSight X500;
- enough specificity without overclaiming seniority.

It avoids:

- “Senior”;
- “AI Engineer” as primary identity;
- “Full-stack” as primary identity;
- vague “multimedia engineer” wording;
- generic “3D artist” positioning.

---

```text
I build interactive real-time 3D systems for technical visualization using Unity, C#, WebGL and Blender.

My main project is TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting and understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone. The project converts complex technical documentation and CAD-derived assets into an optimized interactive 3D experience with component selection, exploded views, cross-section tools, visual modes, technical UI, and usability/workload evaluation.

My strongest areas are:

- Unity / C# runtime interaction systems
- Unity WebGL deployment
- CAD-to-realtime asset optimization
- Blender-based technical asset preparation
- Interactive technical visualization
- Real-time inspection workflows
- Technical UI and documentation
- Python-assisted tooling and automation

I am currently completing my Multimedia Engineering degree at UNAD. I also completed advanced coursework in Electronic Engineering at Universidad Nacional de Colombia, which supports my technical foundation in mathematics, physics, systems thinking and engineering logic.

I am based in Colombia and available for remote contractor/B2B roles in real-time 3D, Unity, WebGL, technical visualization, digital twin visualization, simulation, XR-adjacent development, and technical art workflows.

I also build secondary tooling prototypes with Python and LLM orchestration, including ARA Framework, a research automation prototype. I treat AI as a productivity and implementation assistant, while maintaining responsibility for architecture, integration, testing, technical judgment and final ownership.

# TwinSight X500

**Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection.**

TwinSight X500 is an interactive browser-based 3D viewer for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone. It transforms CAD-derived drone assets into an optimized real-time Unity WebGL experience with component selection, exploded view, cross-section tools, visual modes and technical information panels.

> From static 2D documentation to interactive spatial understanding.

---

[![TwinSight X500 Demo](./media/twinsight-demo-thumbnail.jpg)](https://your-demo-video-link.com)

## Highlights

- Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype.
- Browser-based drone assembly inspection.
- CAD-derived geometry optimized for real-time interaction.
- Component-level selection and highlighting.
- Technical part information panels.
- Exploded assembly view.
- Cross-section / clipping inspection.
- Multiple visual modes: realistic, X-ray, ghosted, blueprint, wireframe, solid and thermal-style.
- Formative usability and workload evaluation using SUS, NASA-TLX Raw and Think-Aloud.

## Screenshots

| Viewer | Exploded View | Cross-Section |

| ![TwinSight viewer](./media/01_viewer.jpg) | ![Exploded view](./media/02_exploded_view.jpg) | ![Cross-section](./media/03_cross_section.jpg) |

## Technical Stack

| Area | Tools / Technologies |
|---|---|
| Engine | Unity |
| Programming | C# |
| Deployment | Unity WebGL |
| Rendering | URP, Shader Graph |
| UI | UI Toolkit |
| 3D pipeline | Blender |
| Asset pipeline | CAD-derived geometry, mesh cleanup, optimization |
| Evaluation | SUS, NASA-TLX Raw, Think-Aloud |

---

## Problem

Drone assembly documentation is often presented through static 2D diagrams, part lists and written instructions. This forces users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between components, orientations, fasteners and hidden structures.

For complex assemblies such as a Holybro X500 V2 drone, this increases cognitive effort and makes it harder to understand how parts relate to each other in 3D space.

---

## Solution

TwinSight X500 converts CAD-derived drone geometry into an optimized Unity WebGL viewer. Instead of reading static documentation, users can navigate the assembly, select components, inspect technical information, activate exploded view, cut through the model and switch between visual modes.

The goal is not only to show the drone, but to make the relationships between its parts easier to understand.

---

## Key Features

### Component Selection

Users can select drone components directly in the 3D viewer. The selected part is highlighted and linked to contextual technical information.

### Exploded View

The exploded view separates assemblies while preserving spatial logic, helping users understand component hierarchy and placement.

### Cross-Section / Clipping

The clipping tool cuts through the model to reveal hidden structures and internal relationships.

### Visual Modes

TwinSight includes several inspection modes:

- Realistic
- X-ray
- Ghosted
- Blueprint
- Wireframe
- Solid
- Thermal-style

> The thermal-style mode is a qualitative visual mode. It is not a physical thermal simulation, FEA result or sensor-driven thermal analysis.

### Technical UI

The interface provides technical part information while preserving the 3D inspection context.

---

## Technical Pipeline

```text
CAD-derived source
        ↓
Tessellation / conversion route exploration
        ↓
Blender cleanup and optimization
        ↓
Selectable component organization
        ↓
Unity import and scene setup
        ↓
Runtime interaction systems
        ↓
UI Toolkit interface
        ↓
Unity WebGL build
        ↓
Usability and workload evaluation
```

The pipeline focused on preserving the visual information needed for technical inspection while reducing complexity enough for browser-based real-time interaction.

---

## CAD-to-Realtime Optimization

A central technical challenge was converting complex CAD-derived geometry into a model suitable for Unity WebGL.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Optimized geometry | 95,617 triangles |
| Source CAD routes | 6.5M+ triangles |
| Canonical research parts | 28 |
| Scene nodes / anchors | 30 |
| Technical elements | 257 |

The final optimized model was prepared for browser-based real-time inspection while preserving the component structure needed for selection, exploded view and technical visualization.

---

## Unity WebGL Architecture

The Unity application coordinates runtime selection, visualization states, UI panels and inspection tools inside a WebGL build.

Main runtime systems:

- Model hierarchy and selectable parts.
- Selection and highlight system.
- Camera and navigation logic.
- Exploded-view state controller.
- Clipping / cross-section controller.
- Visual-mode switching system.
- Technical metadata / part information.
- UI Toolkit panels.
- WebGL deployment configuration.

---

## Evaluation

TwinSight X500 was evaluated as an academic/portfolio prototype using usability, workload and qualitative observation methods.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Participants | 12 |
| Task-condition records | 96 |
| SUS average | 91.88 |
| NASA-TLX Raw, 3D viewer | 8.69 |
| NASA-TLX Raw, 2D support | 19.89 |

The formative evaluation suggested high perceived usability and lower perceived workload for the 3D viewer condition compared with 2D support in the tested tasks.

---

## My Role

I worked across the complete prototype pipeline:

- Prepared and optimized CAD-derived drone geometry for real-time WebGL use.
- Organized selectable components and scene hierarchy.
- Implemented runtime interaction systems in Unity/C#.
- Built component selection, highlighting and information panels.
- Developed exploded view and clipping/cross-section interaction.
- Implemented multiple visual inspection modes.
- Designed technical UI and mobile-first interaction logic.
- Prepared evaluation workflow using SUS, NASA-TLX Raw and Think-Aloud.
- Documented constraints, findings and future improvements.

The source CAD model was used as the technical basis for the drone geometry. My work focused on transforming, optimizing, organizing and implementing it as an interactive real-time WebGL visualization prototype.

---

## AI-Assisted Workflow

AI assistance was used as an implementation and iteration support tool during parts of the development process. Final architecture decisions, debugging, Unity integration, asset preparation, evaluation design, documentation and project ownership remained my responsibility.

---

## Limitations

TwinSight X500 is an academic/portfolio prototype, not a deployed industrial product.

Current limitations:

- Not a production digital twin.
- No live IoT or sensor data.
- No predictive maintenance.
- No WebAR placement.
- No real thermal simulation.
- Formative academic evaluation.
- Prototype scope and WebGL constraints.

---

- Guided assembly sequences.
- Deeper metadata for each component.
- Search and part filtering.
- WebGPU or performance-focused rendering experiments.
- Optional XR inspection mode.
- Sensor/state data as a digital-twin extension.
- Expansion to other drones or technical assemblies.
- Improved mobile interaction and loading performance.

# 19_github_readme_templates

## Purpose

This document provides GitHub-facing templates and cleanup rules for Alexander Woodcock Salomón’s portfolio repositories.

It includes:

- GitHub profile README template;
- pinned repository order;
- repository naming rules;
- TwinSight X500 README template;
- ARA Framework README template;
- Blender technical breakdown README template;
- optional ai-news-aggregator README structure;
- repo descriptions;
- disclaimer language;
- AI-assisted development disclosure;
- asset/CAD/manufacturer disclaimer;
- commit and release hygiene;
- GitHub Pages / portfolio link guidance.

The objective is to make GitHub support the target profile:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

---

# 1. GitHub strategy

## Function of GitHub in this job search

GitHub is not the portfolio by itself. It is technical evidence.

It should prove:

- the project exists;
- technical scope is real;
- documentation is readable;
- code/project structure is not chaotic;
- the candidate can communicate implementation decisions;
- the candidate understands limitations and tradeoffs;
- AI assistance was used responsibly, not hidden or overclaimed.

## GitHub should not look like

- a dump of unfinished experiments;
- a student account with tutorial repos pinned;
- a full-stack profile if the target is real-time 3D;
- an AI engineer profile if ARA is not production-ready;
- a 3D artist profile without code or systems;
- a repository graveyard with no README.

## Main GitHub message

Every visible repo should support this message:

```text
I build technical real-time 3D systems, optimized assets, interactive visualization tools, and supporting automation workflows.
```

---

# 2. Public repository decision matrix

| Repository / project | Public status | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `WebGL-Thesis-Proposal` / TwinSight X500 | Public | Clean and make flagship |
| ARA Framework | Public only if runnable or understandable | Add controlled README |
| Portfolio site | Public | Use as GitHub Pages or source repo |
| Blender portrait breakdown | Public if polished | Use README or ArtStation link |
| ai-news-aggregator | Public only if demo-ready | Otherwise keep private |
| FitApp-Free | Private / defer | Not relevant now |
| tutorial repos | Public okay, not pinned | Avoid front-page emphasis |
| old portfolio attempts | Archive/private | Avoid confusion |
| client-sensitive repos | Private | Do not expose |
| unrelated experiments | Private/archive | Reduce noise |

---

# 3. Recommended pinned repository order

## Default pins

| Pin | Repository | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `TwinSight-X500` / current thesis repo | Flagship technical proof |
| 2 | `ARA-Framework` | Secondary automation/tooling proof |
| 3 | `portfolio` / `delarge95.github.io` | Public portfolio site |
| 4 | `blender-portrait-breakdown` | Supporting technical art proof |
| 5 | `ai-news-aggregator` | Only if functional |
| 6 | `unity-tools-or-scripts` | Optional future tools repo |

## If only three repos are ready

Pin only:

1. TwinSight X500.
2. Portfolio site.
3. ARA Framework.

Do not pin weak filler repos just to fill all six slots.

---

# 4. Repository naming rules

## Recommended naming

If renaming is possible without breaking thesis links:

```text
TwinSight-X500
ARA-Framework
alexander-woodcock-portfolio
blender-portrait-technical-study
ai-news-aggregator
unity-tools-prototypes
```

## If keeping current thesis repo name

Current:

```text
WebGL-Thesis-Proposal
```

Add a clear description:

```text
TwinSight X500 — Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection.
```

Add the project name in the README title:

```text
# TwinSight X500
```

Do not rely on the repository name alone.

---

# 5. GitHub profile README template

Create a repository named exactly:

```text
delarge95
```

Then add this README.

```markdown

Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.

---

# 6. TwinSight X500 README template

This is the most important repository README.

## Recommended file name

```text
README.md
```

## Template

```markdown
# TwinSight X500

Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection.

## Overview

TwinSight X500 is an interactive real-time 3D visualization prototype built in Unity WebGL to inspect and understand the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone.

The project transforms complex technical documentation and CAD-derived assets into an optimized browser-accessible 3D experience with component selection, exploded views, cross-section tools, visual modes and technical information panels.

Core idea:

> Seeing parts is not enough. Users need to understand spatial relationships.

## Project status

Thesis project completed. Public portfolio version in preparation / available at:

- Portfolio case study: PORTFOLIO_URL
- WebGL demo: DEMO_URL
- Demo video: VIDEO_URL

## My role

I was responsible for:

- Unity / C# implementation;
- runtime interaction systems;
- component selection workflows;
- exploded view behavior;
- cross-section / clipping tools;
- visual modes;
- technical UI and information panels;
- asset integration;
- CAD-to-realtime optimization workflow;
- Blender-based cleanup and preparation;
- documentation;
- usability/workload evaluation design and reporting;
- final integration and technical ownership.

AI-assisted tools were used as implementation, debugging, research and documentation support. Architecture decisions, integration, validation, technical judgment and final ownership remained my responsibility.

## Key features

- Interactive drone assembly inspection
- Component selection and highlighting
- Exploded view
- Cross-section / clipping tools
- Visual inspection modes
  - realistic
  - X-ray / ghosted
  - blueprint
  - wireframe
  - solid color
  - thermal-style qualitative mode
- Technical information panels
- Unity WebGL deployment
- Optimized CAD-derived assets
- Mobile/web-oriented interface considerations
- Academic usability and workload evaluation

## Technical stack

- Unity
- C#
- Unity WebGL
- URP
- UI Toolkit
- Shader Graph
- Blender
- Marmoset Toolbag
- RizomUV
- Git / GitHub

## CAD-to-realtime pipeline

The source model came from CAD/manufacturer-derived assets. The production workflow involved:

1. CAD conversion / import.
2. Geometry inspection.
3. Cleanup and simplification.
4. Blender-based optimization.
5. Retopology / low-poly preparation.
6. UV preparation.
7. High-to-low asset processing where relevant.
8. Material setup.
9. Unity import and integration.
10. WebGL-oriented optimization and testing.

## Optimization summary

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Triangle count | 6.5M+ | ~95,617 |
| Deployment target | CAD/native tools | Unity WebGL |
| Interaction model | Static documentation | Real-time 3D inspection |

> Verify these values against the final thesis report before publishing.

## Evaluation

The project was evaluated using:

- SUS;
- NASA-TLX Raw;
- Think-Aloud methodology;
- task-based comparison between 3D visualization and conventional 2D support.

Summary metrics:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Participants | 12 |
| SUS average | 91.88 |
| NASA-TLX Raw, 3D viewer | 8.69 |
| NASA-TLX Raw, 2D support | 19.89 |
| Task-condition records | 96 |

> Verify final values before public release.

## Screenshots

Add images here:

```markdown

![Component selection](docs/images/component-selection.png)
![Exploded view](docs/images/exploded-view.png)
![Cross-section](docs/images/cross-section.png)
![Visual modes](docs/images/visual-modes.png)
```

## Demo video

Add link:

```markdown
[Watch demo video](VIDEO_URL)
```

## Repository structure

```text
Assets/
  Scripts/
  UI/
  Materials/
  Models/
  Scenes/
Docs/
  images/
  diagrams/
  metrics/
README.md
```

Adjust to actual repository structure.

## What this project demonstrates

- Real-time 3D technical visualization
- Unity/C# runtime systems
- Unity WebGL deployment
- CAD-to-realtime optimization
- Technical UI design
- Interactive inspection workflows
- Usability-aware engineering
- Documentation and evaluation

## Limitations

This is an academic prototype, not a commercial production product.

Known limitations:

- based on thesis scope and available time;
- public version may differ from internal development version;
- some CAD/manufacturer-derived assets may require usage disclaimers;
- not a full engineering simulation or FEA system;
- thermal mode, if shown, is qualitative unless explicitly validated.

## Asset and manufacturer disclaimer

This project is an academic/portfolio prototype for technical visualization and assembly understanding.

Holybro X500 V2 references and CAD/manufacturer-derived geometry are used for educational and technical visualization purposes. This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Holybro.

## AI-assisted development disclosure

AI tools were used during parts of development for implementation support, debugging, research and documentation assistance.

AI did not replace technical ownership. Architecture, integration, validation, testing, technical judgment and final project decisions were handled by the developer.

## License

Code license: LICENSE_TYPE

Asset license: see asset disclaimer and repository notes.

If license status is uncertain, do not add an open license until asset/code rights are clear.

## Purpose

This document provides the copy, structure, page architecture and content rules for the public portfolio.

The portfolio should communicate one clear professional identity:

# 1. Portfolio objective

# 10. TwinSight case study copy

## Problem

```text
Drone assembly documentation often relies on 2D diagrams, manuals and static references. These materials can show individual parts, but they require users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between components, fasteners, subassemblies and assembly steps.

TwinSight X500 explores whether an interactive real-time 3D viewer can make those spatial relationships easier to inspect and understand.
```

## Context

```text
The project was developed as a Multimedia Engineering thesis. It uses the Holybro X500 V2 drone as a technical assembly case and focuses on converting complex technical documentation and CAD-derived assets into a browser-accessible Unity WebGL experience.
```

## My role

```text
I handled Unity/C# implementation, runtime interaction systems, technical UI, CAD-to-realtime asset optimization, Blender-based asset preparation, documentation, evaluation design and final integration.

AI-assisted tools were used as support for implementation, debugging, research and documentation. Architecture decisions, integration, testing, validation and final technical ownership remained my responsibility.
```

## Constraints

```text
The project had to balance technical clarity, real-time interaction, WebGL deployment constraints, academic scope, asset optimization, usability evaluation and limited production time.

The goal was not to build a full engineering simulation. The goal was to create an interactive technical visualization prototype for assembly inspection and spatial understanding.
```

## Solution overview

```text
TwinSight X500 provides an interactive 3D inspection environment where users can select components, view technical information, explore exploded views, use cross-section tools and switch between visual modes such as realistic, ghosted, blueprint, wireframe and qualitative thermal-style visualization.
```

## CAD-to-realtime pipeline

```text
The source geometry came from CAD/manufacturer-derived assets. The pipeline involved conversion, inspection, cleanup, optimization, Blender-based preparation, UV work, material planning, Unity integration and WebGL-conscious asset handling.

The goal was to reduce heavy CAD geometry while preserving component identity and assembly relationships.
```

## Optimization copy

```text
The project reduced dense CAD-derived geometry from over 6.5 million triangles to approximately 95,617 optimized triangles. [verify final metric]

This reduction was necessary to make the model suitable for real-time browser-based visualization while preserving the visual information needed for technical inspection.
```

## Interaction systems

```text
The runtime systems were designed around inspection rather than passive viewing.

Core interactions include:

- component selection;
- highlighting;
- technical information panels;
- exploded view;
- cross-section / clipping;
- visual mode switching;
- mobile/web-oriented UI behavior.
```

## Visual modes

```text
The visual modes allow users to inspect the drone from different technical perspectives. Realistic mode supports general recognition, wireframe and blueprint modes emphasize structure, ghosted/X-ray modes help reveal hidden relationships, and qualitative thermal-style visualization explores an alternative analytical layer.
```

## Evaluation

```text
The project was evaluated using usability and workload methods including SUS, NASA-TLX Raw and Think-Aloud methodology. [verify exact final metrics]

The evaluation was designed to compare interactive 3D support with conventional 2D reference material in assembly-inspection tasks.
```

## Results

Use only after verifying final numbers:

```text
Reported evaluation data included:

- 12 validation participants;
- SUS average: 91.88;
- NASA-TLX Raw: 8.69 for the 3D viewer;
- NASA-TLX Raw: 19.89 for the 2D support condition;
- 96 task-condition records.

These results should be presented as academic prototype findings, not as commercial product validation.
```

## Limitations

```text
TwinSight X500 is an academic prototype, not a commercial production product. It does not replace engineering CAD software, formal simulation tools, FEA analysis or manufacturer documentation.

Some visual modes are qualitative. Some asset usage may require public-display limitations. The public portfolio version may not include every model file from the original thesis project.
```

## What I would improve

```text
Given more time, I would improve build profiling, formalize LOD handling, refine mobile interaction details, add more structured user analytics, improve the public WebGL deployment pipeline, expand technical documentation and separate the prototype into clearer runtime modules.
```

## AI-assisted development note

```text
AI-assisted workflows were used during parts of development for implementation support, debugging, research and documentation. AI was not used as a replacement for technical ownership.

I remained responsible for architecture decisions, integration, validation, testing, tradeoff analysis and final project delivery.
```

## Asset/manufacturer disclaimer

```text
This project is an academic/portfolio prototype created for technical visualization and assembly-understanding purposes.

References to the Holybro X500 V2 platform and any CAD/manufacturer-derived assets are used for educational and technical visualization purposes only.

This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or officially supported by Holybro.
```
