# 21B_twinsight_demo_video_final_plan

## 0. Module status

```text
Module: 21B_twinsight_demo_video_final_plan.md
Date generated: 2026-06-12
Status: Complete v1
Purpose: Final production plan for TwinSight X500 demo videos
Input modules: 21, 29, 29B, 29C, B1, B5
Primary artifact: demo video system for portfolio, LinkedIn, GitHub and ArtStation
```

---

# 1. Objective

Produce a polished video system for **TwinSight X500**, the flagship portfolio project.

The video system must prove, in the shortest possible time, that Alexander can operate as:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
Unity WebGL · C# · CAD-to-Realtime · Technical Visualization · Interactive 3D
```

The video must not be a generic thesis presentation. It must be a recruiter-readable and technical-lead-readable demonstration of:

- final product quality;
- Unity WebGL implementation;
- runtime interaction;
- technical UI;
- CAD-to-realtime optimization;
- real-time visualization modes;
- evaluation evidence;
- clarity of role and contribution.

---

# 2. Strategic reason

The market evidence from B1 and B5 reinforces that video proof is not optional.

Relevant hiring signals found:

| Market signal | Implication for video |
|---|---|
| Unity / C# appears repeatedly | show Unity + C# clearly |
| Technical Art roles request pipeline and optimization | show visual modes and CAD optimization |
| Render / Graphic Programmer roles value shaders, math, GPU and performance | include visual mode and optimization evidence |
| VR / XR Unity roles value interaction and profiling | show runtime interaction and future XR-adjacent logic |
| LATAM remote roles ask for portfolio evidence | video must be portfolio-ready |
| Freelance/talent-pool roles ask for strong portfolio | video must be self-contained proof |
| Blender appears in some Unity/VR postings | show Blender pipeline briefly |
| Web platform appears in LATAM freelance roles | show browser/WebGL proof |

Conclusion:

```text
The video must show both product value and technical implementation.
```

---

# 3. Output video package

The required package has three videos.

| Asset | Duration | Purpose | Priority |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Main demo | 90–120 s | portfolio, LinkedIn Featured, case study | 1 |
| Short teaser | 30–45 s | LinkedIn post, homepage, quick recruiter skim | 2 |
| Technical breakdown | 4–7 min | interview follow-up, GitHub, technical validation | 3 |

## Minimum viable version

Before applications, at least produce:

```text
[ ] Main demo: 90–120 s
[ ] Short teaser: 30–45 s
[ ] 8–12 strong screenshots
[ ] Portfolio embed
[ ] GitHub README embed
[ ] LinkedIn Featured entry
```

The long technical breakdown can come after the main demo if time is limited.

---

# 4. Core positioning line

Use this exact positioning across the video package:

```text
TwinSight X500 is a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection.
```

Expanded version:

```text
It transforms CAD-derived drone assets into an optimized browser-based 3D viewer with component selection, exploded view, cross-section tools, visual modes, technical UI panels and usability/workload evaluation.
```

Do not lead with:

```text
This is my thesis.
```

The thesis context appears later as validation.

---

# 5. Audience hierarchy

## 5.1 Primary audience

```text
Technical hiring manager
Unity lead
Technical art lead
Interactive 3D studio founder
XR / visualization team
Nearshore recruiter screening portfolio
```

## 5.2 Secondary audience

```text
HR recruiter
LinkedIn viewer
ArtStation viewer
Academic evaluator
Freelance client
```

## 5.3 What each audience needs to see

| Audience | Needs to understand |
|---|---|
| Recruiter | role fit and keywords fast |
| Technical lead | implementation credibility |
| Technical artist | visual modes, pipeline, optimization |
| Visualization company | industrial/technical communication value |
| XR/simulation company | interaction logic and future extensibility |
| Freelance client | deliverable clarity and browser access |

---

# 6. Main demo — 90-second structure

## 6.1 Timeline

```text
00–05 s   Hook / hero shot
05–12 s   Problem: 2D documentation lacks spatial context
12–22 s   Solution: browser-based Unity WebGL viewer
22–34 s   Component selection and technical panels
34–46 s   Exploded view
46–58 s   Cross-section / clipping
58–68 s   Visual modes
68–78 s   CAD-to-realtime optimization
78–86 s   Evaluation metrics
86–90 s   Role, stack, links
```

## 6.2 Shot-by-shot plan

| Time | Shot | Caption | Purpose |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 00–03 | Final viewer hero | TwinSight X500 | immediate visual proof |
| 03–05 | Orbit with UI visible | Unity WebGL technical visualization | position clearly |
| 05–08 | 2D/manual support visual | Static 2D documentation hides spatial relationships | problem |
| 08–12 | transition to 3D viewer | Interactive spatial inspection in the browser | solution |
| 12–17 | browser frame + app load | Browser-based, no install required | WebGL proof |
| 17–22 | camera navigation | Real-time 3D drone assembly viewer | interaction |
| 22–27 | hover/select component | Component-level selection | runtime proof |
| 27–34 | info panel opens | Technical part information | UI proof |
| 34–40 | exploded view activation | Exploded assembly view | feature proof |
| 40–46 | exploded close-up | Understand hierarchy and placement | value proof |
| 46–52 | clipping plane movement | Cross-section inspection | technical inspection |
| 52–58 | internal structure exposed | Reveal hidden relationships | spatial reasoning |
| 58–64 | visual modes switch | X-ray · ghosted · blueprint · wireframe | technical art |
| 64–68 | visual modes grid | Multiple inspection modes | visual system |
| 68–73 | CAD high-poly / low-poly comparison | CAD-to-realtime optimization | pipeline proof |
| 73–78 | triangle count card | 6.5M+ source routes → 95,617 triangles | metric |
| 78–83 | evaluation card | SUS 91.88 · NASA-TLX Raw 8.69 vs 19.89 | validation |
| 83–86 | final viewer + metrics | Evaluated with 12 participants | credibility |
| 86–90 | end card | Unity · C# · WebGL · URP · UI Toolkit · Blender | stack |

---

# 7. Main demo — 120-second version

```text
112–120 s  Links / stack / role
```

## 120-second shot additions

| UI Toolkit | show bottom sheet / panel interaction |
| Runtime systems | show state transitions |

| GitHub proof | one-second repo/README preview |

# 8. Short teaser — 30–45 seconds

## 8.3 Teaser caption script

```text
Static 2D assembly docs are hard to understand.

TwinSight X500 turns drone assembly into an interactive Unity WebGL viewer.

Select components.
Explode the assembly.
Cut through structures.
Switch visual modes.
Inspect technical data.

CAD-derived assets optimized for browser-based real-time 3D.
```

---

# 9. Technical breakdown — 4–7 minutes

## 9.1 Purpose

The long breakdown is not for recruiters. It is for technical leads and interviews.

It should prove that Alexander understands:

- CAD optimization constraints;
- Unity WebGL constraints;
- runtime systems;
- technical UI;
- visual modes;
- evaluation logic;
- limitations.

## 9.2 Structure

```text
00:00–00:30   Project overview

02:00–02:50   Blender cleanup / asset preparation
```

| Optimization | wireframe before/after |
| Blender | object cleanup, UV, bake, organization |
| Unity | scene hierarchy, prefabs, UI |

| Interaction | selection, exploded, clipping |
| Visual modes | shader/material switch |

---

# 10. Captions

## 10.1 Caption rules

| Rule | Apply |
|---|---|
| Max length | 6–10 words |
| Style | technical, direct |
| Frequency | every major feature |
| Placement | lower third or side label |
| Contrast | readable over footage |

```text
Unity WebGL technical visualization

Component-level selection
```

Use:

```text
captions + restrained music
```

for:

- main demo;
- short teaser.

If voiceover is used, keep it minimal:

It converts CAD-derived assets into an optimized browser-based viewer with component selection, exploded view, cross-section tools, visual modes and technical UI panels. The prototype was evaluated with SUS, NASA-TLX and Think-Aloud protocols as part of an academic validation.

Do not use an overly promotional voiceover.

```text
revolutionary
game-changing
industry-leading
next-generation
metaverse
```

# 21_twinsight_demo_video_script_and_shotlist

## Purpose

This document defines the video plan for presenting **TwinSight X500** as the flagship portfolio asset.

It includes:

- 60-second demo script;
- 90-second demo script;
- 120-second demo script;
- silent version;
- LinkedIn cutdown;
- technical breakdown version;
- shot list;
- capture checklist;
- captions;
- voiceover text;
- editing structure;
- export formats;
- quality gate.

The goal is to make TwinSight understandable quickly to recruiters while still giving technical reviewers enough evidence to care.

---

# 1. Video objective

The demo video must communicate, in under two minutes:

1. what TwinSight X500 is;
2. why it exists;
3. what problem it solves;
4. what features were built;
5. what technical skills it demonstrates;
6. what the measurable outcomes were;
7. what role Alexander had in the project.

The video should not look like a thesis lecture. It should look like a concise technical product demo.

---

# 2. Primary audience

## Recruiter audience

Recruiters need to understand:

- this is a real Unity/WebGL project;
- the candidate can build interactive systems;
- the project is relevant to technical visualization, simulation, XR, digital twin, Unity and WebGL roles;
- there is enough substance to justify an interview.

## Technical reviewer audience

Technical reviewers need to see:

- Unity runtime interaction;
- asset optimization;
- inspection systems;
- cross-section/clipping;
- visual modes;
- UI behavior;
- WebGL/browser deployment;
- evaluation metrics;
- limitations handled honestly.

---

# 3. Core message

Use this as the video thesis:

```text
TwinSight X500 transforms drone assembly documentation and CAD-derived assets into an optimized Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for interactive inspection and spatial understanding.
```

Shorter version:

```text
Seeing parts is not enough. Users need to understand spatial relationships.
```

---

# 4. Video versions to produce

## Required versions

| Version | Duration | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Recruiter demo | 60 s | LinkedIn, quick applications |
| Portfolio demo | 90 s | Portfolio hero/project page |
| Technical breakdown | 120 s | GitHub, technical reviewers |
| Silent captioned version | 60–90 s | LinkedIn autoplay |
| Vertical cutdown | 30–45 s | Optional social post |

## Recommended production order

1. 90-second portfolio demo.
2. 60-second recruiter cut.
3. 120-second technical breakdown.
4. Silent LinkedIn version.

Do not start with the 120-second version. It can become too dense.

---

# 5. Visual style

## Recommended style

| Element | Direction |
|---|---|
| Background | Dark or neutral |
| Text | Minimal, large, readable |
| Pace | Fast but not chaotic |
| Transitions | Simple cuts / fades |
| Captions | Short phrases |
| Audio | Clean voiceover or no voice |
| Music | Optional, subtle, non-distracting |
| Visual priority | App footage first |
| Branding | Minimal |

## Avoid

- long intro animation;
- thesis defense tone;
- generic motivational music;
- excessive text;
- tiny UI text;
- shaky screen recording;
- uncompressed laggy capture;
- showing development errors;
- overexplaining AI;
- putting legal disclaimers in the main video.

---

# 6. Capture requirements

## Minimum capture quality

| Parameter | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Resolution | 1920×1080 |
| Frame rate | 30 fps minimum |
| Format | MP4 H.264 |
| Audio | 48 kHz if voiceover |
| Cursor | Visible only if useful |
| UI scale | Large enough |
| Browser | Clean window |
| Notifications | Off |
| Desktop clutter | Hidden |

## Capture tools

Use any stable screen recorder:

- OBS Studio;
- Nvidia ShadowPlay;
- Windows Game Bar;
- macOS screen recording;

## 120-second voiceover

```text
This is TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype built to inspect and understand the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone.

The research problem comes from technical assembly documentation. Static diagrams and manuals identify components, but they often require users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between parts, subassemblies and fasteners.

TwinSight explores an interactive alternative: a browser-accessible real-time 3D viewer focused on inspection and spatial understanding.

The prototype allows users to orbit the drone, select components, highlight parts and access technical information panels.

The component selection system is designed around inspection workflows. The goal is not just to click a mesh, but to connect geometry, identity and technical information.

The exploded view separates the drone into readable groups while preserving assembly logic. This helps users understand how components relate to each other in space.

Cross-section and clipping tools support internal inspection, allowing hidden areas and layered components to be analyzed more clearly.

The project also includes visual modes such as realistic, ghosted, blueprint, solid color and wireframe-style views. These modes support different inspection tasks.

A major technical part of the project was the CAD-to-realtime pipeline. Dense CAD-derived geometry had to be converted, cleaned, optimized and prepared for Unity WebGL deployment.

The workflow included Blender-based cleanup, retopology and asset preparation, with the goal of preserving component identity while reducing the model enough for browser-based interaction.

Reported thesis metrics include geometry reduction from over 6.5 million triangles to approximately 95,617 optimized triangles, plus usability and workload evaluation using SUS, NASA-TLX Raw and Think-Aloud. These final values should be verified against the thesis report before public release.

My role covered Unity/C# implementation, runtime interaction systems, technical UI, CAD-to-realtime asset preparation, documentation, evaluation design and final integration.

TwinSight is an academic prototype, not a commercial engineering tool, but it demonstrates the kind of real-time 3D technical visualization work I want to continue building.
```

## Purpose

This document provides reusable outreach templates for the international job-search system.

- contractor setup explanations;
- future Portuguese / EU mobility explanations;

- explaining AI-assisted development;
- answering “Why should we hire you?”

The goal is to support consistent, direct, non-desperate, evidence-based communication.

- direct;
- technically specific;
- concise;
- evidence-based;
- no begging;
- no exaggerated enthusiasm;
- no inflated seniority.

- “I can do anything”;

# 23_interview_answer_bank

## Purpose

This document provides prepared interview answers for Alexander Woodcock Salomón’s target roles.

It converts the strategy, CV, LinkedIn, portfolio, TwinSight case study, negotiation framework and outreach documents into interview-ready language.

The answers are written primarily in English because the target market is international. Spanish versions are included where they are useful for LATAM or Spanish-speaking recruiters.

---

# 1. Interview positioning rule

Every interview answer should reinforce the same profile:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

Do not drift into:

- generic full-stack developer;
- pure 3D artist;
- AI engineer;
- game designer;
- graphic designer;
- general multimedia generalist.

---

# 2. Core interview narrative

## 30-second version

```text
I’m a Colombia-based Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on Unity WebGL, C#, technical visualization and CAD-to-realtime optimization. My strongest project is TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL drone assembly inspection prototype with component selection, exploded view, cross-section tools, visual modes, technical UI and usability/workload evaluation. # 17. “How would you debug low FPS in Unity WebGL?”
```

## Answer

```text
I would start by separating whether the bottleneck is CPU, GPU, memory, loading or browser-specific overhead.

First, I would profile in Unity and then test the WebGL build in the browser because editor performance can be misleading. I would check draw calls, triangle count, material count, texture sizes, overdraw, scripts running per frame and garbage allocation.

For WebGL specifically, I would also check build size, memory configuration, compression, asset loading, shader complexity and browser console warnings.

Then I would apply fixes based on evidence: reduce geometry, combine or simplify materials, optimize textures, remove unnecessary update loops, avoid allocations, simplify shaders, use LODs where appropriate and reduce UI or rendering overhead.
```

# 18. “How would you structure an exploded view system?”

## Answer

```text
I would treat exploded view as a controlled transformation system.

Each component or group needs an original position and an exploded target position. The system should store those transforms, interpolate between them, and preserve assembly relationships through grouping or hierarchy.

For a technical visualization project, I would avoid random outward movement. The exploded direction should communicate structure, so it should be based on assembly logic, axes, component groups or manually authored offsets.

I would also keep it reversible, expose a slider or state control, and ensure selection/highlighting still works in both assembled and exploded states.
```

---

# 19. “How would you implement component selection?”

## Answer

```text
I would use colliders, raycasting and a mapping between scene objects and component metadata.

The selection system should not only identify a mesh. It should connect the selected object to a data model containing name, category, technical information, hierarchy, parent/child relationships and UI behavior.

I would also separate visual feedback from selection logic. That way highlighting, isolation, ghosting or UI updates can be changed without rewriting the selection core.
```

---

# 20. “How would you implement cross-section / clipping?”

## Answer

```text
At a high level, I would use a clipping plane or shader-based clipping approach, depending on the rendering pipeline and platform constraints.

The system needs a plane position, orientation and user control. Materials or shaders then discard fragments on one side of the plane. For Unity WebGL, I would keep the shader approach as simple as possible and test compatibility carefully.

If the project requires capped cross-sections or engineering-grade sectioning, that becomes more complex and may require mesh processing or specialized rendering techniques. For a visualization prototype, shader-based clipping is often a practical starting point.
```

# 21. “What is CAD-to-realtime?”

## Answer

```text
CAD-to-realtime is the process of converting CAD or engineering-derived geometry into assets that can run efficiently in a real-time engine like Unity.

CAD models are usually built for precision and manufacturing, not for real-time rendering. They can contain dense geometry, excessive detail, problematic topology, many small parts, or structures that are inefficient for WebGL or real-time engines.

The workflow usually involves conversion, cleanup, simplification, retopology where needed, UV preparation, material planning, hierarchy organization, optimization and engine integration.

The goal is to preserve the technical meaning of the object while making it usable in an interactive real-time environment.
```

career_docs.title: 24_offer_evaluation_scorecard
career_docs.content:
# 24_offer_evaluation_scorecard

## Purpose

This document provides a practical system for evaluating, negotiating, accepting or rejecting job offers.

It is designed for a Colombia-based Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist targeting international remote work, contractor/B2B roles, Unity WebGL, technical visualization, simulation, digital twin, XR-adjacent work and Python tooling as a secondary route.

The system is not legal, tax or immigration advice. Any contract, tax setup or relocation decision should be reviewed with qualified professionals.

---

# 1. Core decision rule

Do not accept an offer only because it is international.

An offer is strategically useful only if it satisfies most of these conditions:

1. compensation is above the minimum threshold;
2. net income is acceptable after taxes, fees and social security;
3. the role strengthens the real-time 3D / Unity / technical visualization path;
4. contract terms are clear;
5. payment risk is controlled;
6. IP and exclusivity terms are reasonable;
7. remote work from Colombia is legally and operationally feasible;
8. the role does not create major strategic dilution;
9. the work can build toward USD 3k–6k/month over 12–24 months.

---

# 2. Offer categories

## Offer type classification

| Type | Description | Default stance |
|---|---|---|
| Strategic offer | Strong role fit + acceptable compensation + safe structure | Consider strongly |
| Cashflow offer | Pays acceptably but weak strategic fit | Accept only if needed |
| Portfolio leverage offer | Lower pay but strong proof/project value | Consider selectively |
| Risky offer | Unclear pay, scope or legal terms | Renegotiate or reject |
| Dilution offer | Pulls profile away from target path | Usually reject |
| Exploitative offer | Free labor, vague equity, abusive terms | Reject |

## Role-fit classification

| Role | Strategic value |
|---|---|
| Real-Time 3D / Unity | High |
| Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D | High |
| Technical Visualization / Digital Twin | High |
| Unity Technical Artist | High if runtime/optimization/tools |
| XR / Simulation | Medium-high |
| Tools / Python Automation | Medium |
| Full-stack | Low-medium |
| 3D Artist / Generalist | Low unless technical |
| Generic web design | Low |
| AI hype role without real scope | Risky |

---

# 3. Offer scorecard

Score each criterion from 1 to 5.

Then multiply by weight.

## Main scorecard

| Criterion | Weight | Score |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gross compensation | 15 | 1–5 |
| Estimated net compensation | 15 | 1–5 |
| Role fit | 20 | 1–5 |
| Portfolio leverage | 15 | 1–5 |
| Contract clarity | 10 | 1–5 |
| Payment reliability | 10 | 1–5 |
| Remote feasibility | 10 | 1–5 |
| Growth / learning ROI | 5 | 1–5 |
| Total | 100 | — |

## Interpretation

| Total score | Decision |
|---:|---|
| 85–100 | Strong accept / negotiate upward |
| 70–84 | Acceptable if no hidden risks |
| 55–69 | Renegotiate or accept only for cashflow |
| 40–54 | Usually reject |
| Under 40 | Reject |

## Automatic override

Reject even if score is high if there is:

- no written contract;
- unclear payment terms;
- broad unpaid test;
- abusive IP assignment;
- illegal or impossible work authorization assumption;
- non-payment history;
- requirement to misrepresent status;
- broad non-compete;
- no clarity on contractor vs employee;
- request for free production work.

---

# 4. Scoring definitions

## Gross compensation

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | USD 6k+/month or equivalent high-value contract |
| 4 | USD 3k–6k/month |
| 3 | USD 1.5k–3k/month |
| 2 | Below USD 1.5k/month but acceptable short-term |
| 1 | Below minimum or unpaid/equity-only |

## Estimated net compensation

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Strong net after taxes, fees, social security and reserves |
| 4 | Good net, manageable deductions |
| 3 | Acceptable net but not high leverage |
| 2 | Net barely above local alternatives |
| 1 | Net too low after obligations |

## Role fit

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Direct Unity/WebGL/technical visualization/digital twin/simulation fit |
| 4 | Strong Unity/3D fit with one missing area |
| 3 | Adjacent technical role |
| 2 | Weakly related |
| 1 | Dilutes profile |

## Portfolio leverage

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Strengthens TwinSight direction directly |
| 4 | Adds relevant production proof |
| 3 | Adds useful but adjacent proof |
| 2 | Little portfolio value |
| 1 | Creates irrelevant work history |

## Contract clarity

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Clear written contract, scope, IP, payment, termination |
| 4 | Mostly clear, minor gaps |
| 3 | Usable but needs clarification |
| 2 | Significant ambiguity |
| 1 | No contract or vague agreement |

## Payment reliability

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Established company, predictable payroll/payment |
| 4 | Good reputation, clear terms |
| 3 | Unknown but acceptable safeguards |
| 2 | Delayed/client-dependent payment |
| 1 | High non-payment risk |

## Remote feasibility

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Explicitly remote worldwide or LATAM contractor |
| 4 | Remote possible with clear contractor structure |
| 3 | Remote allowed but legal setup unclear |
| 2 | Remote only with friction |
| 1 | Requires unavailable authorization or relocation |

## Growth / learning ROI

| Score | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Strong mentorship, technical growth, production standards |
| 4 | Good learning exposure |
| 3 | Some growth |
| 2 | Repetitive or low-growth |
| 1 | Stagnant or harmful |

---

# 5. Compensation thresholds

## Current target bands

| Band | Monthly gross | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| Minimum target | USD 1.5k | Entry acceptable |
| Starter international | USD 2k–3k | Good early target |
| Strong 6-month target | USD 3k–4.5k | Preferred |
| High-value contractor | USD 5k–6k+ | Strong strategic offer |
| Long-term upside | USD 6k+ | 12–24 month target |

## Decision by compensation

| Compensation | Default decision |
|---|---|
| Under USD 1.5k | Reject unless urgent cashflow or exceptional portfolio value |
| USD 1.5k–2k | Accept only if role fit is strong |
| USD 2k–3k | Viable early offer |
| USD 3k–4.5k | Strong 3–6 month target |
| USD 4.5k–6k | Strong offer |
| USD 6k+ | High-value, evaluate legal/contract risk carefully |

## Important distinction

Always separate:

```text
Gross compensation
Net compensation
Cashflow timing
Long-term value
```

A high gross offer with delayed, risky or non-compliant payment can be worse than a lower but stable offer.

---

# 6. Gross-to-net checklist

Before accepting a contractor offer, estimate:

| Item | Question |
|---|---|
| Gross monthly | What is the nominal amount? |
| Currency | USD, EUR, COP or other? |
| Payment fees | Wise, Payoneer, PayPal, SWIFT, bank spread? |
| Conversion loss | What exchange rate applies? |
| Taxes | What must be reserved? |
| Social security | EPS, pension, ARL? |
| Accountant | Monthly cost? |
| Software/equipment | Who pays? |
| Vacation | Unpaid or paid? |
| Sick days | Unpaid or paid? |
| Payment delay | 7, 15, 30, 45, 60 days? |
| Contract termination | How much notice? |

## Net estimate formula

Use a conservative model:

```text
Estimated net = gross
- platform/payment fees
- currency conversion loss
- tax reserve
- social security
- accountant/admin costs
- unpaid time reserve
- software/equipment costs
```

## Required reserve

For contractor income, keep reserves for:

- taxes;
- social security;
- slow payment;
- contract termination;
- equipment failure;
- medical/emergency buffer;
- unpaid vacation.

---

# 7. Colombia contractor compliance checklist

## Before signing

Confirm:

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| RUT | Confirmed / pending |
| CIIU activity | Confirmed with accountant |
| Electronic invoicing | Confirmed / pending |
| IVA responsibility | Confirmed with accountant |
| Export-service treatment | Confirmed per contract |
| EPS/pension/ARL | Process defined |
| Payment method | Confirmed |
| Contract language | Reviewed |
| IP terms | Reviewed |
| Tax reserve | Defined |
| Accountant | Selected |

## Ask accountant

Questions to ask:

1. What CIIU code should be used for Unity / software / technical visualization services?
2. Does this service qualify as export of services?
3. How should invoices be issued to foreign clients?
4. Is IVA applicable in this specific scenario?
5. What social security base should be used?
6. How should foreign currency payments be documented?
7. What deductions or costs can be supported?
8. What monthly tax reserve is prudent?
9. What documents should be kept for DIAN?
10. Are there risks if the relationship looks employee-like?

---

# 8. Contractor vs employee evaluation

## Contractor advantages

| Advantage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| International access | Easier for foreign companies |
| Higher gross potential | Often better than local salary |
| Flexibility | Can work with global clients |
| Portfolio control | Project-based leverage |
| Faster entry | No sponsorship needed |

## Contractor disadvantages

| Disadvantage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| No benefits | No paid vacation unless negotiated |
| Tax/admin burden | Must manage compliance |
| Payment risk | Late or non-payment possible |
| No job security | Contract can end quickly |
| Misclassification risk | If relationship is employee-like |
| Equipment/software | Often self-funded |

## Employee advantages

| Advantage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Stability | More predictable |
| Benefits | Health, vacation, severance depending on jurisdiction |
| Lower admin | Payroll handled |
| Team integration | Better mentorship |
| Career signaling | Stronger formal experience |

## Employee disadvantages

| Disadvantage | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Lower flexibility | Less control |
| Authorization barriers | Foreign employment may require local setup |
| Lower local salary | Colombia salaries may be lower |
| EOR dependency | Employer must support structure |

## EOR evaluation

EOR is useful if:

- company wants employee relationship;
- role is long-term;
- compensation justifies EOR cost;
- employer is willing to pay platform fees;
- compliance matters.

EOR is less likely for:

- small studios;
- short contracts;
- low-budget roles;
- trial projects.

---

# 9. Contract terms checklist

## Must be clear

| Term | Required clarity |
|---|---|
| Parties | Legal names |
| Role | Scope and title |
| Start date | Exact |
| End date | If fixed-term |
| Compensation | Amount and currency |
| Payment schedule | Weekly/monthly/milestones |
| Payment method | Bank/Wise/Payoneer/etc. |
| Late payment | Consequence or remedy |
| Work hours | Expected availability |
| Time zone | Required overlap |
| Deliverables | Defined |
| IP ownership | Clear |
| Confidentiality | Reasonable |
| Exclusivity | Limited or absent |
| Non-compete | Avoid broad terms |
| Termination | Notice period |
| Dispute law | Jurisdiction |
| Equipment/software | Who pays |
| Taxes | Contractor responsibility if B2B |
| Data/security | Reasonable requirements |

## Dangerous contract terms

| Clause | Risk |
|---|---|
| Broad non-compete | Blocks future work |
| Broad exclusivity | Prevents other clients |
| Work-for-hire over all past/future work | IP abuse |
| Payment only after client approval | Cashflow risk |
| Unlimited unpaid revisions | Scope creep |
| No termination notice | Instability |
| No late-payment remedy | Non-payment risk |
| Mandatory unpaid trial | Exploitation |
| Confusing employee/contractor language | Misclassification |
| Jurisdiction impossible to enforce | Legal risk |

---

# 10. Take-home test evaluation

## Acceptable test

A take-home test is acceptable if:

- it is small;
- it has a clear time limit;
- it is relevant to the role;
- it does not produce usable client work;
- it has clear evaluation criteria;
- it does not require unpaid multi-day labor;
- IP terms are clear;
- the company is credible.

## Reasonable test examples

| Role | Reasonable test |
|---|---|
| Unity Developer | Small interaction prototype |
| Technical Artist | Shader/material or optimization task |
| WebGL | Small build/performance task |
| Tools | Small editor script |
| Python Automation | Small workflow script |
| Digital Twin | Conceptual architecture task |

## Unreasonable test examples

| Test | Reason |
|---|---|
| Full feature implementation | Free labor |
| Client-ready prototype | Exploitation |
| Multi-day unpaid build | Excessive |
| Unclear ownership | IP risk |
| No feedback | Low value |
| Requires private assets without agreement | Legal risk |
| Looks like production backlog | Red flag |

## Test negotiation script

```text
I’m open to a focused technical exercise. To keep the scope reasonable, could we define an expected time limit and clarify whether the test is only for evaluation and not production use?
```

## Test refusal script

```text
I’m not comfortable completing a large unpaid production-style task. I would be open to a smaller scoped exercise, a paid test, a portfolio walkthrough, or a live technical discussion instead.
```

---

# 11. Red flags

## Critical red flags

Reject or pause if:

- no written contract;
- payment terms unclear;
- company refuses to define scope;
- asks for free production work;
- broad non-compete;
- broad IP claim over unrelated work;
- payment only after client approval;
- “remote” but requires unavailable work authorization;
- asks to misrepresent legal status;
- insists on employee-like control under contractor structure;
- salary below minimum with no strategic upside;
- company has public non-payment complaints.

## Moderate red flags

Negotiate or clarify if:

- vague role title;
- unclear reporting structure;
- unclear timezone expectations;
- no onboarding process;
- vague “startup equity” promises;
- unclear tool/software reimbursement;
- all communication only by chat;
- no technical interviewer;
- constant urgency;
- trial period without clear compensation.

## Low-level warning signs

Monitor if:

- delayed recruiter responses;
- overly broad job description;
- role mixes too many unrelated skills;
- no clear product/project;
- old job posting;
- compensation hidden until late;
- vague remote policy.

---

# 12. Offer-specific questions

## Compensation

Ask:

```text
What is the gross compensation?
What currency is used?
Is payment monthly, biweekly or milestone-based?
What are the payment terms?
Are there late-payment protections?
Is compensation fixed, hourly or retainer-based?
```

## Contractor structure

Ask:

```text
Is this B2B/contractor, employee, EOR or freelance?
Who is the legal contracting entity?
What invoices or tax forms are required?
Is there a required platform?
Is there a trial period?
```

## Scope

Ask:

```text
What are the first 30/60/90 day deliverables?
What does success look like?
What is the expected weekly availability?
How much meeting time is expected?
What timezone overlap is required?
```

## IP and confidentiality

Ask:

```text
Who owns the deliverables?
Does IP assignment apply only to paid work?
Are personal/portfolio projects excluded?
Can I show non-confidential work in my portfolio?
Are there confidentiality restrictions?
```

## Technical role

Ask:

```text
What engine/platform is used?
What Unity version and render pipeline?
Is WebGL/XR/mobile/desktop the target?
How is profiling handled?
How is asset optimization handled?
Will I write production C#?
Will I work with artists/designers/engineers?
```

---

# 13. Acceptance thresholds

## Strong accept

Accept if:

- score above 80;
- compensation meets target;
- contract is clear;
- role fit is strong;
- remote structure is feasible;
- payment risk is low;
- no major red flags;
- portfolio leverage is high.

## Conditional accept

Accept if:

- score 65–80;
- compensation is acceptable;
- role fit is useful;
- risks can be negotiated;
- cashflow or formal experience value is meaningful.

## Reject

Reject if:

- score below 55;
- compensation below minimum;
- role dilutes profile severely;
- payment risk is high;
- contract is unclear;
- unpaid work is excessive;
- authorization assumptions are false;
- IP/exclusivity terms are abusive.

---

# 14. Negotiation strategy

## General rule

Negotiate based on structure, not just salary.

Consider:

- rate;
- hours;
- payment timing;
- trial period;
- deliverables;
- IP;
- exclusivity;
- scope;
- timezone;
- renewal terms;
- portfolio usage;
- software/equipment.

## If compensation is low but role is strong

Negotiate:

```text
higher rate after trial;
shorter trial period;
reduced hours;
clear portfolio permission;
defined scope;
milestone payment;
review after 30/60 days.
```

## If role is good but contractor risk is high

Negotiate:

```text
advance payment;
short payment cycle;
written contract;
clear termination notice;
paid test;
no broad exclusivity;
limited IP assignment.
```

## If company wants full-time contractor

Clarify:

```text
expected hours;
exclusivity;
benefits;
paid time off;
tools;
whether relationship is truly contractor;
tax responsibility;
EOR possibility.
```

---

# 15. Negotiation scripts

## Ask for higher compensation

```text
Based on the scope, expected availability and the technical requirements around Unity, WebGL and real-time 3D visualization, I would be more comfortable at [target range].

If that is above the current budget, we could also discuss adjusting scope, hours, trial length or review timing.
```

## Ask for paid test

```text
I’m open to a technical evaluation. Since the task appears close to production work and may take several hours, would you be open to making it a paid test or reducing the scope to a shorter evaluation exercise?
```

## Ask for clearer scope

```text
Before accepting, I would like to clarify the first deliverables, expected weekly availability, decision-making process and success criteria for the first 30 days.
```

## Ask about IP

```text
Could you clarify whether IP assignment applies only to paid deliverables created under this contract, and whether my previous work, portfolio projects and independent tools are excluded?
```

## Ask about contractor structure

```text
Since I am based in Colombia, I want to confirm whether this would be structured as an independent contractor/B2B agreement, EOR employment or another setup.
```

## Decline politely

```text
Thank you for the offer. After reviewing the compensation, scope and contract structure, I do not think this is the right fit at this stage.

I appreciate the opportunity and would be open to reconnecting in the future if there is a role with clearer alignment around Unity, real-time 3D or technical visualization.
```

---

# 16. Offer comparison model

When comparing two offers, do not choose only by gross pay.

## Comparison table

| Criterion | Offer A | Offer B |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gross monthly | — | — |
| Estimated net | — | — |
| Role fit | — | — |
| Portfolio value | — | — |
| Payment stability | — | — |
| Contract safety | — | — |
| Timezone fit | — | — |
| Learning value | — | — |
| Future salary leverage | — | — |
| EU relevance | — | — |
| Red flags | — | — |
| Total score | — | — |

## Tie-breaker

If two offers are similar, prefer the one that:

1. strengthens TwinSight-aligned positioning;
2. gives formal production experience;
3. has better payment reliability;
4. avoids legal ambiguity;
5. improves future compensation;
6. allows portfolio-safe work;
7. does not consume all time for low leverage.

---

# 17. Strategic offer examples

## Offer A — Low pay, strong fit

Example:

```text
USD 1.8k/month contractor
Unity WebGL technical visualization
Clear contract
Good portfolio permission
```

Decision:

```text
Possible accept if cashflow is needed and role creates strong production proof.
Negotiate review after 60 days.
```

## Offer B — Higher pay, weak fit

Example:

```text
USD 3k/month
Generic WordPress/web support
No Unity/3D work
```

Decision:

```text
Accept only if cashflow pressure is high.
Do not treat as main career path.
Limit duration if possible.
```

## Offer C — High pay, high risk

Example:

```text
USD 5k/month
Startup contractor
No contract
Payment after client approval
Broad IP terms
```

Decision:

```text
Do not accept without fixing contract/payment/IP risk.
```

## Offer D — Strong strategic offer

Example:

```text
USD 3.5k–5k/month
Unity technical visualization
Remote contractor from Colombia
Clear contract
Defined deliverables
Portfolio-safe non-confidential work
```

Decision:

```text
Strong accept/negotiation candidate.
```

---

# 18. EU mobility and offer evaluation

## Current state

Currently, evaluate offers as:

```text
Colombia-based remote contractor
```

Do not evaluate as:

```text
EU-authorized candidate
```

until legal status exists.

## After Portuguese passport

The offer pool changes.

Higher priority can shift toward:

- EU employee roles;
- Germany/Portugal/Netherlands/Spain roles;
- hybrid EU roles;
- EOR or payroll roles in Europe;
- stronger long-term compensation paths.

## Germany route

If German residence/work authorization becomes active, evaluate:

- German salary vs Colombian contractor net;
- health insurance;
- taxes;
- cost of living;
- local language;
- career leverage;
- long-term stability.

## Do not relocate for weak offers

Relocation should require:

- strong role fit;
- legal clarity;
- sufficient compensation;
- housing feasibility;
- health insurance clarity;
- long-term career value.

---

# 19. Role dilution test

Before accepting, ask:

```text
Will this role make my next application stronger for Unity / real-time 3D / technical visualization?
```

## If yes

Likely strategic.

## If no

Treat as cashflow only.

## If actively negative

Reject unless survival requires it.

## Dilution examples

| Offer | Dilution risk |
|---|---|
| Generic social media design | High |
| WordPress maintenance only | Medium-high |
| Data entry / AI labeling | High |
| Pure call center | High |
| Low-end 3D modeling only | Medium |
| Full-stack CRUD only | Medium |
| Unity mobile game support | Low-medium |
| WebGL product configurator | Low |
| Digital twin Unity role | Very low |

---

# 20. Offer go/no-go checklist

## Go

Proceed if:

- role fit is clear;
- compensation meets threshold;
- net estimate works;
- contract is written;
- payment method is clear;
- scope is defined;
- IP terms are reasonable;
- remote setup is feasible;
- no false work authorization assumption;
- no major red flags.

## No-go

Do not proceed if:

- no written agreement;
- payment terms are vague;
- compensation below minimum;
- unpaid work is excessive;
- company refuses scope clarity;
- IP terms capture unrelated work;
- remote status is misleading;
- requires unavailable EU/US authorization;
- role damages the portfolio path;
- company pressure feels manipulative.

---

# 21. Final offer decision worksheet

Use this before accepting.

```text
Company:
Role:
Offer date:
Employment type:
Location:
Remote scope:
Contractor/EOR/employee:
Gross compensation:
Currency:
Payment cycle:
Estimated net:
Expected hours:
Timezone overlap:
Start date:
Trial period:
Termination notice:
IP terms:
Exclusivity:
Portfolio permission:
Main responsibilities:
Main risks:
Score:
Decision:
Negotiation points:
Final answer deadline:
```

---

# 22. Final recommendation

The safest decision model is:

```text
Do not optimize only for the first paycheck.
Optimize for the intersection of compensation, contract safety and real-time 3D positioning.
```

The ideal first international offer is not necessarily the highest gross number.

The best offer is the one that:

1. pays enough;
2. is legally and operationally clear;
3. strengthens the Unity / real-time 3D / technical visualization path;
4. creates credible professional experience;
5. does not trap the profile in unrelated work;
6. can become a stepping stone toward USD 3k–6k/month.

---

# 23. Next file dependency

The next file should be:

```text
25_application_tracker_template.xlsx
```

This should be a real spreadsheet with sheets for:

1. Applications.
2. Companies.
3. Contacts.
4. Interviews.
5. Offers.
6. Weekly Metrics.
7. Skill Sprint.
8. Content Assets.
9. Settings / scoring definitions.

Spreadsheet generation should follow spreadsheet-specific tooling rules.

career_docs.content:
# 26_weekly_execution_dashboard

## Purpose

This document defines the weekly operating system for executing the international job-search strategy.

It explains how to use:

```text
25_application_tracker_template.xlsx
```

and how to make weekly decisions based on evidence instead of mood, anxiety, perfectionism or endless planning.

This is the final operational control layer of the system.

---

# 1. Core operating rule

The job search should now be treated as a measured pipeline.

The weekly question is not:

```text
Do I feel ready?
```

The weekly question is:

```text
What did the data show this week, and what should change next week?
```

The tracker exists to prevent:

- applying randomly;
- forgetting follow-ups;
- over-researching;
- avoiding applications;
- over-polishing the portfolio;
- chasing low-value roles;
- accepting bad offers;
- misreading silence as failure;
- making decisions without evidence.

---

# 2. Weekly review cadence

## Recommended review time

Use one fixed weekly review block:

```text
Sunday evening or Monday morning
Duration: 45–75 minutes
```

Do not review strategy every day. Daily review creates noise.

## Weekly review inputs

Before starting the review, open:

1. `25_application_tracker_template.xlsx`
2. Portfolio / TwinSight case study
3. LinkedIn profile
4. GitHub profile
5. Calendar
6. Notes from interviews or recruiter calls

## Weekly review outputs

At the end of the review, define:

- next week’s application target;
- next week’s outreach target;
- follow-ups due;
- portfolio improvements;
- interview prep focus;
- skill sprint focus;
- red flags;
- one strategic adjustment maximum.

---

# 3. Weekly dashboard workflow

## Step 1 — Update raw data

Update these sheets first:

```text
Applications
Companies
Contacts
Interviews
Offers
Weekly Metrics
Skill Sprint
Content Assets
```

Do not interpret anything until the tracker is updated.

## Step 2 — Check Dashboard

Open the `Dashboard` sheet and check:

- total applications;
- A-priority applications;
- active pipeline;
- interviews started;
- offers;
- follow-ups due;
- average application score;
- average offer score;
- applications by status;
- weekly activity.

## Step 3 — Identify bottleneck

Classify the week into one of these bottlenecks:

| Bottleneck | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Asset bottleneck | Portfolio/CV/GitHub not ready |
| Volume bottleneck | Too few applications/outreach |
| Targeting bottleneck | Applying to wrong companies |
| Positioning bottleneck | Profile not generating replies |
| Conversion bottleneck | Replies but no interviews |
| Interview bottleneck | Interviews but no progress |
| Offer bottleneck | Offers weak or risky |
| Execution bottleneck | Tracker not maintained |

## Step 4 — Choose one correction

Only choose one primary correction per week.

Examples:

- improve TwinSight case study;
- increase A-priority applications;
- rewrite recruiter opener;
- verify top 10 companies;
- practice WebGL interview questions;
- adjust salary response;
- stop applying to C-priority roles.

Do not redesign the whole system weekly.

---

# 4. Weekly metrics

## Required metrics

Track these every week:

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Applications sent | 15–30 |
| A-priority applications | 5–10 |
| Outreach messages | 10–25 |
| Follow-ups sent | 10–20 |
| Recruiter contacts | 5–15 |
| Interviews started | 0–3 |
| Technical tests | 0–2 |
| Offers | 0–1 |
| Portfolio blocks | 2–4 |
| Skill blocks | 2–4 |

## Minimum viable week

If energy or circumstances are bad, still complete:

| Action | Minimum |
|---|---:|
| Applications | 5 |
| Outreach | 5 |
| Follow-ups | 5 |
| Portfolio improvement | 1 |
| Tracker update | 1 |
| Interview prep | 1 |

A low-output week is acceptable. A zero-tracking week is not.

---

# 5. Weekly decision thresholds

## Application volume

| Result | Interpretation | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 applications | Too low | Reduce friction |
| 6–14 applications | Below target | Add scheduled blocks |
| 15–30 applications | Good | Maintain |
| 31–50 applications | High | Check quality |
| 50+ applications | Risk of low quality | Reduce volume |

## Response rate

Use a rolling 2–4 week view, not one week.

| Response rate | Interpretation |
|---:|---|
| 0–2% | Positioning or targeting problem |
| 3–5% | Weak but usable |
| 6–10% | Acceptable |
| 10%+ | Strong for cold applications |

## Interview conversion

| Signal | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Replies but no interviews | CV/portfolio mismatch |
| Interviews but rejection | Technical/interview gap |
| Tests but no progress | Test execution gap |
| Offers but weak terms | Targeting or negotiation issue |

---

# 6. Application quality system

## A-priority application checklist

Before sending an A-priority application:

- [ ] Role matches one of the main role families.
- [ ] Remote scope is plausible.
- [ ] Work authorization does not immediately block it.
- [ ] CV variant is correct.
- [ ] TwinSight link is included.
- [ ] Message references company-specific fit.
- [ ] Salary range is not obviously below target.
- [ ] Follow-up date is entered.
- [ ] Tracker row is complete.

## B-priority application checklist

- [ ] Role is adjacent but plausible.
- [ ] Correct CV variant used.
- [ ] Portfolio link included.
- [ ] Follow-up date entered.
- [ ] No major red flags.

## C-priority application checklist

- [ ] Fast application only.
- [ ] No deep customization.
- [ ] Do not spend more than 10 minutes.
- [ ] Use only if volume or cashflow requires it.

---

# 7. Weekly review questions

## Pipeline questions

Answer these every week:

1. How many A-priority applications were sent?
2. How many B-priority applications were sent?
3. Which roles produced replies?
4. Which role family produced no signal?
5. Which job boards produced useful roles?
6. Which companies need follow-up?
7. Which recruiters replied?
8. Which applications are stale?
9. Which offers or interviews require preparation?
10. Which target category should be reduced?

## Portfolio questions

1. Did TwinSight become easier to understand this week?
2. Did the demo video improve?
3. Did GitHub become cleaner?
4. Did LinkedIn become more consistent?
5. Did the portfolio gain a visible proof asset?
6. Did any improvement become perfectionism?

## Interview questions

1. Which interview question was weakest?
2. Which technical concept needs practice?
3. Can TwinSight be explained in 60 seconds?
4. Can AI-assisted development be explained cleanly?
5. Can salary expectations be stated without revealing the floor?
6. Can remote-from-Colombia status be explained accurately?

## Strategic questions

1. Is the role target still coherent?
2. Is full-stack creeping back in?
3. Is AI tooling over-dominating the profile?
4. Is 3D art over-dominating the profile?
5. Are applications matching the salary target?
6. Is the strategy moving toward USD 3k/month?
7. Is the 12–24 month path to USD 6k/month being strengthened?

---

# 8. Weekly adjustment rules

## Rule 1 — Do not pivot after one bad week

A bad week is not enough data.

Wait at least:

```text
2–4 weeks
50+ applications/outreach actions
```

before making major positioning changes.

## Rule 2 — Change one variable at a time

Do not change:

- CV;
- headline;
- role target;
- portfolio structure;
- salary range;
- outreach message;

all in the same week.

Change one or two variables, then measure.

## Rule 3 — Preserve the core identity

Every adjustment must preserve:

```text
Real-Time 3D / Unity / Technical Visualization
```

If an adjustment moves away from that, label it as fallback, not strategy.

---

# 9. Bottleneck diagnosis

## Asset bottleneck

### Symptoms

- avoiding applications because materials are not ready;
- portfolio link not shareable;
- GitHub not clean;
- no TwinSight demo;
- CV still uncertain.

### Fix

Choose one asset and finish it to usable quality.

Priority order:

1. CV.
2. LinkedIn.
3. TwinSight case study.
4. GitHub README.
5. Demo video.
6. Portfolio polish.

Do not improve all assets at once.

---

## Volume bottleneck

### Symptoms

- fewer than 10 applications per week;
- many saved jobs but few sent;
- overcustomization;
- too much research.

### Fix

Use application blocks:

```text
3 blocks/week
90 minutes each
5 applications per block
```

Target:

```text
15 applications/week minimum
```

---

## Targeting bottleneck

### Symptoms

- roles require senior-only experience;
- roles require EU/US authorization;
- roles are pure full-stack;
- roles are pure 3D art;
- roles are low-paid local jobs.

### Fix

Increase proportion of:

- Unity WebGL;
- technical visualization;
- interactive 3D;
- digital twin visualization;
- simulation interfaces;
- product visualization;
- LATAM nearshore contractor roles.

Reduce:

- generic full-stack;
- generic 3D art;
- AAA senior roles;
- EU-only local roles before authorization.

---

## Positioning bottleneck

### Symptoms

- profile views but no replies;
- recruiters misunderstand the profile;
- replies are for unrelated roles;
- people ask “what exactly do you do?”

### Fix

Tighten public wording:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
Unity WebGL
Technical Visualization
CAD-to-Realtime
TwinSight X500
Remote contractor from Colombia
```

Remove distracting emphasis from:

- full-stack;
- AI engineer;
- graphic design;
- generic multimedia;
- unfinished apps.

---

## Conversion bottleneck

### Symptoms

- replies but no interviews;
- recruiters ask for CV then disappear;
- portfolio not opened;
- no technical follow-up.

### Fix

Improve:

- first paragraph of CV;
- TwinSight case study top section;
- demo video;
- GitHub README;
- role-specific application message;
- portfolio card clarity.

---

## Interview bottleneck

### Symptoms

- interviews happen but no next stage;
- weak technical explanations;
- AI questions create discomfort;
- salary discussion feels unstable;
- WebGL/Unity questions expose gaps.

### Fix

Use:

```text
23_interview_answer_bank.md
```

Practice:

- TwinSight 60-second explanation;
- AI-assisted development answer;
- CAD-to-realtime explanation;
- WebGL performance answer;
- salary expectation response;
- contractor-from-Colombia answer.

---

## Offer bottleneck

### Symptoms

- offers too low;
- contracts vague;
- unpaid tests;
- equity-only;
- role too broad;
- full-time contractor with employee-like control.

### Fix

Use:

```text
24_offer_evaluation_scorecard.md
```

Negotiate:

- rate;
- scope;
- paid test;
- payment timing;
- IP terms;
- portfolio permission;
- review after 30/60 days.

Reject if risk remains high.

---

# 10. Weekly work blocks

## Default schedule

| Day | Primary work |
|---|---|
| Monday | Target list + applications |
| Tuesday | Outreach + contacts |
| Wednesday | Applications + interview prep |
| Thursday | Follow-ups + recruiters |
| Friday | Portfolio/GitHub improvement |
| Saturday | Skill sprint |
| Sunday | Weekly review |

## Daily minimum

On low-energy days:

```text
1 application
1 outreach message
1 tracker update
20 minutes on one asset
```

## Deep work blocks

Use 90-minute blocks for:

- portfolio case study;
- demo video editing;
- GitHub README;
- technical interview prep;
- skill sprint artifact.

Use 30-minute blocks for:

- follow-ups;
- tracker cleanup;
- recruiter replies;
- job board scanning.

---

# 11. Weekly plan template

Copy this into a weekly note.

```text
Week of: [date]

Primary goal:
[one main goal]

Targets:
- Applications:
- A-priority applications:
- Outreach:
- Follow-ups:
- Recruiter contacts:
- Portfolio blocks:
- Skill blocks:

Top target roles:
1.
2.
3.

Top target companies:
1.
2.
3.
4.
5.

Asset priority:
[CV / LinkedIn / TwinSight / GitHub / Demo / Portfolio]

Interview prep focus:
[topic]

Skill sprint:
[skill + artifact]

Main risk this week:
[risk]

Control action:
[action]

End-of-week result:
[filled during review]
```

---

# 12. Weekly review template

Use at the end of the week.

```text
Week reviewed: [date]

Metrics:
- Applications sent:
- Outreach sent:
- Follow-ups sent:
- Responses:
- Interviews:
- Tests:
- Offers:
- Rejections:
- Portfolio blocks:
- Skill blocks:

Best signal:
[what worked]

Worst signal:
[what failed]

Role family with strongest response:
[role family]

Role family with weakest response:
[role family]

Most useful job board/source:
[source]

Most useful message:
[message/template]

Main bottleneck:
[asset / volume / targeting / positioning / conversion / interview / offer / execution]

One correction for next week:
[correction]

Do not do next week:
[anti-distraction rule]

Next week target:
[measurable target]
```

---

# 13. Monthly review

Every 4 weeks, do a deeper review.

## Monthly questions

1. Which role family generated the most responses?
2. Which role family generated the best interviews?
3. Which role family generated low-quality offers?
4. Which companies were realistic?
5. Which regions were most responsive?
6. Which job boards were useful?
7. Which outreach message worked best?
8. Which portfolio asset got attention?
9. What technical gap appeared repeatedly?
10. What should be stopped?

## Monthly decision options

| Evidence | Decision |
|---|---|
| Good response from Unity WebGL | Double down |
| Good response from technical visualization | Double down |
| Only full-stack replies | Fix positioning |
| No replies from EU | Deprioritize EU until authorization |
| Low salary LATAM only | Move higher in company tiers |
| Technical interview failures | Skill sprint |
| No interviews after 100 actions | Rewrite CV/portfolio |
| Recruiters confused | Simplify headline/about |

---

# 14. 30-day gate

At day 30, verify:

- [ ] Base CV ready.
- [ ] At least one role-specific CV ready.
- [ ] LinkedIn updated.
- [ ] GitHub cleaned.
- [ ] TwinSight case study shareable.
- [ ] Portfolio MVP live or shareable.
- [ ] Tracker active.
- [ ] First applications sent.
- [ ] Outreach started.
- [ ] Demo video at least drafted.

## If not complete

Do not scale applications yet.

Extend setup by 7 days.

## If complete

Move to volume + feedback phase.

---

# 15. 60-day gate

At day 60, verify:

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Applications | 50–90 |
| Outreach actions | 40–80 |
| Recruiter conversations | 3–8 |
| Interview processes | 2–5 |
| Portfolio iterations | 4–8 |
| Skill artifacts | 2–4 |

## If no replies

Likely issue:

- targeting;
- positioning;
- CV;
- portfolio top section.

Do not assume personal failure.

## If replies but no interviews

Likely issue:

- portfolio clarity;
- role mismatch;
- weak proof link;
- CV not specific enough.

## If interviews but no offers

Likely issue:

- technical explanation;
- salary mismatch;
- AI disclosure;
- role seniority mismatch;
- interview preparation.

---

# 16. 90-day gate

At day 90, choose one:

| Path | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Continue | Interviews/offers active |
| Improve portfolio | Repeated proof gap |
| Increase volume | Low application volume |
| Refine targeting | Wrong roles replying |
| Add fallback | Cashflow pressure |
| Skill sprint | Repeated technical failures |
| Accept offer | Offer meets threshold |
| Reject/pause | Offers risky or dilutive |

## Day-90 decision rule

Use tracker evidence only.

Do not decide based on:

- one rejection;
- mood;
- comparison with other people;
- anxiety about age;
- perfectionism;
- fear of applying;
- dislike of one interview.

---

# 17. Anti-dispersion rules

## Project freeze

During the active job-search phase, do not start:

- new flagship project;
- new game;
- new app;
- new full-stack product;
- new AI system;
- new portfolio redesign;
- new course path without artifact.

## Allowed work

Allowed:

- TwinSight improvement;
- ARA README/demo cleanup;
- portfolio MVP;
- GitHub cleanup;
- demo video;
- interview prep;
- small skill artifacts;
- targeted company verification.

## Course rule

No course is allowed unless it produces one public artifact.

Examples:

| Course work | Required artifact |
|---|---|
| Unity profiling | before/after note |
| Shader Graph | small visual mode demo |
| Rebelway | FX clip or breakdown |
| German | CEFR checkpoint |
| Python automation | script/demo |
| WebGL | optimization note |

---

# 18. Response interpretation rules

## Silence

Silence usually means:

- timing;
- volume;
- mismatch;
- ATS filtering;
- hiring freeze;
- role closed;
- not enough proof;
- no referral.

It does not automatically mean the profile is invalid.

## Rejection

A rejection is useful only if categorized:

| Rejection reason | Action |
|---|---|
| Too junior | Add proof / target lower |
| Not authorized | Filter region |
| Not enough Unity | Add Unity proof |
| Not enough WebGL | Add WebGL proof |
| Not enough portfolio | Improve case study |
| Salary mismatch | Adjust target |
| Role filled | Ignore |
| No reason | Track only |

## Positive signal

A positive signal is:

- recruiter asks for CV;
- hiring manager responds;
- portfolio is opened;
- interview scheduled;
- technical question asked;
- request for demo;
- referral offered;
- compensation discussed.

Track all positive signals.

---

# 19. Tool usage recommendations

## Do not use Deep Research for

- weekly planning;
- CV tweaks;
- LinkedIn tweaks;
- outreach messages;
- interview answers;
- offer evaluation;
- portfolio copy.

## Use Deep Research only for

- legal updates;
- immigration rule changes;
- tax rule changes;
- salary benchmarking refresh;
- market shifts;
- new role-market research.

## Use mode agent only for

- live company verification;
- active job openings;
- recruiter/contact discovery;
- job board scraping-like collection;
- top-30 target validation.

## Do not use agent for

- strategy synthesis;
- personal positioning;
- CV writing;
- interview answers;
- legal interpretation.

---

# 20. Top-30 company verification prompt

Use this later with mode agent.

```text
Verify the current live hiring status for the top 30 A-priority companies in my target list.

For each company, check:
- careers URL;
- active relevant roles;
- role title;
- location;
- remote scope;
- contractor/B2B possibility if stated;
- work authorization requirement;
- required seniority;
- language;
- salary if posted;
- application URL;
- recruiter or hiring contact if publicly available;
- date checked.

Relevant roles:
Unity Developer, Unity WebGL Developer, Real-Time 3D Developer, Technical Artist, Technical Visualization Developer, Simulation Developer, Digital Twin Visualization Developer, XR Developer, Tools Developer, Python Automation Developer.

Do not write strategy.
Return tables only.
Do not infer worldwide remote unless explicitly stated.
Mark unavailable information as “not found”.
```

---

# 21. Weekly dashboard anti-patterns

Do not:

- update the tracker only when motivated;
- leave applications without follow-up dates;
- count saved jobs as applications;
- count portfolio polishing as applications;
- count course watching as skill progress without artifact;
- re-plan the whole strategy every week;
- change role positioning after one rejection;
- use low-quality volume to feel productive;
- ignore low compensation red flags;
- accept unclear contractor terms.

---

# 22. Final weekly operating statement

Every week must produce measurable movement in at least three of these areas:

1. applications;
2. outreach;
3. follow-ups;
4. portfolio/GitHub proof;
5. interviews;
6. skill artifacts;
7. offer evaluation.

If a week produces only research, planning or course consumption, it is not a productive job-search week.

---

# 23. System completion status

With this file, the strategic and operational document system is complete.

Completed blocks:

```text
00–16: research, strategy, audit and planning
17–24: application materials and decision systems
25: spreadsheet tracker
26: weekly execution dashboard
```

The remaining work is execution:

```text
1. Fill missing personal data.
2. Finalize CV.
3. Update LinkedIn.
4. Clean GitHub.
5. Publish TwinSight case study.
6. Record demo video.
7. Start applications.
8. Track weekly.
9. Adjust based on evidence.
```

---

# 24. Immediate next actions

## Next 48 hours

1. Fill contact details for CV.
2. Verify TwinSight final metrics.
3. Decide portfolio platform.
4. Choose CV variant 1.
5. Update LinkedIn headline/About.
6. Clean GitHub pins.
7. Create or update TwinSight README.
8. Add 5–8 screenshots to TwinSight materials.
9. Open the tracker and delete/replace sample rows.
10. Define the first 25 A-priority applications.

## Next 7 days

1. Publish portfolio MVP or shareable TwinSight case study.
2. Export base CV PDF.
3. Export first role-specific CV PDF.
4. Record raw TwinSight footage.
5. Send first 10–20 applications/outreach messages.
6. Track every action.
7. Run first weekly review.

---

# 25. Final rule

The roadmap is now safe enough to execute.

Do not keep expanding the research before producing public assets.

The next bottleneck is not information.

The next bottleneck is publication and outbound action.
