career_docs.content:
# 27_strategy_scenarios_conservative_balanced_aggressive

## Purpose

This file defines three execution scenarios for the international job-search roadmap:

1. **Conservative**
2. **Balanced**
3. **Aggressive**

The goal is to decide how much risk, volume, salary ambition, contractor exposure, portfolio pressure, and international targeting should be used during the next 3–6 months.

This document does not replace the main strategy. It turns it into selectable operating modes.

---

# 1. Baseline profile

## Current state

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Location | Colombia |
| Main target | Remote international work |
| Preferred model | Contractor / B2B |
| Thesis | Complete, pending defense |
| Flagship project | TwinSight X500 |
| Formal industry experience | Limited in Unity / Technical Art |
| Main strength | Strong project evidence |
| Main weakness | Limited packaged public proof |
| Current EU work authorization | No |
| Future EU route | Portuguese passport expected |
| Germany route | Possible through marriage/residence |
| Immediate income target | USD 1.5k+/month |
| 6-month target | USD 3k/month |
| 12–24 month target | USD 6k/month |

## Fixed positioning across all scenarios

All scenarios preserve the same core identity:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
```

The scenarios change execution intensity, not professional identity.

---

# 2. Strategic scenario overview

| Scenario | Risk | Speed | Income upside | Stability | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Conservative | Low | Slow-medium | Low-medium | High | Stability and first remote role |
| Balanced | Medium | Medium-fast | Medium-high | Medium | Best default strategy |
| Aggressive | High | Fast | High | Low-medium | High-value international contracts |

## Recommended default

The recommended route is:

```text
Balanced strategy with aggressive targeting for A-priority roles and conservative controls for contract risk.
```

This means:

- apply aggressively to high-fit international roles;
- negotiate carefully;
- do not accept unsafe contracts;
- keep fallback options controlled;
- do not dilute the profile.

---

# 3. Conservative strategy

## Definition

The conservative strategy prioritizes stability, lower risk, realistic first employment, and controlled skill growth.

It aims to secure a first relevant role without overexposing the candidate to risky contractor structures, high-pressure international interviews, or overly senior roles.

## Best use case

Use conservative mode if:

- cashflow pressure becomes high;
- portfolio is still incomplete;
- interviews reveal technical gaps;
- confidence in English interviews is low;
- legal/admin contractor setup is not ready;
- there is strong need for stable routine;
- thesis defense or graduation tasks still consume time.

## Primary target roles

| Priority | Role |
|---|---|
| 1 | Unity Developer, junior/early-mid |
| 2 | Interactive 3D Developer |
| 3 | Technical Visualization Developer, junior |
| 4 | Unity WebGL Developer, small team |
| 5 | Python automation role, secondary |
| 6 | Local/LATAM software role, fallback |

## Target markets

| Market | Priority |
|---|---|
| Colombia remote/hybrid | Medium |
| LATAM nearshore | High |
| US small remote companies | Medium |
| Global contractor platforms | Medium |
| EU local roles | Low until EU authorization |
| Germany local roles | Low until legal route active |
| AAA games | Low |
| Large digital twin enterprise | Watchlist |

## Salary target

| Timeframe | Target |
|---|---:|
| First 3 months | USD 1.5k–2.5k/month |
| 3–6 months | USD 2k–3k/month |
| 12 months | USD 3k–4k/month |

## Application volume

| Action | Weekly target |
|---|---:|
| Applications | 10–20 |
| A-priority applications | 3–6 |
| Outreach | 5–10 |
| Recruiter contacts | 5–10 |
| Follow-ups | 5–10 |
| Portfolio blocks | 2–3 |
| Skill blocks | 2–4 |

## Portfolio standard

Minimum required:

- base CV;
- LinkedIn updated;
- TwinSight case study draft;
- GitHub cleaned enough;
- 5–8 screenshots;
- no major public contradictions.

Demo video can be draft-quality.

## Contractor stance

Conservative mode prefers:

- clear written contracts;
- monthly retainer;
- stable payment terms;
- LATAM-friendly clients;
- smaller but safer roles;
- shorter commitments.

Avoid:

- unpaid tests;
- equity-only;
- payment-after-client-approval;
- ambiguous offshore contracts;
- broad IP/exclusivity clauses.

## Advantages

- Lower probability of severe contract/payment problems.
- Easier first win.
- Less interview pressure.
- More room to continue improving portfolio.
- Lower risk of burnout.

## Disadvantages

- Slower compensation growth.
- Higher chance of accepting roles below long-term potential.
- More risk of drifting into generic software/web work.
- Less exposure to high-value US/EU opportunities.

## Conservative red lines

Reject if:

- below USD 1.5k/month unless survival requires it;
- role is unrelated and consumes full-time capacity;
- no written contract;
- no portfolio value;
- broad non-compete;
- payment risk high.

## Conservative success definition

Success after 90 days:

```text
A stable role or active pipeline around USD 1.5k–3k/month that preserves the Unity / real-time 3D / technical visualization direction.
```

---

# 4. Balanced strategy

## Definition

The balanced strategy combines realistic application volume, strong portfolio positioning, international contractor targeting, and risk control.

It aims to reach the USD 3k/month target within 3–6 months while building toward higher-value roles over 12–24 months.

## Best use case

Use balanced mode if:

- TwinSight case study is publishable;
- LinkedIn/CV/GitHub are coherent;
- English interviews are viable;
- contractor setup can be completed;
- there is no immediate survival-level cashflow pressure;
- the goal is better compensation without reckless risk.

## Primary target roles

| Priority | Role |
|---|---|
| 1 | Real-Time 3D / Interactive 3D Developer |
| 2 | Unity WebGL Developer |
| 3 | Technical Visualization Developer |
| 4 | Digital Twin / Simulation Visualization Developer |
| 5 | Unity Technical Artist |
| 6 | XR / AR / VR Developer |
| 7 | Tools / Python Automation Developer |

## Target markets

| Market | Priority |
|---|---|
| LATAM nearshore | High |
| US remote contractor | High |
| Global remote studios | High |
| WebGL / creative tech agencies | High |
| Technical visualization companies | High |
| Product visualization/configurator companies | High |
| EU remote-friendly companies | Medium |
| Germany/Portugal | Medium future |
| Colombia local | Fallback |
| AAA games | Selective only |

## Salary target

| Timeframe | Target |
|---|---:|
| First 3 months | USD 2k–3k/month |
| 3–6 months | USD 3k–4.5k/month |
| 12–24 months | USD 4.5k–6k+/month |

## Application volume

| Action | Weekly target |
|---|---:|
| Applications | 15–30 |
| A-priority applications | 5–10 |
| Outreach | 10–25 |
| Recruiter contacts | 10–15 |
| Follow-ups | 10–20 |
| Portfolio blocks | 2–4 |
| Skill blocks | 2–4 |

## Portfolio standard

Required:

- polished CV;
- LinkedIn fully updated;
- TwinSight case study public or shareable;
- GitHub cleaned;
- TwinSight README usable;
- 8–12 screenshots;
- 60–90 second demo video or strong draft;
- ARA positioned correctly;
- Blender portrait included only if polished.

## Contractor stance

Balanced mode accepts contractor work if:

- compensation is above minimum;
- payment terms are clear;
- scope is defined;
- IP is limited to paid work;
- remote from Colombia is acknowledged;
- no illegal work authorization assumptions;
- gross-to-net estimate works.

## Advantages

- Best balance of upside and realism.
- Keeps the profile focused.
- Builds market feedback quickly.
- Increases chance of USD 3k/month.
- Preserves 12–24 month growth path.

## Disadvantages

- Requires consistent execution.
- Requires more outreach and rejection tolerance.
- Requires contractor admin readiness.
- Requires stronger interview preparation.

## Balanced red lines

Reject if:

- role is full-stack-only with no 3D/Unity relevance;
- compensation below USD 1.5k/month;
- unpaid production test;
- vague contractor terms;
- company cannot clarify remote/legal structure;
- role consumes full-time capacity while damaging positioning.

## Balanced success definition

Success after 90 days:

```text
A live pipeline of interviews and/or offers in Unity, real-time 3D, technical visualization or WebGL roles, with realistic compensation moving toward USD 3k/month.
```

---

# 5. Aggressive strategy

## Definition

The aggressive strategy prioritizes high-upside international opportunities, direct outreach, speculative applications, contractor positioning, and higher salary negotiation.

It assumes more rejection, more competition, and higher contract risk.

## Best use case

Use aggressive mode if:

- TwinSight case study is strong;
- demo video is polished;
- GitHub and LinkedIn are clean;
- interview answers are rehearsed;
- contractor/tax setup is ready;
- cashflow pressure is manageable;
- the candidate can tolerate rejection and uncertainty;
- target is USD 4k–6k+/month as soon as possible.

## Primary target roles

| Priority | Role |
|---|---|
| 1 | Technical Visualization / Digital Twin Developer |
| 2 | Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer |
| 3 | Real-Time 3D Developer |
| 4 | Unity Technical Artist — optimization/tools/runtime |
| 5 | XR / Simulation Developer |
| 6 | Product Visualization / Configurator Developer |
| 7 | Python Automation / AI Tools Developer, secondary |

## Target markets

| Market | Priority |
|---|---|
| US remote contractor | Very high |
| Global remote-first companies | Very high |
| Technical visualization firms | Very high |
| Digital twin / simulation companies | Very high |
| XR/AR/VR companies | High |
| Creative technology agencies | High |
| Product visualization/configurator | High |
| EU companies open to contractors | Medium |
| Germany/Portugal future targets | Medium |
| LATAM nearshore | Medium |
| Colombia local | Low |

## Salary target

| Timeframe | Target |
|---|---:|
| First 3 months | USD 3k–5k/month |
| 3–6 months | USD 4k–6k/month |
| 12–24 months | USD 6k+/month |

## Application volume

| Action | Weekly target |
|---|---:|
| Applications | 30–50 |
| A-priority applications | 10–20 |
| Direct outreach | 25–50 |
| Recruiter contacts | 15–30 |
| Follow-ups | 20–40 |
| Speculative applications | 10–20 |
| Portfolio/content posts | 2–3 |
| Technical interview practice | 4–6 blocks |

## Portfolio standard

Required before aggressive mode:

- polished TwinSight case study;
- polished demo video;
- strong GitHub README;
- portfolio MVP live;
- LinkedIn Featured configured;
- CV variants ready;
- interview answer bank rehearsed;
- offer scorecard ready;
- contractor setup in progress;
- top 30 companies verified.

## Contractor stance

Aggressive mode actively targets:

- higher monthly retainers;
- USD hourly rates;
- specialized project contracts;
- US/EU clients;
- remote-first companies;
- studios needing Unity/WebGL/interactive 3D;
- technical visualization contracts.

It also requires stricter risk control.

## Advantages

- Highest income upside.
- More exposure to strong companies.
- Faster market feedback.
- Better chance of reaching USD 3k–6k/month.
- Stronger professional positioning if successful.

## Disadvantages

- More rejection.
- More unpaid-test attempts.
- More legal/contract complexity.
- More senior-role mismatch.
- Higher emotional load.
- Greater chance of wasting effort if portfolio is not ready.

## Aggressive red lines

Reject or pause if:

- no contract;
- no clear payment terms;
- broad IP assignment;
- unpaid test over reasonable scope;
- equity-only;
- role requires false work authorization;
- company refuses to define remote structure;
- role demands senior claims you cannot defend;
- role is outside core positioning.

## Aggressive success definition

Success after 90 days:

```text
Multiple active interviews or one high-quality offer in the USD 3k–6k/month range, or strong evidence that the market responds to the Unity/WebGL technical visualization positioning.
```

---

# 6. Scenario comparison

## Strategic comparison

| Factor | Conservative | Balanced | Aggressive |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary goal | Stability | Strong fit + income growth | Maximum upside |
| Best first offer | USD 1.5k–3k | USD 2k–4.5k | USD 3k–6k |
| Application quality | Medium | High | High |
| Application volume | Low-medium | Medium | High |
| Outreach intensity | Low | Medium | High |
| Portfolio requirement | Usable | Strong | Polished |
| Risk tolerance | Low | Medium | High |
| Contractor complexity | Low | Medium | High |
| Rejection volume | Low | Medium | High |
| Profile dilution risk | Medium | Low | Medium |
| Burnout risk | Low | Medium | High |

## Market focus comparison

| Market | Conservative | Balanced | Aggressive |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colombia | Medium | Fallback | Low |
| LATAM nearshore | High | High | Medium |
| US remote | Medium | High | Very high |
| EU remote | Low-medium | Medium | Medium-high |
| Germany | Future | Future selective | Future + selective |
| Portugal | Future | Future selective | Future + selective |
| Global remote agencies | Medium | High | Very high |
| AAA games | Low | Selective | Selective |
| Digital twin | Medium | High | Very high |
| Product visualization | Medium | High | High |

---

# 7. Scenario triggers

## Switch to conservative if

- portfolio is not ready after 30 days;
- cashflow pressure increases;
- interview rejection shows strong technical gaps;
- contractor setup is not legally/admin ready;
- thesis defense demands attention;
- mental load becomes unsustainable;
- application volume collapses.

## Stay balanced if

- applications are being sent consistently;
- some recruiter responses appear;
- portfolio is improving weekly;
- technical gaps are manageable;
- salary conversations are near target;
- rejection is normal but not total silence.

## Switch to aggressive if

- TwinSight gets strong feedback;
- portfolio/demo is polished;
- recruiter response rate is above 6–10%;
- interviews are happening;
- contractor setup is clear;
- USD 3k+ conversations are plausible;
- top A-priority companies show fit.

---

# 8. Hybrid recommended strategy

## Best practical model

The optimal path is not purely conservative, balanced or aggressive.

Recommended hybrid:

```text
Balanced strategy as default.
Aggressive targeting for A-priority companies.
Conservative contract-risk controls.
```

## What this means

Use **balanced volume**:

```text
15–30 applications/week
10–25 outreach messages/week
```

Use **aggressive targeting** for:

- technical visualization companies;
- Unity WebGL roles;
- digital twin visualization;
- simulation interfaces;
- product configurators;
- XR-adjacent Unity roles;
- global remote studios.

Use **conservative rules** for:

- contract review;
- payment terms;
- legal status;
- IP ownership;
- unpaid tests;
- relocation;
- contractor setup.

## Hybrid operating statement

```text
Apply like an ambitious international contractor.
Negotiate like a risk-aware professional.
Position like a focused Unity technical visualization specialist.
```

---

# 9. Scenario-specific weekly plans

## Conservative week

| Day | Action |
|---|---|
| Monday | 3–5 applications |
| Tuesday | portfolio/GitHub improvement |
| Wednesday | 3–5 applications |
| Thursday | 5 outreach/follow-ups |
| Friday | interview prep |
| Saturday | skill sprint |
| Sunday | review |

## Balanced week

| Day | Action |
|---|---|
| Monday | 5–8 applications |
| Tuesday | 10 outreach messages |
| Wednesday | 5–8 applications + follow-ups |
| Thursday | recruiter contacts + interview prep |
| Friday | portfolio/GitHub improvement |
| Saturday | skill sprint + demo polish |
| Sunday | review + next targets |

## Aggressive week

| Day | Action |
|---|---|
| Monday | 10 applications + 10 outreach |
| Tuesday | 10 recruiter/hiring manager contacts |
| Wednesday | 10 applications + follow-ups |
| Thursday | speculative outreach + portfolio posts |
| Friday | interviews/tests + technical prep |
| Saturday | top-company verification + skill sprint |
| Sunday | metrics review + next A-target batch |

---

# 10. Scenario-specific portfolio requirements

## Conservative portfolio

Minimum:

- CV ready;
- LinkedIn coherent;
- TwinSight case study draft;
- GitHub not damaging;
- screenshots visible.

## Balanced portfolio

Minimum:

- public portfolio MVP;
- TwinSight case study ready;
- demo video draft or published;
- GitHub cleaned;
- README complete;
- ARA controlled;
- CV variants ready.

## Aggressive portfolio

Minimum:

- polished portfolio;
- polished TwinSight demo;
- strong case study;
- GitHub technical docs;
- screenshots and diagrams;
- LinkedIn Featured optimized;
- interview walkthrough ready;
- top 30 companies verified.

---

# 11. Scenario-specific salary stance

## Conservative salary stance

Use when:

- role is first relevant job;
- company is LATAM/local;
- project fit is strong but budget moderate.

Language:

```text
For remote contractor work, I’m open to discussing compensation based on scope, expected availability and contract structure. My priority is a role with strong fit in Unity, real-time 3D or technical visualization.
```

Do not anchor too high if the role is clearly lower-budget.

## Balanced salary stance

Use by default.

Language:

```text
For remote contractor work, depending on scope and expected availability, I’m generally targeting the USD 2k–4.5k/month range or an equivalent hourly rate.
```

Adjust per role.

## Aggressive salary stance

Use only for strong-fit US/EU/global roles.

Language:

```text
For a full-time remote contractor arrangement involving Unity, WebGL, technical visualization and real-time 3D systems, I would generally evaluate compensation in the USD 4k–6k/month range depending on scope, ownership and contract structure.
```

Do not use aggressive anchors for low-budget LATAM roles.

---

# 12. Scenario-specific red flags

## Conservative red flags

- low pay plus no portfolio value;
- local job consuming full-time capacity;
- unclear contract;
- unrelated responsibilities.

## Balanced red flags

- role slowly becoming generic full-stack;
- technical visualization not actually part of the work;
- compensation below USD 1.5k;
- no contractor clarity;
- excessive unpaid tests.

## Aggressive red flags

- overtargeting senior roles;
- too much rejection without feedback;
- unpaid production tasks;
- high salary but bad contract;
- US/EU authorization blockers;
- burnout from high volume.

---

# 13. Decision tree

## Start here

```text
Is the public portfolio ready enough to explain TwinSight clearly?
```

If no:

```text
Use conservative mode for 1–2 weeks.
Finish assets.
```

If yes:

```text
Use balanced mode.
```

Next question:

```text
Are recruiters/hiring managers responding after 50+ applications/outreach actions?
```

If no:

```text
Fix positioning, target list or portfolio top section.
Do not immediately switch roles.
```

If yes:

```text
Increase A-priority targeting.
```

Next question:

```text
Are salary conversations reaching USD 3k/month or higher?
```

If no:

```text
Improve target market and company tier.
Reduce low-value local applications.
```

If yes:

```text
Introduce aggressive mode for selected roles.
```

Next question:

```text
Are offers safe and strategically aligned?
```

If no:

```text
Use offer scorecard and renegotiate/reject.
```

If yes:

```text
Accept or negotiate upward.
```

---

# 14. What each scenario must not do

## Conservative must not

- become passive;
- over-focus on local low-pay roles;
- delay applications forever;
- accept unrelated work as main strategy;
- hide from international interviews.

## Balanced must not

- try to optimize every asset endlessly;
- apply to too many unrelated roles;
- ignore contractor/legal setup;
- treat USD 3k as impossible;
- delay outreach.

## Aggressive must not

- overclaim seniority;
- ignore red flags;
- accept risky contracts for higher gross;
- pretend current EU authorization exists;
- burn out through excessive volume;
- treat rejection as personal failure.

---

# 15. Recommended 90-day scenario plan

## Days 1–30

Use:

```text
Conservative setup + balanced preparation
```

Meaning:

- finish CV;
- update LinkedIn;
- publish TwinSight case study;
- clean GitHub;
- create demo;
- send initial applications;
- do not over-scale before assets exist.

## Days 31–60

Use:

```text
Balanced execution
```

Meaning:

- 15–30 applications/week;
- 10–25 outreach/week;
- A/B prioritization;
- interview prep;
- recruiter conversations;
- weekly metrics.

## Days 61–90

Use:

```text
Balanced + selective aggressive targeting
```

Meaning:

- double down on high-response role families;
- verify top A-priority companies;
- negotiate stronger;
- pursue USD 3k–6k roles selectively;
- reject weak or dilutive offers.

---

# 16. Scenario-specific KPIs

## Conservative KPIs

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Applications/week | 10–20 |
| Outreach/week | 5–10 |
| Portfolio blocks/week | 3 |
| Interviews by day 90 | 1–3 |
| Offer target | USD 1.5k–3k |

## Balanced KPIs

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Applications/week | 15–30 |
| Outreach/week | 10–25 |
| Portfolio blocks/week | 2–4 |
| Interviews by day 90 | 3–6 |
| Offer target | USD 2k–4.5k |

## Aggressive KPIs

| Metric | Target |
|---|---:|
| Applications/week | 30–50 |
| Outreach/week | 25–50 |
| Portfolio/content posts/week | 2–3 |
| Interviews by day 90 | 5–10 |
| Offer target | USD 3k–6k+ |

---

# 17. Risk controls by scenario

## Conservative controls

- avoid low-quality full-time traps;
- preserve time for portfolio;
- do not accept below minimum;
- do not drop Unity/3D direction.

## Balanced controls

- maintain tracker weekly;
- measure response rates;
- validate contractor terms;
- refine based on data;
- avoid overcustomization.

## Aggressive controls

- cap weekly hours;
- reject exploitative tests;
- keep legal claims accurate;
- maintain sleep/routine;
- review contract risk before accepting;
- use scorecard objectively.

---

# 18. Recommended scenario right now

## Current best choice

Based on the current profile and document system, the best path is:

```text
Balanced default strategy.
```

But the first 1–2 weeks should behave like:

```text
Conservative setup sprint.
```

After the portfolio, GitHub and TwinSight case study are public, shift to:

```text
Balanced execution.
```

After evidence of market response, selectively apply:

```text
Aggressive A-priority targeting.
```

## Practical sequence

```text
Week 1–2:
Conservative setup sprint

Week 3–8:
Balanced applications and outreach

Week 9–12:
Balanced execution + aggressive targeting for strongest role families
```

---

# 19. Final recommendation

Do not choose a scenario based on fear or motivation.

Choose based on readiness:

| Readiness state | Scenario |
|---|---|
| Assets incomplete | Conservative setup |
| Assets usable | Balanced |
| Assets polished + interviews active | Aggressive selected targeting |
| Cashflow pressure high | Conservative + fallback |
| Strong responses | Balanced/aggressive |
| No responses after 50+ actions | Fix positioning |
| Repeated technical failures | Skill sprint |
| Good offer | Score objectively |

## Final operating rule

```text
Use the balanced strategy as the main roadmap.
Use conservative controls to avoid bad contracts.
Use aggressive tactics only where TwinSight creates a strong match.
```

This is the safest path to move from the current profile toward:

```text
USD 1.5k/month minimum → USD 3k/month realistic target → USD 6k/month 12–24 month upside.
```

---

# 20. Integration with the tracker

Add a field to weekly review:

```text
Current scenario:
Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive / Hybrid
```

Add another field:

```text
Reason for scenario:
Assets incomplete / market response / cashflow / strong pipeline / technical gap / offer stage
```

This prevents switching modes based on emotion.

---

# 21. Immediate action

The current mode should be:

```text
Hybrid:
Conservative setup + balanced execution preparation.
```

Immediate priority:

1. finalize CV;
2. update LinkedIn;
3. clean GitHub;
4. publish TwinSight case study;
5. prepare demo video;
6. start first A/B applications;
7. track results;
8. move into balanced execution.

No additional broad research is needed before this.

# 28B_public_cv_resume_benchmark.md

## 0. Module status

```text
Module: 28B_public_cv_resume_benchmark
Task: A2_retry_public_cv_resume_benchmark
Generated: 2026-06-11
Project: Laboral / Alexander Woodcock Salomón
Purpose: Convert public CV/resume benchmark results into actionable updates for Alexander's CV strategy.
```

This module does **not** reopen the full labor-market strategy. It only audits and synthesizes the A2-Retry CV/resume benchmark.

Target positioning remains:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
focused on Unity WebGL, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and technical visualization.
```

---

## 1. Quality audit of A2-Retry

### 1.1 Result quality

The A2-Retry result is usable.

It collected **17 examples**, which satisfies the requested range of **12–20** examples. The sources include real public PDFs, personal resume pages, GitHub resume content, recruiter blind CVs, and sample resumes.

However, the source quality is mixed. The strongest examples are personal websites and public PDFs. The weakest examples are generic sample resumes and one disordered Scribd document.

### 1.2 Source-quality classification

| Class | Sources | Usefulness |
|---|---:|---|
| Strong | 11 | High |
| Medium | 5 | Partial |
| Weak | 1 | Limited |

### 1.3 Main limitation

Several examples are not exact matches for Alexander’s niche. Many are closer to game development, XR, technical art, or 3D visualization than to **Unity WebGL technical visualization** specifically.

This is acceptable for A2 because the goal is CV structure benchmarking, not job-market validation.

---

## 2. Source inventory

### 2.1 Strong examples

| Label | Source type | Role | Region | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ORLOVA-TA | Personal page | Technical Artist | Canada | High |
| MURZAK-GITHUB | GitHub README | Unity Developer | USA | High |
| DEMIRJIAN-UNITY | PDF | Unity Developer | USA | High |
| SEITZ-XR | PDF | XR Developer | USA | High |
| ARLEND-CAMB | Personal page | 3D Visualization | USA | High |
| DELARA-STA | Personal page | Senior Technical Artist | USA | High |
| TORRES-TA | Personal page | Technical Artist | USA | High |
| GARCIA-TA | Personal page | Technical Artist | Uruguay | High |
| SZALAI-GAMEDEV | PDF | Unity Expert | Not found | High |
| MAYANK-UNITY | PDF | Senior Unity Developer | India | High |
| KENKEL-ENGINEER | PDF | Lead Software Engineer | USA | High |

### 2.2 Medium examples

| Label | Source type | Role | Region | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEVSDATA-UNITY-SAMPLE | Blind CV | Unity Developer | Poland | Medium |
| HIREIT-UNITY | Resume database | Unity Developer | Not found | Medium |
| RESUMEKRAFT-UNITY-SAMPLE | Sample CV | Unity Developer | Not found | Medium |
| SPANN-GAMEDEV | PDF | Gameplay Programmer | USA | High |
| BEAUMONT-GAMEDEV | PDF | Game Developer | Canada | High |

SPANN-GAMEDEV and BEAUMONT-GAMEDEV are real public PDFs, but they are less aligned with technical visualization than the strongest examples.

### 2.3 Weak example

| Label | Source type | Role | Region | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KAISER-SIM | Scribd | 3D Simulation Developer | Argentina | Low |

KAISER-SIM is only useful as a negative formatting reference. The extracted content appears disordered and should not influence Alexander’s CV structure.

---

## 3. Source URLs

| Label | URL |
|---|---|
| ORLOVA-TA | https://tamaraorlova.com/resume |
| DEVSDATA-UNITY-SAMPLE | https://devsdata.com/resumes/unity3d/unity-developer-resume-sample/ |
| HIREIT-UNITY | https://www.hireitpeople.com/resume-database/63-net-developers-architects-resumes/200613-unity-developer-resume |
| RESUMEKRAFT-UNITY-SAMPLE | https://resumekraft.com/unity-developer-cv-sample/ |
| MURZAK-GITHUB | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IvanMurzak/IvanMurzak/main/Resume.md |
| DEMIRJIAN-UNITY | https://fortynina.github.io/portfolio/assets/documents/NinaDemirjianResumeApril23.pdf |
| SEITZ-XR | https://www.josetteseitz.com/_files/ugd/d34654_c1180d17a7364855a9a3e18f51c49398.pdf |
| KAISER-SIM | https://www.scribd.com/document/951035904/Rodrigo-L-Kaiser-Eng-Resume-Text-ATS |
| ARLEND-CAMB | https://the3drenderguy.com/resume |
| DELARA-STA | https://www.samdelara.com/resume |
| TORRES-TA | https://www.carthtorres.com/resume |
| GARCIA-TA | https://iamtheroo.com/resume |
| SZALAI-GAMEDEV | https://peterszalai.com/resumes/peter-szalai-resume.pdf |
| SPANN-GAMEDEV | https://www.noahspann.com/resume.pdf |
| MAYANK-UNITY | https://agrmayank.com/cv/Resume%20-%20Mayank%20Raj.pdf |
| BEAUMONT-GAMEDEV | https://www.jalexbeaumont.com/resume.pdf |
| KENKEL-ENGINEER | https://nonathaj.github.io/Jon%20Kenkel%20Resume.pdf |

---

## 4. Benchmark patterns

### 4.1 Strong CVs use a narrow headline

The strongest examples do not use broad titles like “creative developer” or “3D generalist” as the main positioning. They use direct role labels:

```text
Technical Artist
Senior Technical Artist
Senior Unity Developer
XR Developer
Unity Expert
3D Visualization Artist
```

Alexander should use a narrow headline, not a broad identity label.

Recommended primary headline:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
```

Alternative headline for Unity-heavy applications:

```text
Unity WebGL Developer focused on Technical Visualization
```

Alternative headline for 3D/technical art applications:

```text
Unity Technical Artist focused on CAD-to-Realtime Visualization
```

---

### 4.2 Strong CVs show proof before personality

The best examples prioritize evidence:

```text
role → project → tools → responsibility → result
```

Weak examples rely on generic traits:

```text
passionate
creative
hard-working
team player
problem solver
```

Alexander’s CV should minimize soft claims and increase visible proof.

---

### 4.3 Strong CVs expose project scale

The best CVs include scale markers such as:

```text
5 shipped titles
40,000 downloads
150k+ downloads
500k users
100+ hours saved
2,500+ assets
33 ms frame-time budget
4 GB memory budget
```

Alexander should not invent metrics. He should add measured or verifiable project metrics once the TwinSight evaluation is complete.

Usable current metrics from the thesis context:

```text
28 canonical research parts
30 scene nodes
257 technical elements
Unity WebGL target
30 FPS target = 33 ms frame-time budget
CAD-to-realtime pipeline
mobile-first interface
```

Metrics still pending:

```text
actual FPS
actual frame time
load time
memory use
SUS score
NASA-TLX Raw score
participant count
```

---

### 4.4 Strong CVs organize technical skills by function

The better examples group skills by category. They do not dump every tool into one long list.

Recommended skill grouping for Alexander:

```text
Real-time development
3D production pipeline
Technical visualization
Web deployment
Automation and tooling
Version control
```

Bad pattern to avoid:

```text
Unity, Blender, Photoshop, Python, WebGL, Substance, Git, C#, AI, UX, UI, AR, VR, etc.
```

That kind of list dilutes positioning.

---

### 4.5 Strong CVs connect portfolio and resume

The strongest examples include links to one or more of:

```text
portfolio
GitHub
project pages
PDF resume
LinkedIn
live demos
store pages
itch.io
```

Alexander’s CV should link directly to:

```text
portfolio site
TwinSight live demo
TwinSight GitHub repository
TwinSight case study
LinkedIn
ArtStation or 3D portfolio
```

The CV should not depend on the reader searching manually.

---

## 5. Recommended CV structure for Alexander

### 5.1 Primary structure

```text
1. Header
2. Role headline
3. 2–3 line professional summary
4. Core technical stack
5. Selected project: TwinSight X500
6. Additional projects
7. Technical skills
8. Education
9. Languages
10. Links
```

### 5.2 Why this structure

Alexander has limited formal industry experience in Unity/Technical Art. Therefore, the CV should be **project-led**, not employment-led.

The CV should make TwinSight function as the main proof of capability.

---

## 6. CV content recommendations

### 6.1 Header

Recommended fields:

```text
Alexander Woodcock Salomón
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
Medellín or Colombia
Email
LinkedIn
Portfolio
GitHub
```

Do not include:

```text
full street address
ID number
personal photo
marital status
birth date
unrelated social media
```

---

### 6.2 Summary

Recommended summary style:

```text
2–3 lines
specific role target
specific stack
specific proof project
no inflated seniority
```

Draft baseline:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment. Built TwinSight X500, a Unity WebGL prototype for inspecting and understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone through optimized 3D assets, technical UI, and mobile-first interaction design.
```

For a one-page CV, this can be shortened to:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on Unity WebGL, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and interactive technical visualization. Creator of TwinSight X500, a web-based 3D drone assembly inspection prototype.
```

---

### 6.3 Core technical stack

Recommended stack block:

```text
Unity | C# | WebGL | URP | UI Toolkit | Shader Graph
Blender | CAD-to-Realtime | UVs | Texture Baking | Optimization
Python | Git/GitHub | Technical Documentation | Usability Testing
```

This is stronger than a long mixed list because it mirrors the job family.

---

### 6.4 TwinSight X500 section

Recommended section title:

```text
Selected Technical Project — TwinSight X500
```

Recommended role line:

```text
Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Prototype | Thesis Project
```

Recommended bullets:

```text
- Designed and developed a Unity WebGL prototype for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone through interactive 3D visualization.
- Built a CAD-to-realtime pipeline using Blender, mesh cleanup, modular fasteners, UV preparation, texture baking, and Unity optimization.
- Structured the model into 28 canonical research parts, 30 scene nodes, and 257 technical elements for inspection and interaction.
- Designed a mobile-first interface with Unity UI Toolkit for part selection, isolation, transparency, and assembly understanding.
- Prepared technical evaluation around frame time, load time, memory use, usability, perceived workload, and qualitative feedback.
```

Do not claim final performance metrics until measured.

When measured, add one bullet like:

```text
- Achieved [X] FPS / [Y] ms frame time / [Z] MB memory use in WebGL testing on [device/browser].
```

---

### 6.5 Additional project sections

If the CV has space, add 1–2 more projects. These should reinforce the same positioning.

Useful project categories:

```text
Blender technical asset study
Unity interaction prototype
Python automation/tooling script
real-time shader or visualization experiment
WebGL deployment experiment
```

Avoid unrelated projects unless they prove technical art, Unity, or pipeline ability.

---

### 6.6 Education wording

Recommended wording:

```text
B.Eng. Multimedia Engineering — UNAD
Thesis: TwinSight X500, Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection
```

If needed:

```text
Former Electronic Engineering coursework — Universidad Nacional de Colombia
```

The UNAL background should be secondary. It can support technical credibility, but it should not distract from the current target role.

---

### 6.7 Languages

Recommended wording:

# 28D — ArtStation / Portfolio Benchmark

## 1. Corrección crítica

La versión anterior de este módulo no era válida como **ArtStation benchmark**.

El archivo A4 usado como base contenía portafolios externos, blogs técnicos y GitHub Pages, pero no una muestra real de perfiles o proyectos de ArtStation. Por tanto, cualquier conclusión presentada como patrón de ArtStation queda retirada.

Este módulo corregido separa tres cosas:

1. lo que sí sirve del intento anterior;
2. lo que no debe usarse;
3. la tarea necesaria para completar ArtStation correctamente.

- seniority explícito.

Limitación:

El home muestra más perfil que evidencia técnica. Para Alexander, esto sería insuficiente sin proyectos concretos.

Aplicación para Alexander:

Puede inspirar el texto de posicionamiento profesional:

> Multimedia engineer focused on real-time 3D visualization, Unity WebGL, technical art systems and interactive product visualization.

### 6.4 Harry Alisavakis — Technical Art Blog

URL: https://halisavakis.com/

El blog funciona como repositorio de recursos y artículos. Es útil como referencia de consistencia y marca personal.

Aporta:

- publicaciones recurrentes;
- recursos técnicos;
- enfoque educativo;
- mezcla Unity/Unreal;
- comunidad técnica.

Limitación:

Es más blog que portafolio. No todo está organizado para evaluación rápida de recruiter.

Aplicación para Alexander:

Sirve como modelo para una sección `Technical Notes` o `Breakdowns`, no como home principal.

## 7. Fuentes débiles o incompletas

### 7.1 Rakik — Boom Mike VR

URL: https://technical-art-portfolio.io.framer.ai/boom-mike

Aporta una demo VR con video, pero poca explicación técnica. Es útil como referencia mínima de presentación visual.

No debe ser modelo principal para Alexander.

### 7.2 Rakik — Shader VFX Pack

URL: https://technical-art-portfolio.io.framer.ai/shader-vfx-pack

Aporta una muestra visual de efectos, pero no explica implementación, problema, parámetros ni resultados.

Debe evitarse este patrón si el objetivo es aplicar a roles técnicos.

## 8. Patrones de estructura para el portafolio de Alexander

### 8.1 Landing page

La landing debe responder en menos de 10 segundos:

- quién es Alexander;
- qué rol busca;
- cuál es su proyecto principal;
- qué evidencia técnica puede revisar el evaluador;
- dónde están demo, GitHub, CV y contacto.

Estructura recomendada:

```text
Hero
└── Role headline
└── One-line positioning
└── CTA: View TwinSight X500
└── CTA: GitHub
└── CTA: Download CV

Featured Case Study
└── TwinSight X500
└── Unity WebGL technical viewer
└── Demo / GitHub / Breakdown

Project Categories
└── Technical Visualization
└── Unity WebGL
└── Shaders & View Modes
└── Tools & Pipeline
└── 3D Assets
└── Technical Notes
```

### 8.2 Project card

Cada tarjeta de proyecto debe mostrar:

- nombre;
- rol;
- tecnología;
- tipo de problema;
- resultado visible;
- enlace a demo;
- enlace a breakdown;
- enlace a código si aplica.

Formato sugerido:

```markdown
## TwinSight X500

**Role:** Unity WebGL Developer / Technical Artist  
**Type:** Browser-based 3D technical visualization  
**Tools:** Unity 6000, Blender, WebGL, URP, GitHub Pages  
**Focus:** Spatial inspection, part selection, exploded view, cross-section, heuristic thermal reading  
**Demo:** [link]  
**Code:** [link]  
**Case Study:** [link]
```

### 8.3 Case study técnico

La estructura debe tomar como referencia Jettelly y Julhe.

Plantilla:

```markdown
# Project name

## Context
What problem existed?

## Goal
What the system needed to solve.

## Constraints
Browser, mobile, WebGL, asset size, usability, academic scope.

## Results
Screenshots, video, metrics, validation.

## What I learned

## Links
Demo, GitHub, report, video.
```

## 9. Qué debe adaptar Alexander

### 9.1 De Jettelly

Adaptar:

- breakdown visual paso a paso;
- explicación de comportamiento dinámico;
- uso de imágenes y video;
- foco en Unity.

Aplicar a:

- thermal heuristic view;
- X-Ray mode;
- cross-section shader;
- exploded view;
- selection highlighting.

### 9.2 De Julhe

Adaptar:

- profundidad técnica;
- explicación de problema;

- análisis de rendimiento.

Aplicar a:

### 9.3 De Francisco Múrias

Adaptar:

- grilla de proyectos;
- estética técnica;
- tarjetas visuales;
- enlaces a GitHub;
- separación por tipo de trabajo.

Aplicar a:

- technical demos;

### 9.4 De Wolf van Veen

Adaptar:

- categorías claras;

Aplicar a:

### 9.5 De Omar Rinaz

Adaptar:

- timeline de experiencia;
- formación académica;
- lista de roles;
- sección CV.

Aplicar a:

- About;
- CV page;
- career context.

## 10. Qué no debe copiar Alexander

Evitar:

- portafolios con solo imágenes;
- proyectos sin contexto;
- ausencia de métricas;
- falta de enlaces a demo;
- listas largas de software sin evidencia;
- describirse como senior sin respaldo;
- claims no verificables;
- usar ArtStation como única superficie;
- esconder el GitHub;
- omitir decisiones técnicas.

## 11. Recomendaciones concretas para el portafolio

### 11.1 Proyecto principal

TwinSight X500 debe ser el proyecto hero.

Título recomendado:

```text
TwinSight X500 — Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Viewer
```

Subtítulo recomendado:

```text
Browser-based interactive 3D viewer for inspecting the Holybro X500 V2 drone assembly, focused on spatial understanding, part hierarchy, exploded view, cross-section and heuristic visual analysis.
```

### 11.2 Categorías

Usar estas categorías:

```text
Technical Visualization
Unity WebGL
Shaders & View Modes
Tools & Pipeline
3D Production
Academic Research
Technical Notes
```

### 11.3 Case studies mínimos

Publicar al menos 4 piezas:

```text
1. TwinSight X500 — full case study
2. Cross-section shader / clipping plane
3. Drone CAD-to-Web pipeline
4. WebGL optimization / mobile constraints
```

Deseables:

```text
5. Fastener modular system
6. Exploded view logic
7. UI bottom-sheet interaction system
8. Heuristic thermal visualization
```

### 11.4 Medios visuales

Incluir:

- hero video corto;
- GIF de selección de piezas;
- GIF de exploded view;
- GIF de cross-section;
- capturas before/after;
- diagrama de pipeline;
- diagrama de arquitectura;
- tabla de métricas;
- enlace a demo.

### 11.5 Métricas

Agregar cuando sean verificables:

```text
FPS
frame time
build size
load time
memory
draw calls
triangles
texture memory
SUS
NASA-TLX Raw
task completion
```

No inventar métricas. Si no están medidas, marcar como pendiente.

## 12. Cambios concretos para módulos previos

### 12.1 Actualizar `17_cv_base_and_role_variants.md`

Agregar una sección de proyectos técnicos con enfoque medible:

```markdown
### Featured Technical Project

**TwinSight X500 — Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Viewer**  
Built an interactive browser-based 3D viewer for inspecting the Holybro X500 V2 drone assembly. Implemented part hierarchy, selection, exploded view, cross-section and visual analysis modes for technical study and usability evaluation.
```

Cuando existan métricas finales, añadir:

```markdown
Measured WebGL performance across load time, frame time and memory usage.
```

### 12.2 Actualizar README del repositorio

El README ya está bien orientado, pero puede mejorar como portafolio técnico si añade:

- GIF hero;
- project architecture diagram;
- pipeline diagram;
- screenshots table;
- direct link to case study;
- measured performance section;
- “What I built” section.

### 12.3 Actualizar landing de GitHub Pages

La landing debe priorizar:

1. Demo inmediata.
2. Caso de estudio.
3. Capturas del flujo.
4. Métricas verificadas.
5. Enlaces a manuales.
6. CV/portfolio.

## 13. Estructura recomendada del sitio personal

```text
/
├── Home
├── Projects
│   ├── TwinSight X500
│   ├── Cross-section Shader
│   ├── CAD-to-Web Pipeline
│   └── WebGL Optimization Notes
├── Technical Notes
│   ├── Unity WebGL constraints
│   ├── Shader view modes
│   └── 3D model optimization
├── About
├── CV
└── Contact
```

## 14. Taxonomía de proyectos

| Categoría | Uso |
|---|---|
| Technical Visualization | TwinSight, drone viewer |
| Unity WebGL | Browser deployment |
| Shaders | X-Ray, thermal, clipping |
| Tools | pipeline utilities |
| 3D Production | Blender, bake, optimization |
| Research | thesis validation |
| Notes | technical articles |

## 15. Plantilla para página de proyecto

```markdown
---
title: TwinSight X500
role: Unity WebGL Developer / Technical Artist
tools: Unity, Blender, WebGL, URP
status: public demo
year: 2026
---

# TwinSight X500

## Summary

TwinSight X500 is a browser-based interactive 3D viewer for technical inspection of the Holybro X500 V2 drone assembly.

## Problem

Traditional 2D manuals force users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between parts.

## Solution

The project provides an interactive 3D environment with selection, part hierarchy, exploded view, cross-section and visual analysis modes.

## My Role

I designed and implemented the Unity WebGL prototype, prepared the 3D asset pipeline and developed the interaction systems used in the final thesis demo.

## Technical Stack

- Unity 6000
- WebGL
- URP
- Blender
- GitHub Pages
- C#

## Key Systems

- App state machine
- Part selection
- Bottom-sheet UI
- Exploded view
- Cross-section
- View modes
- Thermal heuristic visualization

## Constraints

- Browser deployment
- Mobile-first interaction
- Academic validation scope
- Complex imported hierarchy
- Performance constraints

## Results

Add measured metrics here when available.

## Media

Add GIFs, screenshots and video.

## Links

- Demo
- GitHub
- Report
- Technical manual
```

## 16. Plantilla para breakdown técnico

```markdown
# Cross-section shader breakdown

## What I wanted to solve

Users needed to inspect internal spatial relationships without losing context of the full drone assembly.

## Constraint

The solution had to work in Unity WebGL and remain usable on mobile devices.

## Approach

I implemented a shader-based clipping plane controlled through the Analyze mode UI.

## Implementation

Explain the clipping logic, material setup, UI control and limitations.

## Result

Show GIF, screenshots and performance notes.

## Lessons

Explain what worked, what failed and what would be improved.
```

## 17. Riesgos

| Riesgo | Mitigación |
|---|---|
| Portafolio solo visual | Añadir breakdowns |
| Claims sin evidencia | Medir antes de publicar |
| GitHub oculto | Enlace visible |
| Proyecto académico percibido como menor | Enfatizar alcance técnico |
| Falta de seniority | Posicionarse como junior/mid técnico |
| Demasiado texto | Usar jerarquía visual |
| Falta de demo | Priorizar build estable |

## 18. Orden operativo recomendado

```text
1. Congelar demo pública.
2. Capturar GIFs clave.
3. Medir rendimiento verificable.
4. Crear case study principal.
5. Crear 2–3 breakdowns técnicos.
6. Actualizar README.
7. Construir landing personal.
8. Ajustar CV.
9. Publicar LinkedIn/GitHub profile.
```

## 19. Prompt para A5

```text
Execute A5_case_study_benchmark.

Objective:
Analyze 3–5 strong accessible technical case studies relevant to Alexander’s positioning:
Unity Technical Artist, Real-Time 3D Developer, Unity WebGL Developer, Technical Visualization Developer, Shader/Tools Developer.

Prioritize:
- Jettelly Real-Time Potion Shader Breakdown;
- Julhe shader breakdowns;
- Francisco Múrias technical projects;
- other accessible technical art breakdowns with code, images, video or metrics.

Output:
- source inventory;
- case study structure;
- storytelling pattern;
- technical depth;
- visual evidence;
- metrics used;
- what Alexander should adapt;
- project page template;
- breakdown article template.

Rules:
- Use public accessible sources only.
- Do not use ArtStation if blocked.
- Do not invent missing data.
- Keep tables concise.
- Provide actionable recommendations.
```

## 20. Conclusión

El benchmark actualizado muestra que el portafolio de Alexander no debe depender de una galería tipo ArtStation. Su ventaja competitiva está en combinar:

- evidencia visual;
- explicación técnica;
- demo WebGL;
- código público;
- métricas verificables;
- claridad de rol;
- estudios de caso.

La prioridad debe ser construir un portafolio híbrido: visual como un artista técnico, documentado como un desarrollador, y medible como un proyecto de ingeniería.

# 28E — ArtStation Profile Optimization Strategy

## 0. Module status

```text
Module: 28E_artstation_profile_optimization_strategy.md
Status: Complete v1
Input: Perplexity Deep Research output + 01_source_of_truth_profile.md
Purpose: Strategy and copy-pasteable texts for optimizing Alexander Woodcock Salomón's ArtStation profile setup
Date: 2026-07-01
```

---

## 1. Profile Section

### Professional headline (3–5 options)

1. `Unity Technical Artist | Real-Time 3D Developer for CAD-to-WebGL Visualization`
2. `Technical Artist (Unity WebGL) | CAD-to-Realtime & Industrial Simulation`
3. `Real-Time 3D Developer | Unity WebGL Technical Visualization & CAD Optimization`
4. `Unity Technical Artist | Interactive 3D UI & CAD Asset Optimization`
5. `Technical Artist | Real-Time Drone & Industrial Visualization in Unity WebGL`

---

## 2. Resume Section

### Professional summary (English)

> I am a Multimedia Engineering student with advanced coursework in Electronic Engineering, specializing in Unity-based real-time 3D visualization and CAD-to-WebGL optimization. My flagship project, TwinSight X500, is an interactive Unity WebGL prototype that visualizes the Holybro X500 V2 drone for assembly inspection, combining technical UI, exploded views, and cross-section tools to help users understand spatial relationships between components. In this project I optimized CAD-derived geometry from 6.5M+ triangles down to 95,617 triangles for web deployment and evaluated usability with SUS and NASA-TLX, demonstrating both engineering rigor and practical performance tuning. I am focused on technical art, interaction design, and tool-building for real-time visualization, looking for roles where Unity, Blender, and CAD pipelines intersect with games, industrial simulation, and interactive training.

### Skills list (text block)

> Technical Art (Unity)  
> Real-Time 3D Development  
> CAD-to-Realtime Optimization  
> Unity WebGL Deployment  
> Mesh Decimation & Retopology  
> Hard-Surface Modeling (Blender)  
> UV Mapping & Baking  
> Shader Graph & Basic Shader Development  
> Technical UI / Interaction Design (UI Toolkit)  
> Exploded Views & Cross-Section Visualization  
> Pipeline Design & Asset Preparation  
> Performance Profiling (WebGL / URP)  
> Usability & UX Evaluation (SUS, NASA-TLX)  

### Software expertise (levels + stack)

> **Advanced**  
> Unity (URP, WebGL, C#, UI Toolkit, Shader Graph)  
> Blender (hard-surface modeling, UVs, CAD cleanup & optimization)  
>  
> **Intermediate**  
> Substance 3D Painter (PBR texturing for assets)  
> Photoshop (texture tweaks, UI elements, presentation boards)  
> Marmoset Toolbag (material lookdev, realtime rendering)  
>  
> **Foundational / In progress**  
> Python (tooling / research automation prototypes)  
> LangGraph / LangChain (multi-agent research tooling)  
> Web stack basics (for WebGL deployment context and integration)  

### Production experience entry for TwinSight X500

> **TwinSight X500 — Interactive Drone Visualization (Unity WebGL Thesis Project)**  
> Role: Unity Technical Artist / Real-Time 3D Developer  
> Tools: Unity (URP, WebGL, C#, UI Toolkit, Shader Graph), Blender, CAD/STEP pipeline, SUS & NASA-TLX evaluation tools  
>  
> Key Contributions:  
> - Developed an interactive Unity WebGL prototype for Holybro X500 V2 drone assembly inspection, with component selection, exploded views, and cross-section/clipping tools.  
> - Optimized CAD-derived geometry from 6.5M+ triangles to 95,617 triangles for real-time web deployment, maintaining visual fidelity while reducing load times and draw calls.  
> - Designed technical UI panels for part metadata, inspection modes, and interaction workflows oriented to engineering users.  
> - Conducted usability tests with 12 participants using SUS and NASA-TLX; achieved SUS 91.88 and reduced NASA-TLX raw workload from 19.89 to 8.69 across sessions.  

### Professional experience templates (coursework & thesis as experience)

> **Multimedia Engineering — Universidad Nacional Abierta y a Distancia (UNAD)**  
> Focus: Real-Time 3D visualization, interactive multimedia, Unity-based technical UI.  
> Highlight: Thesis project “TwinSight X500”, an interactive Unity WebGL visualization for drone assembly inspection integrating CAD-to-realtime optimization, technical UI, and usability evaluation.  
> Status: Thesis completed, pending defense.  
>  
> **Electronic Engineering (Advanced Coursework) — Universidad Nacional de Colombia (UNAL)**  
> Description: Completed approximately 8 semesters (~80% of the curriculum) of Electronic Engineering, building a strong foundation in analytical problem solving, technical documentation, and engineering workflows that support real-time visualization and simulation projects.  
> International wording: “Completed advanced coursework in Electronic Engineering — Universidad Nacional de Colombia” (without claiming the degree).  

---

## 3. Job Preferences Section

### Industry (top 5 to check)

- **Games** – Primary industry for Technical Artists and Unity generalists.
- **Software Development** – Covers interactive tools, WebGL visualizers, and simulation dashboards.
- **AR/VR** – Directly related to real-time 3D, technical visualization, and digital twin-like experiences.
- **Asset creation** – Signals optimization of assets from CAD/STEP into game/real-time meshes.
- **Product Design** – Relevant for industrial visualization, drone/robotics, and hardware UX.

### Medium

- **Real time** – Core medium; Unity/WebGL and interactive technical UI.
- **Digital 3D** – Reflects asset work, Blender modeling, and CAD conversions.

### Tags (strategic recruiter-facing tags)

- Technical Art  
- Pipeline  
- Hard Surface  
- Props and assets  
- Vehicles (for drone / industrial hardware visualization)  
- Environment Design  
- Rendering  
- Lighting Art  
- UI/UX  
- ArchViz  
- Generalist  

### Software (checkboxes)

- Blender  
- Unity  
- Substance 3D Painter  
- Photoshop  
- Marmoset Toolbag  

---

## 4. Locations & Notifications

### Location & remote availability phrasing

- Location field: `Pasto, Nariño, Colombia (UTC-5)`
- About Section remote phrasing:
  > Based in Colombia (UTC-5), open to fully remote or contractor roles worldwide, with overlapping hours for US and European teams.

### Job Digest notifications

- Set **Job Digest** to **Weekly** to avoid fatigue and maintain focus.

---

## 5. Social and Freelance Profiles

### Social profiles (LinkedIn, GitHub, personal portfolio)

- **LinkedIn** – Link once it matches the ArtStation summary and headline.
- **GitHub** – Link after cleaning up the TwinSight repo and adding prototype disclaimers.
- **Personal portfolio site** – Link once first 1 or 2 case studies are fully written.

### Freelance profiles

- Prioritize **ArtStation Jobs, LinkedIn applications, and direct outreach** to studios and companies in games, AR/VR, and industrial visualization.
- Only build **freelance marketplace profiles (Upwork/Fiverr)** later if defining a very specific niche to avoid diluting positioning.

---

## 6. NoAI Tagging & Visibility Strategy

### How ArtStation’s NoAI tag works

ArtStation’s native **"NoAI"** checkbox adds a metadata signal and policy flag prohibiting collection, aggregation, mining, or scraping of content for testing, inputting, or integrating with AI. Epic Games does not use ArtStation content for generative AI training, and the NoAI tag provides an explicit opt-in protection layer.

### Visibility vs. protection (impact on search ranking)

There is **no documented evidence** that enabling “NoAI” or using “#NoAI” in descriptions reduces your ranking in ArtStation’s internal search, job matching, or recruiter filters. Discoverability still depends on presentation quality, correct tags, and portfolio strength.

### Tagging protocol for TwinSight X500 & Blender portrait

- Enable ArtStation’s native **“NoAI”** option on both TwinSight X500 and the Blender portrait projects.
- **TwinSight X500 tags & description:**
  - Hashtags: `#NoAI`, `#NoAIArt`, `#Unity`, `#WebGL`, `#TechnicalArt`, `#CADOptimization`.
  - Short disclaimer line in description:
    > Content and technical breakdowns protected by ArtStation’s NoAI policy. Not licensed for AI training or dataset scraping.
- **Blender Portrait tags & description:**
  - Hashtags: `#NoAI`, `#NoAIArt`, `#Blender`, `#3DArt`, `#CharacterArt`, `#TechnicalArt`.
  - Short disclaimer line in description:
    > Content and technical breakdowns protected by ArtStation’s NoAI policy. Not licensed for AI training or dataset scraping.

career_docs.content:
# 28_competitor_profile_benchmark

## Scope

This module integrates the result of:

```text
A1_linkedin_profiles_benchmark
```

The source data was collected from publicly visible search snippets and LinkedIn-result metadata. LinkedIn profile pages were not fully accessible without login, so this benchmark must be treated as a **surface-level positioning benchmark**, not as a complete profile audit.

## Data limitations

| Limitation | Impact |
|---|---|
| LinkedIn profile pages restricted | About, full experience, education and featured projects are often unavailable |
| Search snippets only | Data is incomplete and may omit important context |
| Most portfolio links not visible | Cannot judge project quality directly |
| Seniority often inferred from title | Confidence varies |
| Remote/contractor status rarely visible | Must not assume remote eligibility |
| Search result snippets may change | Recheck important profiles manually before copying patterns |

## Correct use

Use this module to extract:

- headline patterns;
- role title patterns;
- market vocabulary;
- seniority patterns;
- niche clusters;
- signals to copy carefully;
- signals to avoid;
- profile gaps in Alexander’s current positioning.

Do **not** use it to claim direct equivalence with senior profiles.

---

# 1. Executive findings

## Main finding

The public profile landscape confirms that Alexander’s positioning is coherent if expressed as:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
```

with strong supporting keywords:

```text
Unity · C# · Unity WebGL · Technical Visualization · CAD-to-Realtime · Blender · Interactive 3D · Simulation · XR · Digital Twin
```

The strongest comparable profiles tend to cluster around one of five families:

1. **Unity Technical Artist**
2. **Real-Time 3D / Interactive 3D Developer**
3. **Unity WebGL Developer**
4. **XR / Simulation / Digital Twin Developer**
5. **Unity Tools / Pipeline Developer**

## Key implication

Alexander should not market himself as a generic Unity developer. The benchmark shows that more differentiated profiles combine Unity with a domain:

```text
Unity + Technical Art
Unity + WebGL
Unity + XR
Unity + Simulation
Unity + Digital Twin
Unity + Tools
Unity + Optimization
```

TwinSight gives a stronger niche than generic gameplay.

## Strongest benchmark cluster for Alexander

| Cluster | Fit |
|---|---|
| Real-Time 3D Developer | Very high |
| Unity WebGL Developer | Very high |
| Technical Visualization / Digital Twin Developer | Very high |
| Unity Technical Artist | High |
| XR / Simulation Developer | Medium-high |
| Tools / Pipeline Developer | Medium |
| Pure game Technical Artist | Medium |
| Pure 3D Generalist | Low unless technical |

---

# 2. Headline pattern extraction

## Strong headline formulas found

| Formula | Example pattern | Usefulness |
|---|---|---|
| Role + engine + domain | Real-Time 3D Developer \| Unity & Unreal | High |
| Role + specialization | Unity Technical Artist \| VFX & Shader Specialist | High |
| Role + platform | Unity WebGL Developer | High |
| Role + industry | Unity Developer \| Digital Twin Applications | High |
| Role + stack | XR Developer \| Unity · VR · AR | Medium-high |
| Seniority + role | Senior Unity Developer / Technical Artist | Use only if true |
| Multi-engine profile | Unreal & Unity Technical Artist | Useful only if both defensible |
| Freelance + role | Freelance Real-Time 3D Developer | Useful for contractor route |

## Recommended adaptation for Alexander

Best formula:

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist | Unity WebGL, C#, CAD-to-Realtime Optimization, Technical Visualization
```

Alternative for specific markets:

```text
Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer | Technical Visualization, C#, Blender, CAD-to-Realtime
```

Alternative for digital twin / simulation:

```text
Technical Visualization Developer | Unity WebGL, CAD-to-Realtime, Interactive 3D
```

---

# 3. Role family benchmark

## Unity Technical Artist

### Observed patterns

Profiles in this cluster commonly emphasize:

- Unity;
- shaders;
- VFX;
- optimization;
- technical art;
- pipeline;
- performance;
- VR/AR;
- game studio or mobile game experience.

### Relevant examples from public snippets

| Name | Region | Title / Signal | Seniority | Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rachel Tal | Israel | Unity Technical Artist / FX Artist | Unknown | Unity + FX/TA positioning |
| Aldo Vazquez | Mexico | Unity Technical Artist, VFX, shaders, optimization | Senior | LATAM + strong TA niche |
| Omri Ovadia | Israel | Unity Technical Artist at Beach Bum | Unknown | Game studio TA |
| Scarlet Fairweather | UK | Unity Technical Artist at Scopely | Unknown | Studio TA benchmark |
| Daniel Peri | Israel | Unity TA with VR optimization | Unknown | TA + VR optimization |
| Aakash Upadhyay | India | 3D Generalist & Unity Technical Artist | Unknown | Hybrid 3D + TA |
| Wiktoria Fruba | Poland | Unity Technical Artist at ASTEK Polska | Unknown | EU TA role |
| J Tuason | USA | Senior Technical Artist | Senior | Aspirational only |
| Aela W. | Unknown | Unity Technical Artist, non-traditional background | Unknown | Non-traditional path signal |

### Takeaways for Alexander

Copy:

- Unity + technical art combination;
- optimization vocabulary;
- shader/visual mode vocabulary if defensible;
- pipeline vocabulary;
- runtime + art bridge.

Do not copy:

- seniority if not defensible;
- heavy VFX/shader specialization unless portfolio supports it;
- AAA framing without shipped game experience;
- pure game art emphasis.

### Recommended stance

Alexander can target Unity Technical Artist roles, but should qualify the specialization as:

```text
runtime systems · technical visualization · optimization · technical UI · CAD-to-realtime
```

not:

```text
senior shader specialist · AAA game TA · VFX specialist
```

---

## Real-Time 3D / Interactive 3D Developer

### Observed patterns

Profiles in this cluster often combine:

- Unity;
- Unreal;
- optimization;
- VR/mobile/web;
- interactive systems;
- simulation;
- full-stack or application design.

### Relevant examples

| Name | Region | Title / Signal | Seniority | Relevance |

- lack of technical ownership;
- generic marketing language.

---

## 6.3 WebGL / browser-based case demos

| Case | Platform | Core value | Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Work Spatial | WebGL | browser-based XR onboarding | High |
| NBK Virtugate | WebGL + VR | browser onboarding + optional VR | High |
| WebXR Product Configurator | WebGL / WebAR | product inspection/configuration | Very high |

### Notes

Browser-based demos are the closest reference for TwinSight because they prove:

- no-install access;
- interactive 3D in browser;
- real-time interaction;
- fast comprehension;
- user-facing workflows.

### Application to TwinSight

The video should explicitly show:

```text
Runs in browser
Interactive component selection
Real-time camera movement
Technical UI
No-install viewer
```

---

## 6.4 Digital twin / simulation case demos

| Case | Domain | Core feature | Relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Digital Twin of Production Facility | industrial operations | live IoT + 3D facility | High |
| BIM Site Overlay Visualization | construction | BIM + overlay | Medium-high |
| Construction Confined Space Simulation | safety training | guided procedural training | Medium |

### Notes

These cases are valuable for:

- explaining spatial context;
- showing how 3D replaces fragmented documentation;
- presenting workflows;
- connecting interaction to user decisions;
- using results/metrics.

### Application to TwinSight

TwinSight should use similar language:

```text
spatial context
guided inspection
component-level understanding
interactive technical support
reduced cognitive load
```

But avoid claiming:

```text
live IoT
predictive maintenance
production digital twin
VR training certification
```

---

# 7. Video pattern extraction

## 7.1 Ideal duration

| Video type | Common duration | Recommended for TwinSight |
|---|---:|---:|
| Personal technical reel | 60–120 s | 90 s |
| Project demo | 90–180 s | 90–120 s |
| Deep breakdown | 3–8 min | separate video |
| Social teaser | 15–30 s | optional |
| Recruiter clip | 45–75 s | optional |

## Recommendation

Create three video assets:

| Asset | Duration | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Main demo | 90–120 s | portfolio, LinkedIn Featured |
| Short teaser | 30–45 s | LinkedIn posts |
| Technical breakdown | 4–7 min | interviews, GitHub README |

---

## 7.2 Opening structure

Weak opening:

```text
Logo fade-in → slow orbit → title after 20 seconds
```

Strong opening:

```text
0–3 s: final polished viewer shot
3–6 s: value proposition
6–10 s: problem contrast
```

Recommended opening caption:

```text
TwinSight X500
Unity WebGL technical visualization for drone assembly inspection
```

Second caption:

```text
From static 2D documentation to interactive spatial understanding
```

---

|---|---:|
| Hero reveal | 3–5 s |
| UI interaction | 4–6 s |
| Exploded view | 5–7 s |
| Clipping plane | 5–7 s |
| Visual modes grid | 5–8 s |
| CAD optimization comparison | 5–7 s |
| Metrics card | 4–6 s |
| End card | 3–5 s |

Avoid shots longer than 8 seconds unless the narration requires it.

# 10. Caption system

## 10.1 Caption style

Use short captions, not paragraphs.

Bad:

```text
This system allows the user to select different drone components and view the associated information while navigating the interface.
```

## 10.2 Caption bank

```text
Browser-based drone assembly inspection
Component-level selection
Technical part information

Multiple visual modes
CAD-to-realtime optimization
```

Use “viewer vs 2D support” only if the methodology supports that comparison.

---

# 11. Voiceover recommendation

## Main recommendation

Use **captions + music only** for the public reel.

Add voiceover only for the long technical breakdown.

## Reason

Recruiters often skim videos silently. Captions are safer.

## If using voiceover

Keep it technical and restrained.

Example:

```text
TwinSight X500 is a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for drone assembly inspection. It converts CAD-derived assets into an optimized browser-based viewer with component selection, exploded view, cross-section tools, technical panels, and validation through SUS and NASA-TLX.
```

# 12. Technical breakdown video

Create a separate video, not the main reel.

## Structure

- shader graph, briefly;
- profiler if available;
- before/after asset counts;
- GitHub README;
- final browser build.

# 13. Editing rules

## 13.1 Must do

- show final output in first 5 seconds;
- use captions on every feature;
- keep shots short;
- show interaction, not just orbit shots;
- include metrics;
- include stack;
- include one clear end card;
- export cleanly at 1080p minimum;
- use consistent typography;
- avoid excessive transitions.

## 13.2 Must avoid

- long intro logos;
- slow cinematic-only orbit;
- unclear UI text;
- music louder than explanation;
- too many effects;
- pretending it is a shipped commercial product;
- hiding that it is an academic/portfolio prototype;
- overusing “AI” in the main reel;
- adding unimplemented XR/IoT/WebAR features.

# 19. What this changes in the roadmap


## Add

```text

```

## Priority

The video is not optional. It is one of the highest-leverage artifacts because:

- recruiters skim;
- technical managers need proof fast;
- Unity/WebGL projects are hard to understand from text only;
- the candidate lacks formal industry experience;
- the video can compensate by showing proof.

Before applications, produce at least:

```text

what problem it solves,
what the user can do,
why it is technically relevant.
```
