# 29C_artstation_breakdown_benchmark

## 0. Module status

```text
Module: 29C_artstation_breakdown_benchmark.md
Input task: F3_artstation_breakdown_benchmark
Date generated: 2026-06-11
Status: Complete v1
Source type: public portfolio-pattern benchmark + accessible snippet-derived examples
Primary use: ArtStation / portfolio breakdown structure for TwinSight X500 and Blender portrait
```

## 1. Completion audit

The previous F3 output was **not complete enough** as a final `29C` module.

It had useful general guidance, but it lacked:

- a clear module structure;
- source-quality classification;
- separate treatment of TwinSight and the Blender portrait;
- breakdown taxonomy;
- ArtStation post architecture;
- image requirements;
- technical captions;
- publication checklist;
- mistakes to avoid;
- direct update instructions for portfolio, GitHub and LinkedIn;
- a retry prompt for future deeper ArtStation collection.

This version completes the module as an actionable benchmark and production guide.

## 2. Scope

This module defines how Alexander should present technical-art and real-time 3D breakdowns on:

- ArtStation;
- personal portfolio;
- GitHub README;
- LinkedIn Featured;
- interview follow-up materials.

It focuses on two assets:

1. **TwinSight X500**  
   Unity WebGL technical visualization for drone assembly inspection.

2. **Blender hyperrealistic portrait**  
   Supporting 3D art / character-art signal, useful only if presented with technical breakdown depth.

## 3. Source limitations

ArtStation often blocks automated access through security checks. Several pages and snippets were visible through search, but full profile/project inspection was not reliably available.

Therefore, this module should be treated as:

```text
Portfolio breakdown structure benchmark v1
```

not as a complete database of verified ArtStation examples.

## 4. Source quality table

| Source type | Reliability | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Fully accessible portfolio page | High | direct structure extraction |
| Search snippet from ArtStation | Medium | title/tag signal only |
| YouTube/Vimeo reel page | Medium | video structure |
| Studio case study | High | project narrative |
| General industry pattern | Medium | layout and content planning |
| Unopened ArtStation page | Low | do not cite as factual detail |

## 5. Accessible benchmark signals

## 5.1 Search-snippet signals from ArtStation-like pages

| Signal | What it indicates | Use for Alexander |
|---|---|---|
| Technical Artist Demo Reel 2025 | reels are common for TA profiles | publish TwinSight video |
| Made with Unity | engine tag matters | tag Unity clearly |
| Unity foliage shader | shader breakdowns are portfolio assets | visual modes deserve breakdown |
| Unity URP water shader | URP is valid TA signal | state URP usage |
| Unity procedural fur shader | procedural/shader studies are valued | avoid claiming shader depth without proof |
| 3D Rigger / Technical Artist Demo Reel | hybrid roles use reels | video must show systems |
| topology breakdown | expected for character/asset work | include wireframes |
| material breakdown | expected for realistic work | include texture/material maps |
| shader breakdown | expected for TA | include Shader Graph/code if present |
| game-ready breakdown | expected for real-time assets | include optimization metrics |

## 5.2 Studio/case-study signals already collected

| Source | Relevant signal |
|---|---|
| HapzXR WebXR Product Configurator | browser-based 3D + product interaction |
| HapzXR Digital Twin Facility | spatial context + operational visualization |
| HapzXR BIM Overlay | model comparison + overlay logic |
| Virtual Verse Work Spatial | concise project page structure |
| Virtual Verse NBK Virtugate | WebGL + VR onboarding presentation |
| Industrial3D reels | industrial technical animation language |
| Kinetic Vision reel | technical visualization as product/process/system communication |

## 6. Breakdown taxonomy

## 6.1 Technical art breakdown types

| Type | Typical content | Fit for TwinSight |
|---|---|---:|
| Shader breakdown | graphs, nodes, render modes | High |
| Optimization breakdown | before/after geometry, texture budgets | Very high |
| Pipeline breakdown | CAD → Blender → Unity → WebGL | Very high |
| Tool breakdown | custom editor/runtime systems | High |
| Interaction breakdown | selection, UI, camera, states | Very high |
| Visual-mode breakdown | X-ray, ghosted, blueprint, thermal | Very high |
| Profiling breakdown | FPS, memory, load, draw calls | High |
| UX evaluation breakdown | SUS, NASA-TLX, Think-Aloud | Very high |
| Character art breakdown | topology, UVs, textures, grooming | Medium |
| Environment breakdown | scene assembly, lighting, props | Low-medium |

## 6.2 Character / portrait breakdown types

| Type | Typical content | Fit for Blender portrait |
|---|---|---:|
| Sculpt breakdown | blockout to final sculpt | High |
| Topology breakdown | face loops, eyelids, mouth, deformation | High |
| UV breakdown | UDIMs/UVs, texture density | High |
| Skin material breakdown | albedo, roughness, SSS, displacement | High |
| Groom breakdown | hair guides, eyebrows, beard | High |
| Lighting breakdown | HDRI, key/fill/rim, camera | Medium-high |
| Render breakdown | passes, compositing | Medium |
| Real-time conversion | optimization for Unity/Unreal | High if done |

## 7. ArtStation post architecture

## 7.1 Ideal structure for TwinSight ArtStation post

```text
01. Cover image
02. 30–60 second embedded video
03. One-sentence project summary
04. Role / contribution
05. Final screenshots
06. Feature breakdown
07. CAD-to-realtime pipeline
08. Optimization metrics
09. Visual modes breakdown
10. Unity interaction systems
11. UI / technical panels
12. Evaluation results
13. Tools used
14. Limitations
15. Links
```

## 7.2 Ideal structure for Blender portrait ArtStation post

```text
01. Cover render
02. Turntable video
03. Short project summary
04. Reference board
05. Sculpt stages
06. Topology
07. UVs
08. Texture maps
09. Skin shader / material setup
10. Grooming
11. Lighting
12. Final renders
13. Real-time/game-ready note if applicable
14. Tools used
15. Lessons learned
```

## 8. TwinSight breakdown specification

## 8.1 Cover

The cover should not be a generic drone render.

Use one of:

| Cover option | Strength |
|---|---|
| Full drone with technical UI visible | best overall |
| Exploded view with labels | strongest assembly signal |
| Cross-section with UI panel | strongest inspection signal |
| Grid of visual modes | strongest technical-art signal |

Recommended cover title:

```text
TwinSight X500
Unity WebGL Technical Visualization
```

Recommended subtitle:

```text
Drone assembly inspection · CAD-to-realtime · interactive 3D
```

## 8.2 Opening copy

Use short copy:

```text
TwinSight X500 is a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone. It converts CAD-derived assets into an optimized browser-based 3D viewer with component selection, exploded view, clipping tools, visual modes and usability/workload evaluation.
```

Do not open with:

```text
This was my thesis project about Design Science Research...
```

Academic methodology should appear later.

## 8.3 Role statement

Use:

```text
Role:
Real-time 3D development, Unity WebGL integration, C# runtime systems, technical UI, visual modes, Blender optimization workflow, evaluation design and documentation.
```

If AI assistance is mentioned:

```text
AI assistance was used for implementation support and iteration. Architecture, debugging, integration, validation, final decisions and project ownership remained my responsibility.
```

## 8.4 Key feature cards

Use concise cards:

| Feature | Caption |
|---|---|
| Component selection | Inspect individual drone parts and relationships |
| Exploded view | Reveal assembly hierarchy and spatial placement |
| Cross-section | Cut through structures to expose hidden geometry |
| Visual modes | Switch between realistic, X-ray, ghosted, blueprint and wireframe views |
| Technical UI | Display part information while inspecting the model |
| WebGL deployment | Run the viewer directly in a browser |
| Evaluation | Measure usability and workload using SUS and NASA-TLX |

## 8.5 CAD-to-realtime section

Recommended structure:

```text
CAD source
↓
conversion / tessellation
↓
Blender cleanup
↓
low-poly optimization
↓
UV / bake / material preparation
↓
Unity import
↓
WebGL deployment
```

Include:

- before/after triangle counts;
- wireframe comparison;
- modular fastener system;
- texture/material strategy;
- constraints for mobile/web;
- limitations.

## 8.6 Optimization metrics section

Use a metrics card layout.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Optimized geometry | 95,617 triangles |
| Source CAD routes | 6.5M+ triangles |
| Participants | 12 |
| SUS average | 91.88 |
| NASA-TLX Raw, 3D viewer | 8.69 |
| NASA-TLX Raw, 2D support | 19.89 |
| Task-condition records | 96 |

Add context:

```text
Evaluation was formative and academic, not a production deployment benchmark.
```

## 8.7 Visual modes breakdown

Create a grid:

| Mode | What to show |
|---|---|
| Realistic | final material view |
| X-ray | internal structure readability |
| Ghosted | partial transparency |
| Blueprint | technical drawing aesthetic |
| Wireframe | topology / engineering signal |
| Solid | neutral inspection view |
| Thermal-style | qualitative visual analysis, not real FEA |

Important wording:

```text
Thermal-style is a qualitative visual mode, not a physical thermal simulation.
```

## 8.8 Unity systems breakdown

Include one compact section:

```text
Runtime systems:
- selection/highlighting
- camera control
- exploded-view state
- clipping plane control
- visual mode switching
- bottom-sheet UI
- part metadata panel
```

Optional screenshot types:

- Unity hierarchy;
- script inspector;
- UI Toolkit panel;
- Shader Graph;
- C# snippet;
- profiler screenshot.

Do not include too much code on ArtStation. Put code detail in GitHub.

## 9. Blender portrait breakdown specification

## 9.1 Purpose

The Blender portrait should not be positioned as the main employability proof for technical visualization roles.

It should function as:

```text
supporting evidence of high-end 3D fundamentals, anatomy, material work, grooming and visual discipline.
```

## 9.2 Required sections

| Section | Required content |
|---|---|
| Final render | 2–4 strongest images |
| Reference | board or brief reference explanation |
| Sculpt | blockout / mid / final |
| Topology | face loops and clean deformation |
| UVs | layout and density |
| Skin material | texture maps and shader setup |
| Eyes | iris/cornea material |
| Hair/groom | eyebrows, beard, eyelashes, hair guides |
| Lighting | setup diagram |
| Render | camera, focal length, compositing |
| Real-time adaptation | optional but valuable |

## 9.3 What makes it relevant to technical art

Add a section:

```text
Technical focus:
- topology decisions
- material layering
- groom setup
- render optimization
- texture organization
- possible real-time conversion path
```

## 9.4 What to avoid

Do not frame it as:

```text
main portfolio proof for Unity WebGL roles.
```

Do frame it as:

```text
supporting 3D craft and technical presentation.
```

## 10. Image requirements

## 10.1 TwinSight images


# 3. Detailed case-study notes

## 3.1 WebXR Product Configurator — HapzXR

**Source:** [https://hapzxr.com/case-studies/webxr-product-configurator/](https://hapzxr.com/case-studies/webxr-product-configurator/)

### Confirmed facts

| Field | Data |
|---|---|
| Source type | Company case study |
| Company | HapzXR |
| Region | India / enterprise XR services |
| Industry | Industrial equipment |
| Technology | WebGL, Three.js, WebAR |
| Project type | Browser-based 3D product configurator |
| Access model | Browser + WebAR |
| Metrics | 3× engagement; 45% more qualified leads; 2-week shorter pre-order cycle |
| Confidence | High |

### Case structure

```text
Headline
Short value proposition
Challenge
Solution
Results
Project overview
Snapshot
Delivery flow
Related work
Call to action
```

### Problem pattern

The buyer could not evaluate industrial equipment physically. Static catalogs and 2D renderings failed to communicate scale, detail, and configuration.

### Solution pattern

A browser-based 3D configurator allowed users to:

- rotate;
- zoom;
- customize finishes;
- inspect internal components;
- use WebAR placement;
- send configuration data to CRM.

### Direct relevance to TwinSight

This is the closest collected analogue to TwinSight’s **browser-based inspection and technical product understanding**. It shows how a 3D viewer becomes stronger when framed as a decision-support or sales-support tool, not just a model viewer.

### What Alexander can adapt

- Frame TwinSight as an **interactive technical understanding tool**.
- Use “2D support was insufficient” as the problem.
- Emphasize browser access.
- Show interaction modes clearly.
- Include measurable outcomes if defensible.
- Present features as user-facing workflows, not just implementation details.

### What not to copy

- Do not claim CRM integration.
- Do not claim WebAR unless implemented.
- Do not claim business conversion metrics.
- Do not overstate industrial client impact.

Monitoring systems lacked spatial context. Operators could see alerts but not easily understand where those alerts belonged in the facility.

TwinSight is not a live digital twin, but it is **digital-twin-adjacent** because it maps a real physical product into an interactive 3D structure for understanding spatial relationships.

### What Alexander can adapt

- Use the term **digital-twin-adjacent technical visualization** carefully.
- Show how each component maps to real-world parts.
- Add a “future extension” section for sensor data, maintenance status, or assembly state.
- Emphasize spatial context as the core value.
- Structure the case study around “2D documentation lacks spatial context.”

### What not to copy

- Do not claim live IoT.
- Do not claim predictive maintenance.
- Do not claim production facility scale.
- Do not call TwinSight a full digital twin unless live state/data integration is added.

# 8. Recommended TwinSight case-study copy skeleton

## Title

```text
TwinSight X500 — Unity WebGL Technical Visualization for Drone Assembly Inspection
```

## Subtitle

```text
An interactive browser-based 3D viewer that helps users understand the spatial relationships between drone components through selection, exploded view, clipping, visual modes, and technical part panels.
```

## Problem

```text
Traditional 2D assembly documentation forces users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between parts. For complex drone assemblies, this increases cognitive effort and makes hidden structures, orientation, and component hierarchy harder to understand.
```

## Solution

```text
TwinSight X500 transforms CAD-derived drone geometry into an optimized Unity WebGL experience. Users can inspect components, isolate assemblies, activate exploded views, cut through structures, switch visual modes, and access technical information directly in the browser.
```

## Key features

```text
- Component selection and highlighting
- Exploded assembly view
- Cross-section / clipping inspection
- Technical part information panels

- Mobile-first WebGL interaction design
- Usability and workload evaluation
```

```text
- Reduced CAD-derived geometry from routes exceeding 6.5M triangles to 95,617 optimized triangles
- Evaluated with 12 participants
- SUS average: 91.88
- NASA-TLX Raw: 8.69 for 3D viewer vs 19.89 for 2D support
- 96 task-condition records
```

## Role

```text
I developed the Unity WebGL integration, runtime interaction systems, technical UI, visualization modes, asset optimization workflow, Blender-based preparation, documentation, and evaluation pipeline, using AI assistance as an implementation support tool while retaining responsibility for architecture, debugging, integration, validation, and final technical decisions.
```

# 9. TwinSight case-study section order

## Recommended final order

```text
01. Hero
02. One-line value proposition
03. Problem
04. Solution
05. Demo video
06. Key features
07. Technical pipeline
08. CAD-to-realtime optimization
09. Interaction systems

```

## Why this order

The benchmark case studies show that readers need value first, then details.

Do not start with academic methodology.

Start with:

```text
What problem did this solve?
What can the user do?
What technical proof exists?
What evidence validates it?
```

Then include academic details deeper.

# 31_application_targeting_matrix_and_search_protocol

## 0. Module status

---

# 1. Purpose

This module translates the live-job snapshot into a practical protocol for deciding:

```text
what roles to search,
what roles to apply to,
what roles to reject,
which CV/portfolio variant to use,
which gaps to close before applying,
and how to score opportunities consistently.
```

The goal is to prevent random applications and keep Alexander’s search aligned with the strongest market-positioning evidence:

```text
Unity WebGL / Real-Time 3D / Technical Visualization / Technical Art / XR-adjacent
```

---

# 2. Market evidence summary from module 30

The live-job snapshot found:

| Signal | Value |
|---|---:|
| Verified / captured postings | 9 |
| Snippet-only market signals | 6 |
| LATAM-specific roles | 3 |
| Contractor / freelance signals | 3 |
| Digital twin / simulation signals | 1 |

## Key interpretation

The sample supports a narrow but viable route.

The strongest path is not:

```text
generic Unity Developer
```

The stronger path is:

```text
Unity WebGL / Real-Time 3D Developer
Technical Visualization + Technical Art
XR / Simulation-adjacent portfolio
C# + shaders + optimization + 3D pipeline
```

## Market constraints

| Constraint | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Many postings are senior | seniority pressure is high |
| Portfolio proof matters | Creamos and Mudtek explicitly signal portfolio/reel relevance |
| Technical art is relevant | Flat2VR, FLEXUS, Mudtek |
| XR/VR is relevant | HyperVR, Insight Global |
| LATAM remote exists | Azumo, Insight Global, Creamos |
| WebGL is niche but useful | Creamos/web platform, TwinSight differentiation |
| Digital twin is very relevant but undercaptured | B2 only partial |

---

# 3. Targeting principle

Alexander should not compete primarily as:

```text
Junior Unity Gameplay Programmer
```

He should compete as:

```text
Unity WebGL / Real-Time 3D Developer with technical visualization, technical art and CAD-to-realtime proof.
```

This means the search strategy should prioritize roles where TwinSight is not just “a project,” but direct evidence.

---

# 4. Role priority matrix

## 4.1 Tier A — apply first

| Role family | Why Tier A | Required proof |
|---|---|---|
| Unity Technical Artist | strong technical art/rendering signal | visual modes, optimization, shaders, demo reel |
| Unity WebGL Developer | direct TwinSight evidence | WebGL build, browser demo, README |
| Real-Time 3D Developer | broad fit for interactive systems | demo video, runtime interaction, C# |
| Technical Visualization Developer | strongest thesis-domain fit | case study, CAD pipeline, metrics |
| Interactive 3D Developer | broad non-game framing | browser demo, UI, interaction |

## 4.2 Tier B — apply selectively

| Role family | Why selective | Required proof |
|---|---|---|
| XR Unity Developer | adjacent, but needs XR proof | frame as XR-adjacent unless VR exists |
| Simulation Developer | domain-relevant, but may require physics/engineering depth | clarify visualization vs simulation |
| Unity Developer | viable if not purely gameplay/mobile | use Unity WebGL/technical visualization variant |
| Tools / Pipeline Developer | relevant but needs tooling proof | ARA + Unity pipeline documentation |
| Shader / Render Technical Artist | attractive but risky | only if visual modes and shader proof are strong |

## 4.3 Tier C — fallback only

| Role family | Reason |
|---|---|
| Full-stack Developer | dilutes positioning unless role is 3D/web-adjacent |
| Python Automation Developer | secondary via ARA, not main route |
| LLM Application Developer | secondary unless applying to tools/automation |
| 3D Artist / Blender Generalist | weak compensation and weaker fit |
| Gameplay-only Unity Developer | high competition; TwinSight less relevant |
| Mobile game Unity Developer | apply only if WebGL/3D/optimization valued |

## 4.4 Reject / avoid

| Role type | Reject reason |
|---|---|
| Senior AAA Technical Artist | overclaim / shipped-title gap |
| Senior Shader Engineer | insufficient specialized shader proof |
| Production Digital Twin Engineer | may require IoT/cloud/industrial deployment |
| Robotics Simulation Engineer | may require ROS/physics/control systems |
| Pure VFX Artist | TwinSight not enough; style mismatch |
| Pure 3D Character Artist | secondary portfolio only |
| Full-stack SaaS Developer | unrelated proof |
| Mobile casual gameplay roles | weak alignment unless Unity/C# and remote LATAM are strong |

---

# 5. Recommended public role titles

Use these titles in searches and materials.

## 5.1 Primary title

```text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
```

## 5.2 Application-specific variants

| Target role | Use this title |
|---|---|
| Unity WebGL | Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer |
| Technical visualization | Technical Visualization Developer |
| Technical art | Unity Technical Artist |
| Real-time systems | Real-Time 3D Developer |
| XR | Unity XR / Real-Time 3D Developer |
| LATAM nearshore | Unity Developer — WebGL / Technical Visualization |
| Freelance | Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Developer |

## 5.3 Titles to avoid for now

```text
Senior Unity Developer
Senior Technical Artist
Digital Twin Engineer
XR Specialist
Shader Engineer
Full-Stack Developer
AI Engineer
3D Generalist
```

Unless the role context specifically requires a simplified label.

---

# 6. Search term protocol

## 6.1 Primary search terms

Use these daily or 2–3 times per week.

| Technical Visualization Unity remote | thesis-domain fit |
| Unity C# contractor LATAM | nearshore contractor |

| Unity Shader Graph remote | technical art route |
| Unity XR Developer remote | XR-adjacent route |
| Digital Twin Unity freelance | simulation/digital twin route |

# 7. Source protocol

## 7.1 Best sources by purpose

| Source type | Use |

# 8. Remote eligibility protocol

Do not treat “remote” as enough.

Every posting must be labeled as one of:

```text
Worldwide
LATAM only
US only
Canada only
EU only
EU + NA
UK only
Hybrid
On-site
Unknown
```

## 8.1 Colombia suitability labels

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Colombia-eligible | explicitly LATAM/global/contractor |
| Likely eligible | no restriction visible, but remote/global wording |
| Unclear | remote but region not defined |
| Likely not eligible | EU/NA/US-only |
| Not eligible | work authorization excludes Colombia |

## 8.2 Immediate filter

Reject or postpone if:

```text
US work authorization required
EU work authorization required now
hybrid in city/country not accessible
security clearance required
onsite only
```

Exception:

```text
Save for future EU/Portugal/Germany path if strategically relevant.
```

---

# 9. Application scoring model

Score each opportunity from 1 to 5.

## 9.1 Fit score

| Score | Definition |
|---:|---|
| 5 | Direct TwinSight fit: Unity/WebGL/technical visualization/CAD/interactive 3D |
| 4 | Strong Unity/technical art/XR fit with one gap |
| 3 | General Unity role with partial overlap |
| 2 | Weak role with mostly unrelated requirements |
| 1 | Distraction |

## 9.2 Probability score

| Score | Definition |
|---:|---|
| 5 | remote LATAM/contractor + portfolio-based + not senior-heavy |
| 4 | plausible with strong project proof |
| 3 | competitive but possible |
| 2 | mostly senior/shipped-title/local-only |
| 1 | unrealistic now |

## 9.3 Compensation score

| Score | Definition |
|---:|---|
| 5 | likely USD 6k+/month path |
| 4 | likely USD 3k–6k/month |
| 3 | likely USD 1.5k–3k/month |
| 2 | low/unclear |
| 1 | below target or unpaid |

## 9.4 Portfolio-fit score

| Score | Definition |
|---:|---|
| 5 | TwinSight directly answers role requirements |
| 4 | TwinSight + ARA/portrait answer most requirements |
| 3 | needs portfolio adaptation |
| 2 | current proof weak |
| 1 | unrelated portfolio |

## 9.5 Region score

| Score | Definition |
|---:|---|
| 5 | LATAM remote / Colombia eligible |
| 4 | global remote |
| 3 | unclear but possible |
| 2 | EU/NA-only but maybe future |
| 1 | not eligible |

## 9.6 Total score

```text
Total = Fit + Probability + Compensation + Portfolio-fit + Region
Max = 25
```

## 9.7 Action threshold

| Total | Action |
|---:|---|
| 21–25 | Apply now with tailored materials |
| 17–20 | Apply if materials are close |
| 13–16 | Save / apply only if low effort |
| 9–12 | Watchlist |
| ≤8 | Reject |

---

# 10. Application priority matrix

## 10.1 Priority A

Apply within 24–48 hours.

Criteria:

```text
Fit ≥ 4
Probability ≥ 3
Portfolio-fit ≥ 4
Region ≥ 4
```

Typical roles:

```text

Unity Technical Artist
Technical Visualization Developer
Interactive 3D Developer

```

## 10.2 Priority B

```text
Probability ≥ 3
Portfolio-fit ≥ 3
Region ≥ 3
```

Typical roles:

```text

```

## 10.3 Priority C

Save but do not prioritize.

```text

```

Typical roles:

```text
mobile gameplay Unity
senior general Unity
broad game programmer

```

## 10.4 Reject

Reject if:

```text

Fit ≤ 2

requires shipped AAA titles

requires relocation now
requires clearance
requires advanced shader/math/GPU beyond current proof
```

# 11. Material variant selection

# 2. Interview positioning baseline

## 3.4 Technical Visualization version

The solution is a browser-based Unity viewer where users can inspect parts, reveal assembly structure and compare visual modes interactively.

# 4. 2-minute project explanation

Use this when asked:

```text
Tell me about your main project.
```

## Answer

```text
TwinSight X500 is a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone.

The problem was that static 2D assembly documentation forces users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between components, orientations and hidden structures. I wanted to test whether an interactive 3D viewer could support understanding more directly.

Technically, the project involved transforming CAD-derived drone geometry into an optimized real-time WebGL asset, organizing components for selection, implementing runtime interaction systems in Unity/C#, building technical UI panels with UI Toolkit, and adding features like exploded view, clipping/cross-section inspection and multiple visual modes.

The project was also evaluated as an academic prototype using SUS, NASA-TLX Raw and Think-Aloud methods. The formative results suggested high perceived usability and lower perceived workload for the 3D viewer condition compared with 2D support in the tested tasks.

For me, the value of the project is that it demonstrates the full pipeline: CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL, runtime interaction, technical UI, technical visualization and evaluation.
```

---

# 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions

## 5.1 What problem were you solving?

```text
The core problem was spatial understanding. Drone assembly documentation is often shown through 2D diagrams, part lists and written instructions. Users must mentally reconstruct how components relate in 3D space. TwinSight addresses that by turning the drone assembly into an interactive 3D viewer where users can select parts, see hierarchy through exploded view, cut through geometry and inspect technical information directly in context.
```

## 5.2 Why Unity WebGL?

```text
Unity gave me a mature real-time 3D environment for interaction systems, visual modes, UI and asset organization. WebGL was important because the prototype needed to run in the browser without requiring a local install. That made it more accessible for evaluation and more aligned with technical visualization tools that need to be shared easily.
```

## 5.3 Why not Three.js?

```text
Three.js would also be valid for browser-based 3D. I chose Unity WebGL because my project needed a real-time engine workflow with scene hierarchy, interaction systems, UI Toolkit, rendering modes and a pipeline closer to Unity technical-art and real-time visualization roles. For this portfolio direction, Unity was the stronger strategic fit.
```

## 5.4 Is it a digital twin?

```text
I would describe it as digital-twin-adjacent, not a full production digital twin. It represents a real physical drone assembly in interactive 3D, but it does not currently include live sensor data, operational state synchronization, predictive maintenance or real-time telemetry. The current scope is technical visualization and assembly inspection.
```

## 5.5 Is it a simulation?

```text
It is not a physics simulation. It is an interactive technical visualization prototype. It simulates inspection workflows visually, but it does not simulate drone physics, structural loads, heat transfer or flight behavior.
```

## 5.6 What was the hardest technical part?

```text
The hardest part was balancing technical readability with WebGL constraints. CAD-derived geometry can be too heavy for browser deployment, so the challenge was preserving enough visual detail for inspection while reducing geometry and organizing the model into selectable components. The second challenge was coordinating multiple runtime states: selection, exploded view, clipping, visual modes and UI panels.
```

## 5.7 What would you improve next?

```text
I would improve three areas. First, I would deepen the metadata system so each component has richer technical information. Second, I would add guided assembly steps and search/filter tools. Third, I would explore WebGPU, XR inspection or sensor-state integration as future extensions, while keeping the current version honest as a WebGL technical visualization prototype.
```

---

# 6. CAD-to-realtime optimization defense

## 6.1 Explain the CAD pipeline

```text
The project started from CAD-derived geometry that was not suitable for direct real-time use. I inspected different conversion/tessellation routes, cleaned and optimized the assets in Blender, organized the model into logical components and prepared the geometry for Unity WebGL. The goal was not to preserve every CAD detail, but to preserve the visual information needed for assembly inspection while making the model usable in a browser.
```

## 6.2 Explain the triangle reduction

```text
The source routes exceeded 6.5M triangles in some forms, while the optimized runtime model was reduced to 95,617 triangles. I treat that as a portfolio and academic-prototype optimization metric, not as a production benchmark. The main point is that I could transform heavy CAD-derived data into a WebGL-ready inspection model while preserving component readability.
```

## 6.3 What did you decide to keep or remove?

```text
I prioritized silhouette, component identity, assembly relationships and features needed for inspection. I removed or simplified geometry that did not contribute to understanding the assembly, especially excessive tessellation or internal details that would not be visible or useful in the final viewer.
```

## 6.4 How did you handle fasteners?

```text
Fasteners were treated as modular repeated elements where possible. The goal was to avoid treating every screw as a unique asset when repeated geometry could be handled more efficiently. For a future production version, I would further standardize fastener families, metadata and instancing.
```

## 6.5 What would you do differently in a production pipeline?

```text
In production I would formalize the optimization pipeline more strictly: asset naming rules, automated validation, LOD strategy, texture budgets, profiler targets, versioned exports, and clearer handoff between CAD, DCC tools and Unity. I would also define target device constraints earlier.
```

# 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense

## 7.1 Runtime systems to explain

Be ready to explain:

```text
selection system
highlighting
camera/navigation
exploded-view state
clipping controller
visual-mode manager
UI Toolkit panels
part metadata
WebGL build configuration
```

## 7.2 Explain selection system

```text
The selection system connects user input to selectable drone components. When a part is selected, the viewer updates highlighting and displays contextual technical information in the UI. The important design point is separating the selectable component identity from the visual feedback and metadata presentation.
```

## 7.3 Explain exploded view

```text
The exploded view is a state-based transformation of assembly components. Instead of random separation, each component or group needs a defined offset direction and target position so the assembly remains understandable. The value is preserving spatial logic while making component relationships visible.
```

## 7.4 Explain clipping

```text
The clipping tool allows the user to cut through the model visually to inspect hidden structures. In Unity this can be handled through shader/material logic or clipping plane approaches depending on the implementation. The goal is not destructive geometry editing, but runtime visual inspection.
```

## 7.5 Explain visual modes

```text
The visual modes are inspection states that change how the model is rendered or interpreted visually. Some modes support readability, like realistic and solid modes. Others expose structure, like X-ray, ghosted, blueprint or wireframe modes. The thermal-style mode is qualitative only; it is not a physical simulation.
```

## 7.6 Explain UI Toolkit usage

```text
UI Toolkit was used to structure technical panels and interaction controls in a way that could support a more app-like interface. The interface needed to display component data while keeping the 3D inspection workflow visible.
```

## 7.7 Possible technical questions

| Question | Answer direction |
|---|---|
| How do you avoid coupling UI and model logic? | separate component metadata, selection state and UI rendering |
| How do you optimize for WebGL? | geometry reduction, texture budget, draw calls, loading, UI simplicity |
| How do you manage visual modes? | central mode manager, materials/shaders/states |
| How do you debug WebGL builds? | browser console, Unity logs, simplified repro scenes |
| How do you handle large models? | split hierarchy, optimize mesh, instancing, LOD, compression |
| How do you scale to multiple products? | metadata schema, import pipeline, prefab conventions |

# 8. WebGL constraints defense

## 8.1 What are WebGL constraints?

```text
WebGL deployment imposes stricter constraints than desktop builds: memory, loading time, browser compatibility, build size, shader support, compression, UI readability and runtime performance. For technical visualization, the challenge is making the experience accessible without sacrificing the core inspection value.
```

## 8.2 How did you address WebGL constraints?

```text
I focused on geometry optimization, reducing unnecessary CAD detail, organizing the scene hierarchy, keeping the UI readable and designing the interaction around core inspection tasks rather than adding unnecessary features. The project is still a prototype, so further profiling and build optimization would be part of the next step.
```

## 8.3 If asked about FPS/performance

Use only measured values if available.

If not final:

```text
The project was optimized around browser feasibility and reduced geometry, but I would avoid claiming final production performance until I run a complete profiling pass across target devices and browsers.
```

## 8.4 If asked about mobile

```text
The UI logic was designed with mobile-first constraints in mind, especially through bottom-sheet interaction patterns. However, final mobile performance and usability would require dedicated device testing before claiming production readiness.
```

---

# 9. Technical art / shader defense

## 9.1 How strong is your shader experience?

```text
My current shader/technical-art proof is strongest in visual inspection modes and material/render-state logic inside TwinSight. I would not claim to be a senior shader engineer. My strength is applying rendering and visual-mode techniques to improve technical readability in real-time 3D.
```

## 9.2 Explain visual modes as technical art

```text
The visual modes are not just aesthetic. They support different inspection tasks. For example, ghosted or X-ray-like views help reveal internal relationships, wireframe helps communicate structure, and blueprint-style rendering supports a technical drawing aesthetic. The design goal is visual readability for technical understanding.
```

## 9.3 If asked about URP/HDRP

```text
TwinSight is aligned with URP/WebGL constraints rather than high-end HDRP rendering. For browser deployment, URP is a more practical fit because it supports lightweight rendering and broad platform compatibility.
```

## 9.4 If asked about Shader Graph

```text
Shader Graph is useful for building and iterating visual modes without writing every shader manually. For deeper production shader work, I would still need to validate performance, compatibility and fallback behavior, especially for WebGL.
```

# 10. Evaluation defense

## 10.1 Why SUS and NASA-TLX?

```text
SUS provided a standardized usability measure, while NASA-TLX Raw helped capture perceived workload. Since the project compares interactive 3D support with 2D support for assembly-understanding tasks, both usability and workload were relevant.
```

## 10.2 What were the results?

```text
The formative evaluation involved 12 participants and 96 task-condition records. The SUS average was 91.88. NASA-TLX Raw was 8.69 for the 3D viewer condition and 19.89 for the 2D support condition.
```

## 10.3 What can you claim from the evaluation?

```text
I can claim that, in the tested tasks and sample, the prototype showed high perceived usability and lower perceived workload for the 3D viewer condition compared with 2D support. I would not claim universal superiority of 3D documentation based on this sample.
```

## 10.4 What are the limitations?

```text
The sample size was limited and academic. The evaluation was formative, not a large-scale industrial validation. It supports the portfolio and thesis argument, but it should not be overgeneralized as proof of production impact.
```

# 11. AI-assisted workflow defense

## 11.1 Short answer

```text
I used AI assistance as an implementation and iteration support tool. Final architecture decisions, debugging, Unity integration, asset preparation, evaluation design, documentation and project ownership remained my responsibility.
```

## 11.2 More detailed answer

```text
AI helped me accelerate parts of implementation and problem-solving, especially when exploring code structure or debugging options. But I still had to decide the architecture, integrate the systems in Unity, test behavior, adapt code to the actual project, prepare assets, validate the build and document the work. I see AI as a productivity tool, not a replacement for technical ownership.
```

## 11.3 If challenged: can you work without AI?

```text
Yes. AI can accelerate iteration, but it does not remove the need to understand the system. In a production environment I would follow the team’s policy on AI usage. My priority would be maintainable code, clear documentation and reproducible decisions, whether AI is allowed or not.
```

## 11.4 If asked what AI generated

```text
I would separate it by category: code assistance, debugging suggestions, documentation support and planning. I would not describe AI as the author of the project. The integration, testing, adaptation and final decisions were mine.
```

## 11.5 Avoid

Do not say:

```text
AI did most of the code.
I just prompted.
I do not fully understand the code.
I can only work with ChatGPT.
```

# 17. Soft launch vs hard launch

## 17.1 Soft launch

Use if assets are good but not perfect.

```text
portfolio published
GitHub ready
LinkedIn Featured updated
no public announcement yet
apply selectively
```

## 17.2 Hard launch

Use when public post is ready.

```text
LinkedIn post
ArtStation post
demo video public
portfolio fully linked
```

## 17.3 Recommended path

```text
Soft launch first.
Hard launch after QA.
```

Reason:

This allows applications to begin without forcing a public announcement before QA is complete.

## 18.3 Use questions as feedback

If people ask:

```text
What is this?
```

Then the hero/thumbnail is unclear.

If they ask:

```text
Did you build this?
```

Then the role/contribution is unclear.

If they ask:

```text
Is it a real digital twin?
```

Then limitation wording must be more visible.

If they ask:

```text
Can I try it?
```

Then live demo link must be more prominent.

# 20. Launch failure modes

## 20.1 Failure mode: too academic

Symptom:

```text
people do not understand the value quickly
```

Fix:

```text
move thesis/methodology lower
lead with demo, problem, solution, features
```

## 20.2 Failure mode: too visual, not technical

Symptom:

```text
looks like a 3D render, not a developer/TA project
```

Fix:

```text
add pipeline, architecture, metrics, GitHub, runtime systems
```

## 20.3 Failure mode: overclaiming

Symptom:

```text
interviewers challenge digital twin/AI/thermal claims
```

Fix:

```text
tighten limitations and safe wording
```

## 20.4 Failure mode: broken proof loop

Symptom:

```text
viewer cannot move from LinkedIn to portfolio/GitHub/demo
```

Fix:

```text
cross-link all assets
```
